en: To be combined with the visit of the Palace.
Medieval frescoes of the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries on the hills of Majano.

First traces in the 10th century (the name Curcavagnus is attested in 1164), several times rebuilt; in 1667 the Marquis Flamino Giacinto Balbiano transformed it into a baroque brick villa. From 1902 to 2010 it was the retirement home of the nuns of the Cottolengo; from 2010 it is the seat of the Paolo Ferraris Foundation, a cultural center with exhibitions and events, with the Salone delle Feste and the museum project "The tools of memory" on the tools for the restoration of paper and parchment. In the hamlet there is also the Romanesque church of the Saints Vittore and Corona.
Ethnographic Museum of Mortigliengo with demonstration laboratories of traditional activities: production of walnut oil and apple vinegar, cultivation and drying of chestnuts, hemp processing.
Majolica dome and sacred art.
In Monte Martello, a sanctuary built in 1475 around an existing cell with fourteenth-century frescoes.
The historic town theatre, reported by Visit Tuscany.
The Romanesque on the Castagnola.
The history of Sicilian ceramics.
The life of the Baronies in a noble house.
The beech woods of Gargano behind the village.
Lighthouse built in 1932 in memory of the fallen of the First World War: from the top of its 32 meters dominates the Murge and the valley of Ofanto.
Green found in a former quarry.
On the trail of Ligabue.
Touch and find out.
The tanks under the village.

Fraction at about 1,565 m on the right side of the valley, in a panoramic position under a large rocky bastion, overlooking Pizzo Stella, Groppera, Emet and Suretta; it is known for its blue-violet peel potatoes. From Campodolcino you climb on almost all paved road and little traffic: 6.2 km and 485 m of difference in altitude, about 55 minutes by road bike.

Centre of Alta Irpinia at 870 meters, founded by the Longobards around the castle and bishop's seat since 1076, was one of the most affected by the earthquake of 23 November 1980; today we visit the Castle of the Imperial with its museums, the Cathedral of Sant'Antonino Martire and, in the district of San Guglielmo, the Abbey of the Goleto founded in 1133.
A War of 1642.
A panoramic summit accessible from the village.
Semicircular tower of the early sixteenth century, called Porta Rondella, which marks the southern entrance of the castle.
The natural history of Calabria in a mountain village.
The church under the castle.
closed until spring 2027 according to the site of the Park

On the north-western saddle of Mount Sant'Antonio, with ample view of the valleys, a complex linked to the cult of the waters with phases from the end of the Middle Bronze to the Iron Age: well temple with circular chamber of about 4.80 m in blocks of white tuff, paved square of about 15 x 13 m crossed by a canal in basalt, a round one with central fireplace, rectangular buildings with seat along the walls and a corridor towards a nuraghe of about 15 m of diameter in large basalt blocks. Digged in 1988-89 by Fulvia Lo Schiavo and Anna Sanna after severe vandalisms; near the medieval castle called Capula and the medieval village abandoned in the fifteenth century.
The church of Barberini, basilica since 1845.

Church on the highest point of Piazza, just over half a kilometer from the ancient village, built in 1472, 1474 or 1476 (the date is uncertain) and today national monument. It preserves fifteenth-century frescoes with stories of the life, marriage and death of Mary. Called Madonna di Lessano until 1660, she is patron saint of Pianezza (feast on 12 September) and is located on a branch of the Via Francigena. Opening on request at the cultural office (tel. 011 9670217).
The tradition of the potters of Montottone, with the possibility to try the lathe.
€10 whole; €7 from 18 to 25 years and students; free under 18

It exhibits five Roman wrecks found between 1958 and 1961 during the work of the airport, in the ancient harbour basin: three river vessels for the transport on the Tiber, a sea cargo ship and a fishing boat with central tub for the live catch. Reopened after a long restoration.

The most populous center of the municipality, on the SS64 Porrettana, at 492 meters: the church of the Saints Mary and Frediano of the second half of the eighteenth century, the Logge of the mid nineteenth century with frescoes of 1998 by Paolo Maiani, the dam on the Limentra (1923-1928) and, in the hamlet Valdibura, the Grand-ducal Customs of the mid nineteenth century on the border between the Grand Duchy of Tuscany and the Papal State.
A Roman bridge under the city.
A noble residence with a secret garden.

Begin in 1063 by Buscheto, masterpiece of the Romanesque Pisan with classical, Byzantine and Islamic influences: elliptical dome, white and black marbles, the pulpit of Giovanni Pisano and the apse mosaic with San Giovanni di Cimabue (1302).

Built in 107 A.D. in the Trajan age to bring water to the port of Centumcellae then under construction, it is located just outside the village surrounded by greenery; VisitLazio indicates it as the stage not to be missed.
MiC card indicates closed every day
The canal aperitif.
Pacher's masterpiece.

The ancient Nuceria Alfaterna, capital of the San Marzano tomato: the castle of the Park that hosted Dante and Boccaccio, the archaeological museum of the Agro Nocerino in the convent of Sant'Antonio, the district of the Vescovado and medieval convents.
Church and Cistercian monastery of 1260, with the Badia Grande of 1290 and the Gothic cloister; the nuns prepare almond and pistachio cakes.
Kayak on the river and birdwatching in the ponds.
The Walser house.

Rebuilt in 1517 after the fire of 1471, after the fire of Tullio Lombardo with the baroque bell tower of Filippo Juvarra of 1732 68 meters high and works by Cesare Vecellio, Schiavone, Jacopo Da Ponte and Andrea Brustolon.
Fresh water under the Limbara.

Villa of the 4th century A.D., probably Lucio Aradio Valerio Proculo, governor of Sicily: about 3,500 square meters of mosaics, including the Corridor of the Great Hunt with the capture of animals in Africa and the ten girls in bikini are engaged in sports exercises.
The Assumption of the Clarisse Monastery.
The millenarian parish where the stage of the Carolingia Street ends.

Inaugurated in 2004 together with the Archaeological Park, it exhibits the finds of the excavation campaigns at the foot of the Mitra Hill, the sacred area of the Italic temple of Hercules, the sanctuary of Jupiter and the sacellus of a female deity. According to the MiC card is open in July and August (9-13 and 16.30-19.30), in the rest of the year by reservation.
Romanesque church of the XII century with interior with three naves.
Sacred building of the historic centre of elegant architecture, with sacred art works and liturgical decorations inside; it has architectural barriers.

San Gervasio is the ancient castle of Valdera; the parish church was built in the 11th century near the walls of the castle and has been recently restored. The village is the stop of the network of paths of Palaia.
The panoramic walk over the Alps and the Monviso.
Summer 365 days a year.

Along Corso Reginna, the central street, the palace was the residence of the Marquis Mezzacapo and today houses the municipal library, the historical archive, a cultural workshop and offices of the municipality; the gardens, known for the scenic fountains, are home to shows and events.

Born from the ancient hermitage of Santa Maria Eremitana, passed to Carthusians, Benedictines, Cistercians and Basiliani and, after 1320, to the Franciscans as Santa Maria delle Grazie; on August 22, 1523 came from Paris the Sacred Spina, relic of the crown of Christ donated by Queen Giovanna of Valois to the confessor Dionisio Sacco, Franciscan of Policastro. 14th-century bell tower, church full of works of art, cloister, vegetable garden and wood; today it is inhabited by the Mariana Family            the five Stones, with guided tours.
Founded in 1077 and renovated in 1495 on a project by Bernardino De Lera, with neoclassical façade by Luigi Voghera, 12th century bell tower and the 13th century Sant'Agata Table.

In the former oratory of Santa Croce, on the square of Valloria, exhibits objects of peasant life, craftsman and maid recovered with the community: agricultural tools, tools and instruments built by Giacomo Pisani (1886-1959), including a "percussive" halfway between piano and organ, a violin and a self-scatting camera. The MiC card indicates opening every day 8-18 (updated to 2020); the Province says open on request. Tel. 0183 282396.

Cittadina della Piana with an 18th-century old town, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1783: the Mother Church with the marble altarpiece of the 16th century Deposition, the church of the SS. Trinity with the majolica dome, the nineteenth-century Rosary and the Civic Museum with eighteen works by the sculptor Francesco Jerace.
The caves that talk with the wind.
Ceramics and graphics of Cascella.
The heart of the village, next to the museum.

Inaugurated in 1998 and since 2006 housed in a renovated 18th century rural house, on two floors and six rooms, it has an archaeological section with finds from the Roman age at the beginning of the 19th century and one dedicated to the art medal of the twentieth century, with works by the Bujesian masters and engravers Pietro Giampaoli, Celestino and Vittorio Giampaoli, Guerrino Mattia Monassi, Piero Monassi, Pietro Galina and Enore Pezzetta. A room is dedicated to the earthquake of 1976 with over one hundred and twenty medals of fifty Italian artists; there is also a didactic itinerary on how a medal was born. Timetable to be requested from the Municipality (tel. 0432 960151).
A wood for the fallen.
The art of Valnerina.
The workshops of the past and a collection of insects out of scale.

Medieval village almost intact in the highest point on Trasimeno, founded according to tradition in 543 by the commander of the Ostrogoth Arrigo for the siege of Perugia, remembered in August by the Festa dei Barbari.
Defensive tower of 1564 against pirates, the only remaining of the original three.
The colored sails in the center of the village.
An East trip to Cagliari.
The little church of the legend of the miller and devil.

At the headquarters of Cambiano, where in 1982 the Pininfarina Research and Studies Centre was established, the company visit shows unique pieces, prototypes, standard cars, cabriolets and coupes documenting the company's contributions to aerodynamics, safety and aesthetics, as well as industrial design objects such as the Olympic torch of Turin 2006. Company visit, partially accessible.

At the foot of Mount Summano, Santorso preserves the neoclassical sanctuary of Sant'Orso designed by Ottone Calderari and the environments designed and inhabited by Alessandro Rossi: the nineteenth-century villa with the romantic garden and the model farm; in the center and on the slopes of the mountain, numerous fountains.
The sacred art of the island in one seat.

Built from 1292 to 1465 on top of a staircase, with unfinished façade and three carved portals, three aisles of equal height and thirteen chapels; in the crypt of 1596 Jacopone da Todi rests, inside the Madonna and Child of Masolino; the bell tower can be visited, with 360 degrees view.

A complex rich in woods and paths with the Tabcu Mannu and Mount Arbu; around the holm oak forests and vineyards of Crabiolu, Fustiragili and Bingioniga and, in the background, the limestone heels of Ogliastra. The river Quirra and its tributaries change color from blue to green.
The view over three valleys.
the MiC card is closed every day, the regional portal is available on request. 081 19936289, pa-fleg@cultura.gov.it)
The sunset on Vicenza.
The synagogue of the ancient ghetto, signalled by Terre di Siena among the monuments of the city.
The ancient Appian Gate, the largest of the walls gates, from which the Appian Way begins.

Church of the thirteenth century mentioned in the bull of Boniface VIII of 1302; it preserves the portal of the sixteenth century, some terracotta statues and a cross. On August 24th, the historical festival takes in procession ladies, knights and bishops in medieval dresses.
The most important collection of paintings of the Sienese school of the Three and fifteenth centuries: Duccio di Buoninsegna, Simone Martini, Pietro e Ambrogio Lorenzetti, Sassetta.
The pastures and trails on the plateau.

Itinerary of the Ticino Park of 7.62 km, accessible all year round in about 3 hours: it starts and arrives south of the Becca Bridge, between the riverbank and the Bronese State Road 617 and follows the banks of the Po and for a stretch the dirt road parallel to the state road, between agricultural landscapes and the center of Mezzanino, with views of the bridge at the confluence of the Ticino in the Po.
11th-century castle, residence of Countess Adelaide who married Oddone di Savoia; now home of the Civic Museum. In the area also Roman remains with a monumental entrance of the first century AD.

Centre of the Diano Valley inhabited by the Neolithic, where the Romans founded Consilium: the remains of the Norman Castle on the hill, the National Archaeological Museum with the accessories of the necropolis and, in the historic center, Baroque chapels such as St. Joseph and the Madonna del Monte.
The votive bow.
Near the cathedral, the ancient office of weights and sizes of the hole.
Where tradition places the martyrdom of Paul.

Memorial park inaugurated in October 1972, on about 16,000 square meters, with over 2,400 wrought iron stems dedicated to the fallen alpine of the province of Treviso and beyond; since September 1998 every evening it plays a bell in their memory.
The village on the gulf.
Ruins of a convent to discover walking around the lake.
A little baroque with the relics of the Magi.
The Italian art of the XX and XXI century in the ancient Hospital of Leopoldine, with exhibitions and temporary installations.
A green break between museums.

An ancient residence renovated several times, today of eighteenth-century appearance on a project by the architect of court Francesco Gallo, country house of the Benso di Cavour where the statesman was born, formed and worked. It is a museum house dedicated to Camillo Benso and the lifestyle of the Piedmontese ruling classes under the Savoy: the Memorial, reopened on March 17, 2021 after a long restoration, includes the tomb of Cavour in the crypt of the chapel, declared a national monument. Reservation required; free with Torino+Piemonte Card and for children under 6 years.
€4 full; €3 reduced; free up to 19 years and the first Sunday of the month; included in the single ticket of the Civic Museums
Nature in the city.
The Pavese Renaissance.
A road that passes through a mountain, unique in Italy.
The frescoes of the Corgna.

In the center of the village, the hill brings together three churches: St. Martin, from the twelfth century, the oldest monument of Scena, with two naves and on carolingia measures; the old parish church, rebuilt in Romanesque style between the twelfth and thirteenth centuries and redesigned in the sixteenth century; the new neo-Gothic parish church, built between 1914 and 1931 because the old one had become too small. In the center the large heart of flowers with views of the church is among the most photographed points of the village.
Rural civilization and archaeology of the valley.

Ring that starts from the parking lot of the Three Fountains Sante: beyond the faunistic fence, the path 9 climbs up into the woods along a canal, crosses a bridge over the glacial melting water and reaches three waterfalls fed by the glacier, then descends into the wood at the starting point.
The village dominated by the villa La Ferdinanda, among vineyards and olive groves.
It preserves the "Madonna del Rosario" attributed to Simone De Magistris.
The most important monument of the city according to the municipality.
A glazed terracotta in a mountain village.
In the confraternity of San Sebastiano, it tells the spirituality, history and society of the city.
A 6.5 km hike along the paths 141 and 141V (change in altitude 490 m, difficulty E), mostly along the Via dei Monti or

The village was born in the 11th century from the union of three fortified nuclei and preserves intact the medieval system; from the hill, at 463 meters, the view ranges from the Gran Sasso, Majella, the Vettore and Sibilla to the Adriatic.

Opened on 18 June 2016 in the former ALPI plant on the Minori port, it tells the tuna trap of the Saline, active until the seventies, Stintino and Asinara with videos narrated (subtitles in English), vintage images and testimonies. He exhibits tools, diaries, articles, the dresses of the mattanza, models of boats and trap and paintings of Sardinian artists such as Stanis Dessy and Ausonio Tanda. Admission for a fee.
The only museum in the world on the intelvese art of stucco and scagliola.
The journey of the Comedy in nine marbles through the streets of the village.
Since 2004 it has preserved the historical and documentary heritage of the Bagnone valley, telling the gender relations in the Lunigiana society with photos and testimonies.
The square is an outdoor museum.
Birdwatching on the coastal lake.
A nuragic village of a hundred huts.
The findings of the Roman city of Sassina, home of Plauto, including large funeral monuments.
The history of the city under the Duomo.
He keeps a fine painting by Andrea da Jesi.
The historic and colourful market on the edge of the Spanish Quarter, with fish stalls, mozzarella, fruit and craft shops.
Romanesque church with Gothic elements.
From Volta's electricity to the present day.
The artifacts of Tusculum.
The tower on the Langhe.
See the exhibits of the sanctuary before or after the visit to Mount Senes.
Source does not indicate exact address
The Dauni promontory above the bay.
An exhibition in the garden of the dukes.
Medieval alleys and carved trunks.
Inferno waterfall: path for experienced hikers (EE) and stretch of 4 km in 4x4 (Riserva Valli Cupe)
The trades of the Pistoia mountain.

It dominates the main square with a square mast of the twelfth century; in the seventeenth century Roberto Orsini and his son Mario, bishop of Tivoli, transformed the fortress into a noble residence, entrusting the decoration to the painter Sabino Vincenzo Manenti. In the main room the frescoes of the four elements, the four continents and the human temperaments, with the Rat of Europe in the center of the vault stucco. In 1632 part of the feud passed to the Borghese, who had it entirely in 1761.
The baronial palace dating back to the year 1000, in the heart of the village.
The cathedral above the excavations.
Typical products of the village are truffles, chestnuts, mushrooms and cheeses, celebrated by the Truffle Festival in July and that of the chestnut on the last Sunday of October.
The sulphurous waters of the Valenzan hill.

The original village on the edge of the hill, documented by the 11th century as Grocte or Grupte, is dominated by the remains of the fortress erected between the 9th and 10th centuries. From Piazzetta Peretti, near the Clock Tower, you can enjoy an exceptional view from the balcony porch of the building of the eighteenth-century Teatro dell'Arancio; from the Madonna park you can reach the ancient Incasato, with the portrait of the poet Mario Rivosecchi carved by Pericles Fazzini.
€6 (with guide), reduced €4; cumulative with the museum €10, reduced €7
The church of Piazza Navona with the concave façade of Borromini, rebuilt in the middle of the seventeenth century for Innocent X on the site of the martyrdom of Agnes.
19th-century palace dated 1847, work of Apulian workers, of public property, overlooking Piazza Trieste with a second access from Piazza Giovanni Paolo II. The main body is now used as a museum.
The symbol of the Friulian Dolomites.
The Austro-Hungarian cemetery in the pastures.
The paths of the park around the village.
A medieval crime sung by Dante.
16th century castle and finds of the ancient Makella.
15th century frescoes signed on the way to Compostela.
The origins of the village, one kilometer from the center.
The castle of the Roccabruna in the center of the village.
€8 whole; €4 reduced; family €20; cumulative 3 months with La Specola €24

Masterpiece of the Romanesque padan in three phases (XI-XIII century): the three-door façade with statues of Davide and Ezekiel is from the workshop of Benedetto Antelami, the bell tower of 1569; inside the Christ judge in the apse basin, the final judgment of the thirteenth century and works of Vincenzo Campi, Chiaveghino and Ferdinando Bibiena; in the crypt a Roman sarcophagus. Pilgrim's stop on the Via Francigena.

Under the church of the SS. Stimitate (titled in 1602) a path with two faces on the excavation shows the remains of a temple of the VII-VI century B.C. superimposed on those of a hut of the Iron Age, under a modern case; here were found the polychrome terracotta and the veliternal "tabula." Recovery completed in 2016.
The unique Madonna delle Grazie.
A 15th-century convent.
The Bassano in the cathedral of the walled city.

Church of the Carmelites rebuilt from 1727 and completed around 1758, with a major altar consecrated in 1759 and canvas by Pietro Cataldo Mauro (1760); it preserves the Madonna della Libera by Giovanni Stefano Caramia (1660), the wooden Crucifix by Giacomo Genovini (1630), the carved pulpit by Domenico Semeraro (1859) and the inlaid wardrobes of the sacristy. From the church you enter the cloister of the former convent. Open 7:30-12:30 and 16:30-20:30.

The "Sass Cavalasc" is a colossal erratic rock on the shore of the Verbano, in the territory of Ranco near the border with Ispra, which emerges from the water next to a beach. Like the other erratic boulders in the country, it was transported by glaciers that covered the entire Lake Maggiore during the glaciations.
The historic centre on an island of about 1 km2, joined to the mainland by two bridges and to walk, with Piazza Duomo, the market and the Temple of Apollo.
Roman arches along the river.
The small nucleus of 87 inhabitants gathered around the castle, on the first hills of the Tuscan-Emilian Apennines.
The sanctuary of Mithras in a cave.

Hill reached with an easy path, with frescoes of Byzantine style called "figureddi" depicting the four Evangelists, the Madonna and a saint, probably the work of Basilian monks between the fourth and the sixth centuries.
The Challant Castle.
Unspoilt alpine architecture and a view of the plain.

One of the most important valleys of the Massif del Grappa, deep and wild, suitable for trekking, mountain biking and hiking; it is very close to the take-off and landing areas of the free flight of Semonzo and Roman Ezzelino.
The square of Mario Botta in the heart of a village of Bassa.
The mud spa that made the resort famous.
One of the main parishes of the city and the minor basilica, at the centre of the city's religious life; it is the first stage of the municipal itinerary  "Devotion and sacred art."
Pisa from above without the Tower.

Consecrated in 1471 and reformed in neo-Gothic style between 1875 and 1880 by Angelo Cattò, in the square of the village. Behind the main altar is the polyptych of Cima da Conegliano (1489), nine compartments on two orders around a wooden statue of St. Bartholomew; it also houses a Venetian-Cretan icon of the sixteenth century and paintings by Vittoriano Urbini (1588) and Giuseppe Brina. Visitable during opening hours and during functions.

Palace probably built in the fifteenth century by the Lazzaroni family and then expanded, purchased in 1881 by the notary Giuseppe Lambertenghi; the family, who still lives there, shows rooms with rich furnishings, fixtures and art collections. According to the city guide it is open from 10 May to 10 October on Thursday, Friday and Saturday (10-12.30 and 14-16) and in the rest of the year on the first Monday of the month, with visits every 30 minutes.

Managed by the artist's family, he was born when his son Francesco, after the death of the sculptor in 1928, collected works and materials from the studies of Paris and Milan in Barzio and bought an ancient seventeenth-century church near the oratory (the oratory of St. John the Baptist), with the advice of Piero Portaluppi. It exhibits about 25 sculptures, including waxes and plasters such as "Man who reads" (1893), "Bookmaker" (1894), "Sick at the hospital" (1899), "Conversation in the garden" (1899) and "Ecce Puer" (1906), in addition to rotational drawings; the original set-up with stands and vintage windows is preserved.

Longobard Abbey founded in the VII century, preserves the original Romanesque plant with apse and facade; it is located along the Via Francigena, whose stage 26 arrives from Massa to Camaiore and the 27 continues to Lucca.
Founded in 1975 by the Association for the Conservation of Popular Traditions to preserve the theatre of the puppets; it bears the name of its founder, Doctor Antonio Pasqualino.
A little known and very suggestive site.
Two hundred years of tower clocks in the factory that builds them.
A great residence extended never ended.
16th century complex built on Roman foundations, overlooking the main square of the town.

The ancient Lilibeo, the city of wine and the landing of the Thousands: the Baroque center from Porta Nuova to the Duomo, the Baglio Anselmi museum, the historical cellars and the lagoon of the Stagnone with the salt pans and the Phoenician island of Mozia.

28-metre-high brick tower, the only surviving tower in the castle, with the Government Palace at the base; from an opening in the clock dial the prisoners were lowered into the cell below. It houses the Museum of Rural Civilization.

The river returned in 1983 a monoxyl pirogue about 6.5 meters long; from the banks you can see the Berici and Euganean Hills. The old nearby mill, today in the territory of Veggiano, dates back to the 11th century.

The parish, then dedicated to St. Sirus and belonging to the diocese of Brugnato, is already attested in 1143 and appears in the Eximum of the churches of the bishopric of Brugnato in 1452. Joined in San Pietro in Frascati in 1498, it passed to the diocese of Genoa in 1519 and was reconstituted parish in 1715 by Cardinal Lorenzo Fieschi; since 1892 it was of the diocese of Chiavari and since 1959 of Spezia. N. S. of the Belt on the second Sunday of July; festive Mass at 11.

Built at the end of the 11th century at the initiative of the judge of Torres Mariano I in the village of Salvennor, abandoned in the 18th century, passed around 1139 to the Vallombrosan monks. T-shaped plant with three apses, brick masonry of limestone and black volcanic stone and close relation with the nearby Saccargia; remains a stretch of the portico that joined it to the disappeared monastery. The area is now close to industrial plants.
The rosette and the painted nave.

Established in 1982 with the works donated by the artists of the annual exhibition "Ripearte" has over three hundred works, including Umberto Peschi, Giorgio Bompadre and Renato Barisani; with the route "Diffuse" small groups of works are exhibited in shops, restaurants and reception places.

The main street with medieval and Renaissance buildings, tower houses and terracotta loggias; the Marro House-fortress has a glazed walkway on the foundations of a Roman temple. In the small square of the Singer, he opened the first Ferrero pastry shop.
The great medieval Pisan painting.
The origins of Genoa.

The museum preserves the statues made during the editions of the Symposium of Wood and Granite between 1980 and 2000, when sculptors from all over the world carved granite and wood in the streets and squares of the village; other statues are exhibited throughout the town.

Municipality of the Alpago basin, dominated to the north by the chain that goes from Mount Teverone to the Horse; it houses the Museum of Natural History of the Alpago and is crossed by the Path of Sensitivity, footpath designed also for visually impaired people.

Ethnographic and archaeological museum founded in 1979 by Vittorio Polli. The oldest finds come from the collective burials of the Buca di Andrea, discovered in 1975 by Onorato Pesenti and dating from the middle of the III millennium to the XIX century BC; next to, work tools, household objects, furnishings and clothing tell life and traditions of the valley. Timetable indicated by the Municipality: Tuesday-Saturday 9-12 and 14-17, Sunday by reservation; guide on request 15 €.
The shrine dearest to the Teramans.
One of the oldest churches in the village.
The church that marks the birth of the eighteenth-century country, with stuccoes and vintage canvases.
One of the monumental entrances that testify to the Venetian domination; inside the museum dedicated to the walls.
Clear pools of water in the valley floor.

Gothic-Catalan parish built between 1585 and 1605 by the picapedres Gontinio Pinna and Miguel Baldabella; on the portal the coat of arms of the Carroz, lords of the Duchy. Inside the nave with juniper beams, five chapels per side and presbytery with starry vault; it houses a wooden group with Crucifix, Madonna and St. John, polychrome statues of the seventeenth century, wooden altars of the eighteenth century, tabernacle and baptismal font in eighteenth-century marble. At the exit there is sa perda de sa bregungia, ancient medieval gogna.
The most surprising monument of Modenese.
The 700 sq.m. painted ceiling and the angels of Sammartino.

Regional nature reserve, last coastal marsh of the area and stop for many migratory birds such as herons and marine acorns; it is equipped for birdwatching, with guided tours and workshops for children.
A church museum.
The former Baroque cathedral with the Caravaggio Tobiolo.
The Roman Novaria.

Natural area to be explored on foot, which takes its name from a tower once used to communicate with the mainland by smoke signals. From the beach of Torrefumo entered the village in 1814 the statue of the Assumption, welcomed by a great procession.
A Lombard church with crypt.
€4, reduced €2 (4-17 years and over 65), Sunday €2

In the area of Villa di Toppo Florio, about 2900 objects document the peasant viticulture from the nineteenth century to the mid-twentieth century: sections on viticulture and wine making, the workshop of the carpenter workshop rebuilt, trade and consumption of wine, a Friulian inn of the thirties and a documentary collection. Open only by reservation (tel. 0432 63611).
The fabric of shorts and chapels of a grey country.
A sanctuary of ancient and unusual popular devotions.

In 1029 there was already a church with a bell tower on an outlying rock, around which the Benedictine monks built the center of their curtis; about 250 years later the defenses were strengthened. The tower is visited with the guides of the FIE and some rooms of the shelter host exhibitions and events.
The story of an Alpine regiment through weapons, relics and documents.
Church of the historic center indicated by the Abruzzo Region among the places to visit.
La Roma industriale e street art.
The life of a manor house and the wine of Campidano.

Medieval village of narrow and steep alleys, with an ancient system of fortifications still well readable: the fifteenth-century Porta Antonietta and the Porta di Mezzo remain. Every 5 January, since 1951, the village hosts one of the oldest and most famous living nativity scenes in Italy, with shepherds, women in costume and Magi and the Child interpreted by the last born of the country.
A green oasis in the city.
Walk in the shade of the white firs of Alto Molise.
Excavations under Piazza Italia with the eleven layers of building of the city, a sequence ranging from the Greek to the modern age.
The highest concentration of farms in Puglia.

Where the Basilica of San Domenico was located, in which Stradivarius was buried in 1737: today we see the bronze copy of his tombstone; in front of the church the Beloved, Guarneri and Stradivarius had shop.

Photos, folk art, books and a collection of traditional children's games.

It is called "the two seas" and is a soft sandy tongue with pink reflections due to the granite fragments between the sea and the pond of Notteri, with low seabed and dunes of junipers and lentisks; on the southwestern promontory the Spanish tower of the seventeenth century, about 9 meters high, reachable on foot. Parish of Conturbia, consecrated between 1122 and 1151 by Bishop Litifredo: facade in hut, wall in serizzo blocks of the twelfth century, porch added in the seventeenth century. On the south side there is a frescoed bezel from the middle of the 12th century with St. Peter; inside there is a 15th-century Crucifixion, an 18th-century high altar and the Baroque wooden pulpit carved around 1701 by Antonio Francesco Viano da Oleggio.

The works for a foundry of cannons began in the late eighteenth century and were completed in 1841 under Ferdinand II of Bourbon; the complex, of about 15,000 square meters, was active until 1865 as a steel-armor plant. Church of the XIII-XIV century (of the XV according to the portal of the Borghi), rebuilt in the nineteenth century, next to Palazzo De Lieto; it is one of the most important churches of the city of the 44 churches.

Pavese village along the Po and the Via Francigena, dominated by the Castle Cusani Visconti Botta Adorno (Castello Procaccini), medieval fortress transformed in the eighteenth century into a villa of delight that houses the Museum of Lombardy Rural Civilization and the Museum of Lombard Wine; in the center a monumental cedar of Lebanon.

Valico about 2,057 m at the foot of the Marmolada, with a plateau of about 2.5 km; the lake is an artificial basin of the mid-Twentieth century that collects the ice-clad waters for hydropower (not bathing), and at the foot of the dam in the fifties arose a laboratory for the study of cosmic rays. Collection formed by Erio Tripodi in the eighties and set up in a steam train, a locomotive  "Cirilla" of 1910 with carriages "centoporte": rare systems of automatic reproduction of sound still working (musical boxes, organettes of Barberia, organnets of French tabarin of the eighteenth century, mechanical floors and piano), relics of the Italian song from street music to Neapolitan melody to light music, and a section on the Sanremo Festival with photos, autographs, records, posters and sketches of sets. On a second carriage a study center with library and record archive. Guided visits; tel. 0184 291000.

First Lombard museum dedicated to prison history, in the former life sentence: objects, instruments and weapons of the use of prisons between 1785 and 1954, with the graffiti of young prisoners still visible on the walls; it also tells the military prison of 1920-1945, with cells without services nor water and punishment cells.

In Bardino Vecchio along the road to the Colle del Melogno, it was born according to tradition from an apparition of 1722, when the Virgin appeared to a mute girl who regained the word. City overlooking the gulf between the Circeo and Gaeta, the Via Appia and the Via Francigena del Sud: high up the sanctuary of Monte Sant'Angelo with the so-called Temple of Jupiter Anxur, in the center the Forum Emiliano, the Roman Theatre reopened in 2023 and the Cathedral of San Cesareo.

Villa built by Scipione Avogadro at the end of the sixteenth century, renovated by Giovanni Battista Marchetti in 1731 and in the nineteenth century by Emilio Alemagna; purchased in 1947 by the Scalabrini Fathers, after the restoration completed in 2006 it became a hotel with conference center.

The bell tower dates back to 1794 and was built in the Baroque style between 1670 and 1680 after the 1662 earthquake. He kept eleven paintings by Mattia Preti, including the Miracle of St. Francis of Paola (1678), the Lightning Christ (1680) and the Martyrdom of St. Sebastian (1687), a Pietà by Giovan Battista Ortega (1603), a 17th century scagliola palace, an organ by Francesco Ferrazzano (1754) and a golden wooden pulpit. Protected since 1997, it is the third protected marine area of Italy by extension: 16,654 hectares of sea along 32 km of Ionian coast between Porto Cesareo and Nardò, from Punta Prosciutto to Torre Inserraglio, divided into three zones (A integral reserve in front of the Strea peninsula and between Torre Sant'Isidoro and Casa Giorgella, B and C with activities allowed at different levels). Abbey in isolated position downstream of the hamlet Monastero, probably founded in 1009 according to a writing by Saint Pier Damiani, on the remains of a Roman villa. In the crypt there is a fresco of the Madonna with the Child in the thirteenth century; in the porch of the upper church there is a St. George who kills the dragon; in two niches frescoes attributed to Andrea De Magistris (the Virgin and the Magdalene, St. Lucia and St. Catherine). Open for the festive liturgy at 10:00.

Area protected by the Regional Parks Plan, known for sinkholes and sinkholes; the main caves are the Tana del Forno (1,300 m of development, 204 m of depth), the Conca and the Tana delle Turbiglie (over 800 m of development).

Stone bridges on the Roya River and kayak routes on the Bevera stream.

Permanent Museum of municipal property with works acquired by the Suzzara Prize, established in 1948 by Dino Villani and the mayor Tebe Mignoni with the support of Cesare Zavattini, on the idea of equaling art to the products of work: the winners also received cheese, animals and eggs. The collection documents the season of realism with works by Guttuso, Sassu, Birolli, Romagnoni, Zigaina and Ligabue; the Prize is renewed every two years and temporary exhibitions alternate during the year.

On Sunday after 15 August six districts (Burò, Ghetto, La Bianca, Nona, Polveriera, S. Antonio) run a run of donkeys, born in 1965 and according to the tradition designed in the first sixteenth century by Agostino Chigi on the Sienese model, with procession in costumes of the sixteenth century, Carroccio towed by oxen and flagners. The protagonist of the festival is the yellow bread of Allumiere, with durum wheat semolina ground twice and black truffle of the Monti della Tolfa; in June there is Asinitaly, national fair of the donkey.

Information point of the Park in Rabbi Fonti, at the thermal baths: material and publications of the Park and an operator who advises programs and excursions to be done alone or with the experts of the Park, such as the guided exits at dawn in autumn for the greed of the deer and the snowshoeing among the farms. Fortified village of Pesarese, Orange Flag and among the most beautiful villages in Italy, dominated by the Malatestian fortress linked to the history of Paolo and Francesca sung by Dante in the 5th Song of Hell; around, two circles of walls and paths of the Bosco di Paolo and Francesca.

It is located in the mill built in 1841 on the shore of the lake, bought in 1887 by the Abegg of Zurich; the museum was born in 1953 at the will of the family, presented as the first museum of industrial archaeology in Italy, and in 1976 was donated to the municipality. It exhibits basins for the artisan and industrial trattura, tools for the breeding of the baco and for the twisting and a large spinning machine in the round of the first half of the nineteenth century, with working machinery; a section is dedicated to the future of silk in biomedical and cosmetic. Open Saturday 14.30-17.30 and Sunday 9.30-12.30 and 14.30-17.30.

Baroque village rebuilt after the earthquake of 1693, between the late Baroque towns of the Val di Noto UNESCO World Heritage Site and Borgo dei Borghi 2025: the sanctuary of Santa Maria della Stella with the Nativity of Andrea della Robbia, the Mother Church with the museum in the crypts, the former abbey of San Benedetto and the Norman Santa Maria la Vetere.

Built between 1573 and 1592 by Alonzo Sanchez de Luna d'Aragona, treasurer of the Kingdom of Naples and then duke of Sant'Arpino, on the site of the ancient church of Sant'Elpidio; embellished in 1798 for the wedding of the sixth duke, then passed to Caracciolo and in 1903 was purchased and restored by Giuseppe Macrì, who in 1932 left it to the Municipality. It has a square plan around a courtyard, a pipe doorway with doric columns, a balcony with the ducal coat of arms and traces of paintings in the vaults of the noble floor; today it is the seat of the Town Hall.

Small church with a single nave with a barrel vault and square apse, a hut façade with an ancient fresco of the saint above the portal and a pyramid cusp bell tower. Inside a wooden altar carved and gilded of the seventeenth century with the relics of the saint, the vault of the presbytery painted in starry sky with the Agnus Dei, frescoes of St. Anthony the Abbot and the Adoration of the Magi and various canvases, some in bad condition. It is among the Places of the Heart of the FAI.
Green and transparent water bay, with sandy backdrop and small pebbles suitable for diving and a beautiful sunset; well served by parking lots and the MareBus.

Built in the fifteenth century by the Orsini, lords of Fiano: a robust central cylindrical mast, thirty meters high and crowned with blackbirds, with a square side tower. It leans on Porta Capena, the entrance of the village; inside a courtyard with the staircase that goes up to the noble floor.

Norman church with three aisles, with marble bas-reliefs under the altars and a marble icon from the Gaginian period of the sixteenth century on the main altar; it preserves a wooden crucifix of the seventeenth century probably attributed to Fra Umile da Petralia, restored in 2006, the chapel of the Blessed Sacrament with the great fresco of the Fall of Manna and, in sacristy, portraits of the archpriests from 1601 to 1892.

On Cuccuru Nolza (740 m), the highest point of the plateau of Pranu, about 7 km from the village: quadrilobed nuraghe with high mast today about 13 meters and four corner tower bastion, surrounded by a village of huts of about 2,5 hectares. The village dates back to the 16th-XV century BC, mastic and first towers in shale to the 14th-XIII, the other two towers in porphyry to the 12th century BC; studied by Giovanni Lilliu, excavated between 1994 and 2000, returned to the top a small courtyard with seat and fireplace. A staircase leads to the top of the tower; the stop of the Green Train Mandas-Sorgono is about 300 meters.

Relief that separates the Casentino from the Valtiberina, on the 1,100 meters with the summit of Monte Castello, rich in water and covered with oak, chestnut and beech woods; suitable for hikers of all levels, offers views from the top. On the ascent, the village of Falciano, gate of the Alpe, preserves two ancient mills still in operation.

Born from a chapel erected around 1487 around the elm of the apparition, destroyed in 1558 and rebuilt, it was completed in 1884 by Pio Casoli; eighteenth-century façade, baroque bell tower of over 40 meters, high altar of Carmela Adani (1938) and frescoes by Anselmo Govi (1935). Visitable on request.

Raised in 1480 in Gothic-Catalan style, with baroque façade of the early eighteenth century; it preserves a fourteenth-century table of the Madonna with Child and the mausoleum of the Count of Moriana.

Beech of about 20 hectares, about 1600 meters in Val Cervara, convales of the Aceretta between Monte Marcolano and Monte Schiena di Cavallo. The dendrochronological analyses of the University of Tuscia have rebuilt a series from 1523 to today, with a beech of at least 503 rings; it is a forest where the trees are born and die without human intervention, inhabited by deer, wolves and marsican bear. Valle Cervara is among the beech forests of the Park included on the UNESCO site of the ancient primordial beech woods of the Carpathians and other regions of Europe.

Ancient Byzantine village at the foot of the Small Sila, among the calanchi of the Marchesato, known for the murals of Vico Leone; it preserves the main church of St. Nicholas and St. Mary Major, the oldest in the village, and outside the town the Sanctuary of Santa Spina, which since 1523 has kept a thorn of the crown of Christ.

Cascina Picchetta's manor house, already defined as palatium in 1575, when Lucrezia Cioccara acquired possessions; enlarged between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, passed to the Jesuits and then to the Natta d'Alfiano. Purchased by the Park in 1989, since 2001 it is home: U-shaped plant with towers at the corners and tiburium with lantern, grotesque decorations in the Hall of the Octagon and landscapes in the west porch. From spring to autumn, salt on the ground floor and gardens open on Sunday afternoons according to an annual calendar, with free entrance and guided tours.

Roman complex near the amphitheatre with a thermal building and three houses, lived from the 1st century BC to the VI-VII century A.D.: fragments of frescoes and mosaics with rosettes between acanto leaves.

Ancient extra-urban parish church about 2 km south of the center, erected between VII and VIII century along a medieval path between Adriatic and Tyrrhenian; it became a center of Marian devotion for the apparitions narrated by tradition, was expanded in the XVII century and, according to tradition, St. Francis stopped there going to Verna.

Three marble tombs of the counts Andreani made in the fourteenth century, in about fifty years, by the champions: a Romanesque of Iacobo Andreani in white marble of Musso and black stone of Varenna, a Gothic with three statues attributed to the champions masters, and a Gothic flowered commissioned by Stefano Andreani in 1371. They are what is left of the cemetery that until the early nineteenth century occupied the churchyard.

Village perched on a hill of tuff between the valleys of Rio Chiaro and Rio Torbido, almost abandoned due to the fragility of the rock, today one of the most visited in Europe.

Roman maritime colony founded in 194 BC on the left bank of Lake Patria and assigned to the veterans of the second Punic war; flourished in Augustian age and between the end I and II century A.D., then decayed with the impaludation of the area. The hole with Capitolium, basilica and theatre was discovered in 1932; in the urban park of over 67,000 m2, recently redeveloped, you can see a spa complex with a bath still fed by natural springs, vaulted substruttuzioni, a wall in cross-linked work and over 80 meters of basolato of the Via Domitiana. Part of the artifacts is exhibited at the Museo Archeologico dei Campi Flegrei in Baia.

The fifteenth-century church rebuilt in the eighteenth century by Giuseppe Merenda, with the stone portal of Istria by Marco Cedrini from 1465 and the choir in walnut.
12th century church renovated at the end of the last century, with apse frescoes by the Sienese painter A. Villigiardi (1896).

Cited from the end of the 8th century and already a garrison of the diocese of Luni, it is considered a symbol of the Romanesque in Lunigiana: in sandstone, with protruding façade, carved reliefs and capitals storied with symbols of medieval beasts. It rises on the right bank of the Aulella near a medieval bridge, beyond which there are the ruins of an 11th century castle, along the Via del Volto Santo. Inside a late medieval triptych with the Virgin enthroned between the Saints Cornelius and Cyprian, with the predella depicting the transport of the Holy Face from Lucca.

The ancient Suessa between the Roccamonfina volcano and Garigliano: the Romanesque cathedral, the Roman theatre with the cryptoportico, the archaeological museum in the ducal castle and the long Roman bridge of the Aurunci.

Marine cave discovered in 1932 by the fisherman Luigi Buonocore: the light enters from an underwater crack and tints the water of emerald green, while stalactites and stalagmites form columns under the vault. It is thought as a didactic journey on the history and daily life of the city; the final seat is planned on the lower floors of Palazzo Ferrari. Rare example of late antique defensive architecture, born in the 5th century as a Roman military outpost downstream of Castelseprio castrum and then used by Goths, Byzantines and Longobards. In the 8th century the Benedictine nuns transformed it into oratory and mausoleum; on the second floor there are frescoes with Christ blessing and angels, the Virgin and Child, a group of saints and a theory of nuns in prayer, restored from 1978 to 2019 by Pinin Brambilla Barcilon. The excavations with the University of Padua found at the entrance a horse burial of the sixth century.

Country of the plain of Chierese, a land of Roman centuriation, where the castle donated in 1619 by Carlo Emanuele I became Palazzo Grosso, rebuilt by Bernardo Vittone and today City Hall and seat of the Museum of the Soundscape; Vittone also worked at the parish church of the Assumption, where in 1842 he was baptized San Domenico Savio, born in the nearby hamlet of San Giovanni.

It has only one nave and two side baroque altars; the altar of the Sorrows is by the sculptor Pietro Antonio Perucca di Valperga, who completed it in 1708.

Considered the oldest ironworks in Tuscany, operating from the fourteenth century until the eighties of the twentieth century, it is an example of industrial archaeology: the mountain steelmaking used water and local woods to work the Elba mineral, enhanced by Cosimo I in the sixteenth century and by the Grand Ducal road of 1778. You can see sweaters, wheels and forges and in the workshops you can try the techniques of the blacksmith; it is the main stage of the itinerary of the Iron of the Ecomuseo.

Palace of the late eighteenth century designed by Giovan Battista Vinci, a rare example of wooden frame masonry, which in 1810 hosted Gioacchino Murat; today a receptive structure.

Opened in August 1975, it exhibits the triassic fossils collected in the Cortina area largely by Rinaldo Zardini, one of the largest collections of the genus: megalodontes, shells of marine invertebrates, corals and sponges that tell the geological evolution of the Ampezzo. Borgo del Casentino with the remains of one of the oldest castles in the valley: the polygonal tower houses the documentation centre on rural culture, next to the palace with a loggia of the early fifteenth century; in the territory the Romanesque parish church of Sant'Antonino in Socana with the altar of an Etruscan temple of the fifth century BC and the church of Sante Flora and Lucilla a Carda.

Born in 1976 as an exhibition of the Florenzano foundation and municipal museum since 1994, in the former convent of Sant'Anna: more than 900 objects from the late nineteenth century to the sixties on agriculture, linen weaving, crafts and sacred vestments, with a multimedia room and sound biographies of Women's Voci.

The village is about 550 meters above the Eleuterio valley, about 30 km from Palermo, dominated by the great rock of the Fortress; the main monument is the Castle Beccadelli Bologna of 1559, home of the Archaeological Museum of the Eleuterio Valley, with the finds of the ancient Makella dug on the Montagnola. The road through the village would be built by the Romans in the second half of the third century BC.

Colonia diritto Latino founded by the Romans in 328 BC on the left bank of Liri, in the valley between Mount Cairo and the Ausoni and Aurunci mountains; celebrated by Tito Livio, it was destroyed in 124 BC and rebuilt a little further south as Fabrateria Nova. Deep canyon dug in thousands of years by the Sagittarius river, WWF oasis since 1991 and regional nature reserve since 1997; English travellers of the late nineteenth century called it "fearful and beautiful." A panoramic view of the gorges can be reached from via Duca degli Abruzzi.

The most important Lombard building of Salerno, seat of the court of Prince Arechi: it rests on a Roman thermal frigidarium then used as a Christian cemetery, with the chapel of the Virgin and the hypogeum; it also hosted the Salernitana Medical School.

Villa built from 1593 to 1647 for the Selvatico on the hill of Sant'Elena, with the sudoriferous cave frequented already in the Middle Ages; in the hall the frescoes of the Stories of Antenor of Luca Ferrari (1650) and in the dome works of Lorenzo Bedogni and of the Paduanino. It climbs with 144 steps to the romantic park of about 11 hectares redesigned by Giuseppe Jappelli, with thermal lakes.

The highest center of the municipality, with a historical center to walk, marked paths between ancient chestnut groves (the Via della Castagna) and a panorama from Monte Amiata to the coast. In the old town hall the House museum dedicated to folk traditions, daily life and ancient crafts.

Centre of Alta Irpinia 750 meters, called Carbonara until 1861: less than 2 km from the village the Archaeological Park preserves the ancient center abandoned after the earthquake of 1930, while the ethnographic Museum "Beniamino Tartaglia" exhibits about 14,000 objects of the Altirpina life.

Colle of about 400 meters 1 km from the castle towards Montefabbri, picnic destination and walks with playground and nature trail; at the crossroads with Via Vittorio Veneto the small neoclassical church of the Madonna del Monte.

The spa of the seventeenth century rises on the ruins of an older one and uses hyperthermal volcanic waters at almost 43 °C for baths and mud; in the nineteenth century there was added the Grand Hotel delle Terme, neoclassic, designed by Damiani Almejda, loved by the Palermo nobility and base of Ignazio Florio during the Targa Florio.
Ruins of the Da Varano in a historic village of the Apennines.

Secular chestnuts of the reserve: the Gigante Buono can be reached with the Salice-Greco route (800 meters, about 1 hour), the Giants of Cavallopoli along a path of 3.2 km towards the waterfall of the same name, tourist to the trees and then for expert hikers equipped.
From the Mediterranean maquis to paleoanthropology.

From the cliff the view embraces the coast from Neptune to Terracina, the Pontine islands and the Oasis of Ninfa; from the terraces of Norba take off the paraglidings, in one of the most spectacular launch sites in Europe, overlooking the Pontina Plain, Lepini and Ninfa.

Church of the sixteenth century in front of the ancient porta a mare of the medieval walls, at the end of Via Santa Maria: on the portal the Madonna and Child of Bartolomeo Ordóñez, inside an altar in polychrome marble with a sixteenth-century canvas of the Virgin of Carmel.
The center of Lesa combines palaces, arcades and alleys to the lakefront; from Via Gibertini starts the walk towards Belgirate, which follows a stretch of an ancient Roman road.
Church and Gothic convent erected in 1252, with a major altar in polychrome marble of 1644 and the sarcophagus of Nicola Ruffo of 1372.
In the district of Augeluzzi, between olive groves and trulli, the cave dates back to the Middle Paleolithic and testifies to the presence of Neanderthal man in the territory.

Village with a medieval profile on the hills of Treviso, dominated by the Rocca on Mount Rich, linked to the queen of Cyprus Caterina Cornaro, Eleonora Duse and Freya Stark; in the center porch the Duomo with works of Lorenzo Lotto and the Civic Museum in the Loggia della Ragione.
A cycle of late dogotic frescoes intact.

Built in the 11th century in lava stone on a rocky spur overlooking the sea, with panoramic terrace on the coast and on the Faraglioni of Aci Trezza. It houses the Civic Museum, inaugurated in 1985, with an archaeological collection from prehistory to the Middle Ages, a mineralogical one with minerals of the Cyclops and Aci Castello islands (analcimes, phillipsite, aracicular aragonite) and volcanic origin, and a paleontological one with fossils from Mesozoic to Pleistocene, among which ammonites.

Built in 1603 next to the foundation around which the village was born and became parish in 1605 at the request of Marco Mancino; the foundation no longer exists, but its site is recognized in Madrice square along the current Via Roma, the ancient directing trazzera.
The flavors of Pinerolean in a museum.

A combination of medieval alleys, arches and vaults with remains of walls and towers. Since 1982 Italian and foreign artists have been painting on the walls of the houses every year their interpretation of the nativity: today the works are over 50 and form an open-air gallery.

In the capital the clock tower of 1739 and the church of Santa Maria Assunta, with white marble facade and three bells merged in the sixteenth century, among the oldest in Versilia. The territory has been inhabited since ancient times, as shown by the tombs of the Ligurian Apuani.
The peasant life of an Ionian country.
The Renaissance cloisters of the Benedictine monastery of St. Peter, today space for exhibitions and meetings.
The collection of weights and scales considered the most important in Europe, with a weight of the fourteenth century.
The Last Supper of 1559.
The medieval village in spiral.

The municipality of the great airport and the port channel of fishing boats, on the mouth of the Tiber: here stood the imperial ports of Claudio and Traiano, with the necropolis of the Sacred Island and the Museum of Ships, and along the coast the beaches of Fregene and the oasis of the Roman coast.
The history of the most famous salami of Parmense, in the cellars of a castle.

Inaugurated in 1935 on a project by Ettore Baldanza after the earthquake of 1908 had destroyed the cathedral of 1841, of which only the Chapel of the Blessed Sacrament remains; neoclassical with three naves, 62 meters long, with wooden ceiling with drawers painted by D. Cricket. It houses a marble Madonna from the 16th century, perhaps Gagini from Oppido Vecchia, the chapel of the Santissima Annunziata with the wooden group of A. Head and the Baroque processional throne of the Annunziata; in the Chapter Room vestments bishops from the seventeenth century and an Ecce Homo wooden donated by San Carlo Borromeo.
The oldest Romanesque church in the Lower Parma.
The story of Varese in a villa.

Medieval stone village of Oltrepò Pavese dominated by the castle of the captain of Ventura Jacopo Dal Verme, with walls over four meters thick, a contemporary art museum and a natural reserve of over 80 hectares; in the village the church of São Paulo, the fourteenth-century oratory of San Rocco and the octagonal cemetery.
Woods, paths and a neo-Gothic villa on the Hills.
One hundred meters suspended on the void above the waterfall.
The gulf between Circeo and Gaeta.

The last intact city belt of South Tyrol: about 10 meters high, the walls were rebuilt in the sixteenth century by order of Emperor Maximilian I after the battle of Calva on 22 May 1499, the Confederates plundered the city; the extension, proposed by military architect Jörg Kölderer, was completed in 1580. There are three door-towers and the ring of walls around the old shopping centre; sections of the oldest walls are seen in the alley San Pancrazio.
The avant-garde painter born in Gradisca.

Medieval building of the late 9th-beginning 10th century, originally of Greek rite, with polygonal apse in local stone cones facing east according to the Byzantine tradition and a large biphora that illuminates the interior.
The baroque of the Josafatti in the heart of the village.

The island of the Rabbit is located in front of Torre Chianca, inside the protected marine area; between the tower and the island, in very low waters, a submerged necropolis is visible to tourists and bathers.
The medieval bridge on the pilgrim's way to Loreto.
The sanctuary of Blessed Amandola.
The emblem of Nuragic civilization.
The protected area in the territory of Alghero which includes the bay of Porto Conte between the promontory of Capo Caccia and Punta Giglio.
In 1681, transformed and enlarged in 1838, with presbytery covered by octagonal dome.
The village of the rafters.
Hemp and nut oil in peasant life.
View of the Apennines.
Monks' caves and views of the gulf.
The Visconti hunting campaign between the Certosa and the castle of Pavia.

18th-century parish church in the center of the village, neoclassical, with tetrastyle pronao stone columns and classical tympanum that suggest an ancient temple; rectangular hall with two lateral rooms and bell tower facing north. Italia.it underlines the austerity of the whole carnica.

Crypt of the twelfth century under the apse of the Duomo, three naves with vaults cruising on two rows of unequal columns, with traces of the door and walled windows and an altar rested on two fifteenth century foliage capitals. It recalls the parish church of Santo Stefano, the first Christian church of the village (about 5th century), built near a Roman sacellus of which remain a stele to Jupiter and two capitals. Visitable during the cathedral hours.

Along the left bank of the Sele, in the regional reserve Foce Sele-Tanagro: 110 hectares, about 70 occupied by the invasion of the dam of 1934, wetland of international importance (Ramsar) with reeds. Celebrated for the otter, counts 184 species, 47 nesting, and the paths allow you to observe aquatic plants and fauna.

The bell of peace, 3,36 meters high, merged in 1924 with the bronze of the cannons of the nations in war: every evening it rings 100 chimes for the fallen; it is reached with half an hour on foot from the center.

From the centre the path follows the Rujo stream towards the Valley of San Daniele, passing next to ancient mills; the route ring from Piazza Roma (9,1 km, about 3 hours and 30, difference in altitude 501 m, difficulty E) touches the churches of San Silvestro and San Gaetano and the Bosco delle Penne Mozze and goes back along the Via dell'Acqua.

On the mountains of Torno you can reach on foot the Avelli, tub graves (V-VI century A.D.) dug in the erratic boulders left by the glaciers, in the localities Maas, Rasina, Piazz and Negrenza. In Montepiatto stands the Stone Pendula, erratic stone shaped like a fungus and natural monument; some erratic boulders were recognized as natural monuments by the Lombardy Region in 1984.

Giant bench n. 142 of the project by Chris Bangle, on the top of one of the two morainic hills south of the village, overlooking the mountains of the Alpine arch of the Valley of Susa. On the other side of the hill, just below, stands the manor house of Menate, quoted from 1345; at the foot of the slope flows the Dora Riparia.
A small castle in the woods.

In the hamlet of Gudon the local museum, founded in 1972 in the Pfleghaus, exhibits agricultural tools and artisans, a collection of paintings, sacred and profane art and documents of local history (open from Easter to All Saints). The fifteenth-century church of San Martino has the sacristy, called the Koburger chapel, frescoed by Ambrosius Gander; the Castel Summersberg, of the fourteenth century, opens the courtyard only on Monday evening in summer by reservation.
The baths of an emperor on the lake.

How to enter a house of the 1930s still inhabited: over 600 ceramics collected by the collector Giuseppe Gianetti since 1932, including 201 porcelains of Meissen of the eighteenth century and Italian and European majolica, with a contemporary ceramic section.

Mount Pelpi (1480 m) closes the basin of Bedonia. Along the Strada del Fungo Porcino, all curves and views over the Parma hills, you can reach the steps of Tomarlo, Bocco and Cento Croci, on the border between Emilia and Liguria.

Village of the Argentina valley among the most beautiful villages in Italy, 3 km from the sea: the medieval bridge with fifteen arches, the convent of San Domenico with the Adoration of the Magi del Parmigianino, the castle and the beach of Arma di Taggia.

The largest common fruit of South Tyrol, between Merano and Bolzano: in Lana di Sotto the parish with the door-to-door altar by Hans Schnatterpeck, the largest in the Alps, and the Museum of Fruit Growing; around the Gaul Gorge, the path of the Brandis Roggia, the Foiana Farm Museum and Monte San Vigilio by cable car.

The center is aligned with Corso Garibaldi, which follows the path of the Roman consular, and perpendicular to the stream Arda. Palazzo Grossi, private and non-visitable, shows a Renaissance frieze in terracotta and two ogival windows; private also Palazzo Bertamini Lucca.
The Roman Atri.
The house of San Terenzo where Mary and Percy B lived. Shelley.
A winding path that climbs up to the fork of Pala Barzana and then descends, with steep and dry hairpin bends, towards the Colvera Valley.

The ancient Teate Marrucinorum on a hill between the Maiella and the sea: the Warrior of Capestrano at the Museum of Villa Frigerj, the Civitella, the theatre, the thermal baths and the Roman temples, the Cathedral of San Giustino and the Marrucino Theatre.
The Roman Lilibe.

Medieval town of the Isarco Valley dominated by the Sabiona cliff, the acropolis of Tyrol with its monastery; the old town has paved streets in porphyry and Gothic churches, the Civic Museum in the former convent of the Capuchins houses the Treasury of Loreto and Albrecht Dürer designed it in 1494 from the point now called Dürerstein.

The ancient Castel San Marco, abandoned in the eighteenth century for hydrogeological failure and collapsed in 1771, was rebuilt downstream by Pope Clement XIV as Castel Clementino and completed under Pius VI; it took the name of Servigliano in 1863. The neoclassical village has a quadrangular plan, three monumental doors and two main streets that cross. In the week of August, the donation of the Piana di San Gualtiero by the abbot of Farfa (1450) was recalled.
From the bishop's garrison to the Renaissance palace.
The charred library of antiquity.
The urns of the Bronze Age in the Gesso Valley.

Late Aragonese parish church on the hill of the historic center, probably begun between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries (inscriptions of 1555 and 1695 in two chapels). Façade in pink trachite with Mannerist portal and rose window of about 3 meters, bell tower of about 30 meters with sundial; inside a single nave with communicating chapels, presbytery with star vault and keys depicting St. Gavino on horseback, eighteenth-century polygonal baptismal font and Baroque pulpit. Feast of the saint on October 25.

Romanesque church that in 1157 Bishop Enrico Montecuccoli put at the head of a network of 30 chapels; the interior has three naves on pillars, four of which octagonal. It preserves the red marble saints water table of Verona donated in 1609 for the baptism of the leader and writer Raimondo Montecuccoli.
Park in the historic center in a panoramic position between the sea and Apennines, from which comes the nickname of "Balcony of the Sibillini."
A Venetian square in the mountains.

In the medieval halls of the castle, he tells of the life and movement of David Lazzaretti (1834-1878), the "prophet of the Amiata" founder of the Jurisdavid Community, with paintings, objects, photographs, clothes and banners; among the pieces the garments of Lazzaretti, finds from the Museum of criminal anthropology of Turin and a letter in which Fr Giovanni Bosco offers to testify in his favor.
The disappeared countries of Sardinia.

A place of worship already in the 12th century, rebuilt in the 16th century and rebuilt in Baroque forms in the 17th century with frescoes; it has a marble portal of Vezza of 1748 and a side in white marble of 1902, and was consecrated to Saint Martin of Tours in 1921.
The mosaics of a Roman house.
