Fresh local produce.

Built between 1121 and 1198 by the counts of Loritello, it had originally three naves; damaged by the earthquake of 1744, it was rebuilt to a single nave preserving the portal in limestone with floral motifs. Inside, the niches of the lateral altars with traces of colour and baroque stuccos remain; behind, the bell tower shows wall stratifications from the Norman foundation to the twentieth century. Facade and roof collapsed with the earthquake of 1905, after which it was abandoned in favor of the nearby church of Santa Maria Assunta.

A small late Baroque church near the court of Naples North, entrusted to the Confraternity of the Gonfalone del Santo Sepolcro: Latin cross plan, dome of the first decades of the eighteenth century and valuable majolica floor; on the high altar stood the canvas of Francesco Solimena with San Bonaventura that receives from the Madonna the Gonfalone.
A ten-hectare liberty park.

The fifteenth-century complex was created to accommodate travellers and pilgrims at the ford of the Secchia, on the streets towards Sassuolo, Frassinoro, Lucca and Rome; it was then a farm. Today, with a porch courtyard and tower, is home to the theatre center La Corte Ospitale; in the church of Santa Maria (16th century) remains fragments of frescoes of the Garofalo (1543).
Piazza del centro storico indicated by the Abruzzo Region among the stops of the visit.

Also known as the Ethnographic Museum of Farming and Craftsmanship, it is housed in the Professional Institute for Agriculture and Environment and was set up in 2000 with the pupils: agricultural tools, domestic tools, shoemakers, bottai and blacksmiths and three permanent photographic exhibitions.
Romanesque building with a rose window on the façade, flanked by two bell towers.
A thousand alpine flowers.

Medieval village overlooking the sea on the southern side of Mount Conero, born around an 11th century castle, with the square of the church of San Nicola and its viewpoint on the coast. The territory includes beaches such as the Two Sisters, the Picena necropolis of the Pini and the Badia of San Pietro on the top of the Conero.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 2 of the 6 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
Two kilometers of white sand.
The Sibillini Carbonai trade.
The place of surrender to the French.
The palace dates back to 1530-1551; the church, Collegiate since 1580, was rebuilt in 1717 after the collapse of 1688 and preserves works by Tarquinio Salvi, Agabiti, Ridolfi and Giovanni Contarini.

It dates back to the middle of the seventeenth century: the central aisle was built on the ruins of an ancient newsstand erected by the early Christians in the place where in 252 the three martyr brothers stayed. Impressive architecture with a majestic access staircase; inside relics and religious symbols.

Sacile has the historic center on two islands of the river Livenza, with Piazza del Popolo and the loggia of the fifteenth-century town hall, Palazzo Ragazzoni and the Cathedral of San Nicolò with the frescoes of Pino Casarini, whose works are exhibited in the nearby gallery dedicated to him.
Seaside resort of the Riviera di Ponente with the Wall of the lovers, the Budello parallel to the promenade and the Benedictine church of Santa Croce overlooking the sea.

On the karst hill above Piazza della Repubblica, the symbol of the city: prehistoric castle, castle of the Patriarch of Aquileia, Venetian fort, Napoleonic garrison and Italian observatory in the Great War. The walk on the Venetian walls preserves traces of the fighting of 1915-1917; in the mast an exhibition on the Karst territory and, according to PromoTurismoFVG, the paleontological museum. Open Saturday and Sunday 9.30-13 and 16.30-19; you walk up the paths of the Great War Park or with the RoccaBus.
Prehistoric signs along the mountain road.
High-altitude lawns under 3,000.
Indicated as closed by the MiC: check at the tour desk
The bishop's city.
For the pupil's triptych.

Church at the foot of the castle, in the center of the village, rebuilt in the seventeenth century on a plant of 1324 and several times renovated; the patron saint is celebrated in mid-January with bonfires, processions and typical sweets.
Castle, moat and ancient fruits.

Early Christian Baptistery among the oldest in the West, linked to Pope Marcello I from which they take their name church and village; the bathtub in the center was fed by a perennial spring. It was probably destroyed in the 6th century, rebuilt in the 12th century; it re-employses fragments of a Roman villa and preserves frescoes of the VI-VII and the 9th century. Included in the integrated ticket "Certosa and Padula" .
The balcony between Apuane and Apennines.
Rudolf Stolz's Macabre Dance.

Country on top of a hill between Macerata and San Ginesio, considered the home of cooked wine: historic center almost intact with the Brunforte Castle of the Lords of Loro, the Tower of Victory overlooking the Conero alla Maiella, the thirteenth-century Santa Maria di Piazza and the church of San Francesco with the exhibition of the tools of cooked wine.
Memorial of the fallen of the two world wars, built in the sacred area that housed the church of the Crucifix.
Path also accessible to people with motor and visual disabilities
The Matterhorn view.
Palace of 1770, one of the best preserved eighteenth-century villas in the city, with golden façade in tuff of Aspra.
The oldest way.
Pieve documented since 1189 on a natural terrace, restored between the XV and XX century; the gray stone façade has bas-reliefs and arches, inside works by Simone De Magistris and Morale da Fermo.
A clock at 10 hours, rarity of the Napoleonic age.
The crafts of the past, with objects donated by the country.

Built in the first thirty years of the seventeenth century, with a sixteenth-century bell tower and clock working: it preserves a Santa Caterina in marble (1534) and a water saint (1530) by Antonello Gagini, works by Andrea Calamech, Rinaldo Bonanno and Filippo Jannelli, baptismal font of 1625, pulpit of 1648, choir of 1612 and silver seventeenth-century Messinese. On the floor runs the dark chamber sundial made in 1854 by Nicolò Perroni Basquez.
The fourteenth-century town hall has been rebuilt several times, with the clock tower, overlooking Piazza Saffi in front of San Mercuriale.
The amphitheatre square dedicated to pianist Mieczysław Horszowski, who held the inaugural concert in the summer of 1986.
Salesian missions to the world.

In the halls of the Municipal Museum of Ponza Porto is set up the Permanent Exhibition of Color, with eight panels of 4 x 1.40 meters on the chromatic reliefs of the three historic centers: Ponza Porto, Santa Maria and Le Forna; there is also a photo library.
Medieval bridge of 1358 in blocks of local stone called "cardellino" with a single arch of 37 meters on the Aniene.

About 2,800 hectares of cliffs, valleys, streams and waterfalls, with Serra Middai, habitat of royal eagle, deer, deer and mouflon; the ascent to Punta Margiani Pubusa (1.325 m) passes through the sinkhole of Su Stampu and the monument of Perda Liana. The excursions can be booked at the Palazzina Liberty.
The profane Moncalvo.
You walk in through a crenellated door.
Ancient house and farm with the farm for farm workers, since 1900 dairy farm; it is located near the dam of Pertusillo, in a tourist area of the valley.

The ancient church, mentioned by the second half of the thirteenth century, was expanded several times, also by Simone Cantoni at the end of the eighteenth century; the new church, begun in 1904 and consecrated in 1926, is three naves on a Latin cross plan in brick and stone, in eclectic style between late Romanesque and Gothic, with octagonal apses. The bell tower, 77.45 m high, is among the highest in Italy and leads to the top of the Golden Angel, considered protector of Lissone.

Borgo dell'Agro Veientano along the Via Francigena, on the edge of the Veio Park: Palazzo Chigi with the Museo dell'Agro Veientano and the tower of Andrea Bruno, the church of San Lorenzo with the dark room sundial, the baroque villa of Versaglia, the catacomb of Monte Stallone and the Mola in the Valley of Sorbo.

A fourteenth-century house-tower with trilobed mullioned windows where he lived until his death in 1311, Gaia da Camino, quoted by Dante in the 16th canto of Purgatory, lady of the village from 1307 with her husband Tolberto. The frescoes by unknown author (XIV-XV century) depict court life, warriors in armor, personifications of the Sciences and landscapes; today it is the museum and art gallery.

A large stone building about 1,000 meters in the upper Elvo Valley, built in the mid-eighteenth century by the Ambrosetti family, Lanieri di Sordevolo; it owes its name to the Trappist monks who took refuge there from 1796 to 1802 fleeing from revolutionary France. It houses the cell of the Ecomuseo del Biellese dedicated to rural construction techniques, with guided tours, educational activities and guesthouse; it is reached on foot in about 10 minutes from the SP512 (Tracillino, about 8 km west of Oropa) or in about an hour of mule track from Prera.
The UNESCO beech woods of Gargano.
The sanctuary at the foot of the Musinè.
The greenway on the former 1930 military railroad that departs from Treviso between streams, fields, country churches and Venetian villas, along the Sile towards Quinto di Treviso.

On Mount Sant'Angelo, the last spur of the Ausoni mountains on the sea, the sanctuary was built mainly between the II and I century BC in cement work: the Temple Major on high podium rests on a terrace with twelve arches, with the rock and the oracular cave, cisterns and the Small Temple linked to the cult of Feronia. Recent excavations attribute the major temple to Venus Obsequens more than to Jupiter Anxur. From the terrace the view goes from the Circeo to Gaeta and the Pontine islands; open every day 9-20.

The Sile, 90 km long and one of the longest rivers in Europe, crosses the municipality and is protected by the Regional Natural Park of the river Sile (about 4,152 hectares in 11 municipalities). The Alzaia is a bike path on the banks from the bridge of Musestre to the basin of Portegrandi, part of the Girasile greenway; the river is navigable by boat, canoe and kayak.
Chestnuts and borlengos, from the hall to the woods.
the museum remains closed to the public from 6 January to 2 April, open from Tuesday to Sunday (source: museumcorreale.it); tickets also online

In the ancient convent of the Dominicans he tells more than seven hundred years of paper tradition: a medieval gully rebuilt and working, the phases of hand-working, a section on the filigree and demonstrations of the master papermakers, with workshops to make their own sheet.
On the shore of the largest lake of the morainic amphitheatre of Ivrea, where remains a palafittic village of the Bronze Age UNESCO heritage.
The quartz beaches of Sinis.
Built in 1908 and active until the 1970s, it is one of the best preserved industrial archaeology sites in Sicily, today dedicated to renewable energy and didactic dissemination.
At the extreme tip of the promontory of the old town, next to Santa Scolastica, over three thousand years of stratified history until the first settlements of the Bronze Age.

Heart of the village crossed by the course of the People, opened at the end of the nineteenth century demolishing Porta Romana: from the loggia the panorama goes from Monte Conero to Macerata, Recanati and Loreto. On the square the bronze statue of Ottrano, the Porta Nuova called Porticella with the staircase to the ancient part, and the desecrated Church of the Angels with the signs of the battle grenades of 1944; inside the fourteenth-century walls, Largo Bramante is another viewpoint on hills, Conero and sea.
The exhibits of Cominium and the former vote of Pescarola.

Anthropological demoetanological museum in Palazzo Barone, also spread over the territory to the Roman villa of the district of San Tommaso. Four sections: rural life and wine tradition with tools and tuff cellars; photographs of community life; Saint Barbato, born in Castelvenere in 602 and then bishop of Benevento; archaeology and prehistory with Sannito-Roman epigraphs, cippi and remains of the palafitta.

Ancient rural village of the principality of Bisignano and Corigliano farmhouse under Sanseverino and Saluzzo, where Albanian refugees came to escape from the Turks between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. In the historic hilly centre there are two parish churches dedicated to Santa Maria di Costantinopoli, one of Greek rite and one of Latin rite, the church of the Confraternity, the palace of the town hall and some old fountains.
A senator's library and the smallest book in the world.

A shrine town built around the Basilica of the Holy House (1468-1587), which according to tradition houses the house of Nazareth, which arrived here in 1294; the fortress is surrounded by walls with round walkways and overlooks Piazza della Madonna with the Fontana Maggiore and the Apostolic Palace, seat of the Papal Museum with the paintings of Lorenzo Lotto.
Visit of the churches by reservation at least 2 days before: quiparcosanmauro@libero.it or tel. 0921 674083 (Parco delle Madonie)

On the noble floor of the Renaissance palace started after 1500 for Francesca di Brandenburg: coffered ceiling of 1508, the Redeemer of Andrea Mantegna (1493), two paintings attributed to Correggio, nine Flemish tapestries of the sixteenth century, coins of the Mint of Correggio and finds of the territory. Free admission; open Saturday afternoon, Sunday and holidays, on other days by reservation; closed in August.
The restored house where the writer lived during the confinity in the 1930s, today multimedia museum.
The noon cannon shot.
Sondrio's civic heart.
Small town centre at 1725 meters at the end of the Rhêmes Valley, in the Gran Paradiso National Park, at the foot of the Parey Grant.
The park opened in 1998 from Niki de Saint Phalle to Garavicchio: 22 monumental sculptures 12-15 meters high covered with mirrors, Murano glass and ceramics, with the ticket office of Mario Botta.
Naturalistic oasis behind the coast of Su Giudeu, habitats of numerous animal species, even rare.
You can visit them with a single ticket; the mosaic floor of the Südhalle, from the IV-V century, is protected by a special structure.

A small modern museum dedicated to the extraction of porphyry, the resistant stone used in urban furnishings: with multimedia tools and an interactive itinerary, it tells the geology of the territory, the ancient history of porphyry and the socio-economic context of quarries. Visits only by reservation (tel. 0461 689799); for singles and small groups every first Friday of the month, I meet at 13:45.

Almost 28 hectares on the first hills outside Porta San Mamolo: meadows, woods, orchards and one of the most beautiful viewpoints on the city. From here start the CAI 904 trail towards Ronzano and Gaibola.

Alpago mountain municipality at 922 meters, at the foot of Monte Cavallo and surrounded by the Cansiglio Forest, ancient dominion of the Serenissima: on the Pian del Cansiglio you will find the Regional Museum of Man, the naturalistic museum of the Forest Carabinieri, the Alpine Botanical Garden and the karst abyss of the Bus de la Lum.

A small town on the Piedmontese shore of Lake Maggiore, mentioned already in 998 and made famous by the Sempione railway: from here you reach the Borromee Islands with the palaces of Isola Bella and Isola Madre, while in the village there are the Villa Ducale di Rosmini, the park of Villa Pallavicino and, behind, the Mottarone.
Prince's hill.

The square in front of the basilica, closed to the north-east by the Apostolic Palace, houses in the center the Fontana Maggiore, a Baroque masterpiece by Carlo Maderno and Giovanni Fontana, and on the churchyard the monument to Pope Sixtus V. Here work the Madonnas, who reproduce famous religious paintings in chalk.

In the historic centre, it has origins around 1300 and Romanesque plant; it was attacked by the troops of Dragut in 1553 and an epigraph recalls the restoration of 1830 wanted by Leopold II. Inside, 19th century statues in plaster and a canvas of the Madonna del Carmine.
Park with fountains where you can taste the waters of Sangemini and Fabia, two springs fed by the slopes of Monte Torre Maggiore and rich in mineral salts; the historical source dates back to 1889.
Completed in 1590, it is the oldest building in Piazza Sant'Oronzo after the amphitheatre.
The road to the sea.

Romantic complex nestled in a well-kept park, around which the village develops: the north side retains the medieval defensive system, while the southern facade has the most refined appearance of a 18th century country villa.
The 10th century fortress, home to the University of Bologna residential centre, with a panoramic terrace to the sea and the Interreligious Museum on Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
To understand the ancient Teramo before visiting its remains.
An easy walk between parish churches and views of the Visone valley.
Church of the 14th century with the octagonal mausoleum that houses the Ventimiglia tombs; the organ of 1547 is indicated as one of the three oldest reed organs in Italy with the original mechanisms.
Enter the house of a family of the nineteenth century.
Medieval streets under the castle.
A historic house to visit.
A thousand years of peasant life around the chestnut tree.
Crafts of wood and village life in a huge museum.
Next to San Francesco al Prato, with the façade carved by Agostino di Duccio between 1457 and 1461.
A nineteenth century noble salon intact.
The crypt of the patron with frescoes from the 12th century.
Tombs of the Punic necropolis re-used for a long time as homes by the poorest families.
Middle Ages of ridge.
The medieval castle became an 18th century villa.

Villa Valdina, built in the 18th century, is built around a 16th century tower and houses works of the Novelli. At the beginning of the course is the holiday villa in Art Nouveau style by Ernesto Basile.

Heart of the village, surrounded by buildings and patronal houses of the Seven and Nineteenth Century, with the monumental eighteenth-century octagonal fountain in red stone called "Dama delle fonte" (Dama of the sources).
Stilts told.
The most sumptuous noble palace.

The Museo del Lavoro Contadino was founded in 1982 on the initiative of the Municipality with the Institute of History of the University of Urbino: on the ground floor of the castle, sections on the production of wheat, the farmhouse and crafts. On the first floor the museum of earth sciences, born from the donation of prof. Renzo Pieruccini, exhibits about 4,000 pieces on Earth, minerals and rocks.
Chestnuts, egg pasta and Lepini truffles.
Under the church, a thousand years of overlapping history.
Garibaldi relics in the ancient house of veterans.

Founded by the Cistercians in 1135 in the Saluzzo plain a few steps from the Po, it is one of the most important medieval monasteries of Piedmont; in 1690 the battle of Staffarda was fought. Owned by the Foundation Ordine Mauriziano.
€8 full, €6 reduced; free on Wednesdays under 26 years
The red façade on the square.
On the river Evançon at the entrance of the valley of Chasten, restored; it ground cereals and produced walnut oil.
On the coast, the Spanish tower of 1572, the largest in Sardinia, which gives its name to the hamlet.

In the nineteenth-century mill complex of the Mulino Nuovo, cultural space since 1996: the ethnographic museum in the silos recreates environments and work of the late nineteenth century, with a space for temporary exhibitions.

Remains of a Roman villa of Augustine age (late 1st century BC-early 1st century AD) of about two hectares at the end of the peninsula: the name was born from the travellers of the 15th century who exchanged the ruins covered with vegetation for caves, but the villa was built after the death of Catullo. You can see the "Botteghe" , the Great Cryptoporic , the Hall of Giants , the large cistern and the thermal sector , in an olive grove of about 1,500 plants. The museum, opened in 1999, exhibits frescoes, stuccoes and mosaics of the villa and Lombard finds of the monastery of San Salvatore, including a pluteo with dedication to Desire and Adelchi. Times indicated by the MiC: Tuesday-Saturday 8.30-17, Sunday 8.30-14, Monday closed; cumulative valid 7 days with Castle and Villa Romana of Desenzano.

Borgo della Ciociaria at the confluence of Liri and Sacco, the seventh stage of the Via Francigena del Sud, known as the City of Argil for the skull of Homo erectus about 800,000 years ago found in 1994. It preserves the remains of the Roman colony of Fregellae in the Museum         . Amedeo Maiuri , the bridge over the Liri of the meeting between Innocent IV and Manfredi (1254) and the Collegiate Church of Santa Maria Maggiore.

Roman colony founded in 184 B.C. south of the present town: the excavations have highlighted the porticoes of the hole with the tabernacles, a temple on high podium and a domus patricia with mosaic floors and frescoed walls.

Natural gorge excavated by the Pioverna stream (according to the sources about 15 million years ago, with the competition of the Adda glacier), with large pots and caves, open on suspended bridges and walkways. At the entrance stands the Cà del Diavol, pentagonal tower with a fresco of the devil, linked to legends of satanic rites, which houses a multimedia exhibition. It is reached from the staircase to the right of the church of Saints Nazarus and Celsus; indicated times: every day 11-13 and 15-19.

From the Piazza delle Aquile, with the tombstone surmounted by three eagles for the privileges of Philip IV of Spain, you can see Capo Milazzo and the Aeolian Islands. Via Moschita preserves portals and wrought iron grates of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries and the arch of the ancient synagogue; in Piazza Pertini the Palazzo Peculio (municipio) and the Monte di Pietà seventeenth century; the Porta Raineri, to the north, was rebuilt at the beginning of the nineteenth century.
The 17th-century parish of the village, cited by the municipality among its characteristic places.
Tyrolean Baroque and Gothic frescoes in the town square.

Medieval village in the extreme north of Lazio, the first Lazio village on the Via Francigena for those coming from Tuscany, dominated by the castle of the twelfth century with views of Lazio, Umbria and Tuscany; in the square the sixteenth century Palazzo Sforza, home of the museum of peasant civilization.
Casola is one of the gateways to the regional park, part of the UNESCO site on karst.
The dome of the Tosca.
Church built in 1600, with annex a large college building.
€4.50, reduced €4/€2.50, family €9

Established in 1991, almost 15,000 hectares of sea in front of the headlands of Capo Colonna, Capo Cimiti, Capo Rizzuto and Le Castella, with low and sandy beaches and few rocky stretches; in the backdrops groupers, mullet, chestnuts and parrot fishes. Only guided and regulated tours are allowed in Capo Colonna and Capo Cimiti.
Literary walk between alleys and lake.
A tower with a legend.
Palace of 1875 in Piazza del Popolo with residence, distillery and shop with liberty friezes; the distillery produces the mistrà, dry distillate of anise and fennel.
Bathrooms and birdwatching on the lake.

Border village between the Kingdom of Naples and the Papal State, on a rock of travertine dominated by the sixteenth-century fortress of Philip II, the last Bourbon bulwark fallen on March 20, 1861; in the village the Ruetta, medieval churches and the sanctuary of Santa Maria dei Lumi.
The largest church in the city, with the apse and the chapel of the bell tower frescoed by the Rimini school of the fourteenth century, rediscovered after the earthquake of 1916.

Village of a few hundred inhabitants in the Natural Reserve of the Mincio Valleys, born around an ancient fishing community and the square of the Sanctuary: between the late eighteenth and early nineteenth century the district had about twenty houses. The entire village can be visited freely as an urban museum.In Ferragosto there are the ancient fair and, since 1973, the National Meeting of the Madonnas on the churchyard.
The place to taste Bologna, lunch or aperitif.
The convent of libraries.
A castle overlooking the valley above the Temple.
The exhibits of Bithia, a stone's throw from the site.

On the Vomero from 1325, a baroque jewel with the Cuciniello nativity scene of 800 pieces, the Carrozza degli Eletti, 950 paintings of the nineteenth century and the Cloister Grande with marble skulls.
You visit freely outside of the functions
Museum of contemporary painting with Italian artists and temporary exhibitions.
The castle on the hill.
Raffaellino del Colle in the Lombard parish.
Portals, cloister and frescoes of a medieval abbey.

Town of the high Volturno Valley overlooking the lake of the same name and the Mainarde, born from the union in 1928 of the villages of Castellone and San Vincenzo. The Benedictine abbey of San Vincenzo al Volturno rises on its territory, with the archaeological area and the Epifanio Crypt.
The tower on the Valais street.

Medieval village with a fifteenth-century castle and, in its territory, Metaponto: the Greek colony founded in the 7th century BC with the temple of Hera of the Palatine Tables, the archaeological park and the national museum.
The assembly line of the Ford T and 19th century cars.
The rooms and caves of the Caetani dukes.
The relics of the sanctuary.
The square with the town hall and the parish church, overlooking the Gran Sasso massif.

The center is divided into eight historic districts; the ruins of the former Franciscan monastery of 1638 stand out, with the church of Our Lady of the Sacred Heart, celebrated in May. A map of Insula Sardinia from 1550 already bears the name of the country.
It preserves the monumental crucifix of the year 1000.
Trastevere's heart.
Public gardens indicated by the Region among the places to see.
The panoramic hill with the Fontanone, among the terraces with the most beautiful view of Rome together with the Garden of the Oranges.
Private collection of about two thousand objects, gathered by Pierangelo Boccalari, on agricultural work, the crafts and domestic life of Lomellina.
The poet's house.
You can see the amphitheatre from inside the museum.
Museum in the open air along the path n. 5 of the Marmore Waterfall, with the equipment of the former hydroelectric power stations.
The seaside resort between the sea and Apuane, with establishments, free beaches and pine forests; a coastal avenue connects it to Viareggio and a bike path to Forte dei Marmi.
Hiking trails among the largest pine forest in the Italian Alps, streams, peat bogs and the Gran Lago, one of the largest natural basins in the region.
Founded in 1027, Romanesque with subsequent Gothic and Baroque transformations and Romanesque bell tower over 50 meters high.
Fresh in the summer.
The modern shrine of the city.

Hermitage in the valley of Acquarella, above Albacina, among the woods of Mount San Vicino: inhabited by hermits from the thirteenth century, it has a church of 1441 wanted by the hermit Frandeno, leaning on a tower that controlled the valley of the Esino. In April 1529 it was held the first chapter of the Capuchins, which redacted the constitutions of Albacina, abandoned in 1585, was restored in 1845. You can reach it with a suggestive path in the woods; the festival is May 3.
The green around the parish church.
National monument of the X-XI and XVII centuries.

Borgo della piania bergamasca, 26 km from Bergamo, known for the Sanctuary of Santa Maria del Fonte, was built where in 1432 Our Lady appeared to a woman of the people and half of more than two million pilgrims a year; in the village the Gothic church of Saints Fermo and Rustic, the monastery of San Bernardino with the Passion cycle of Fermo Stella and Palazzo Gallavresi with the Pinacoteca civica.

The gallery of the Academy of Fine Arts, born from the collection of the ancient Institute officialized in 1895 and re-arranged recently, with works from the seventeenth to the thirteenth century and the strong imprint of the nineteenth-century Neapolitan.
Small baths in the Mediterranean maquis with hot water rich in sulphates and calcium, with limited number of guests.
The Madonna in stone of the thirteenth century.
Church that tradition dates back to the 9th century, with frescoes of the 14th-XV century brought to light recently.
One of the narrowest alleys in Italy, a few tens of centimeters wide.

The central square brings together the late Baroque parish church, the Loggia theatre and the town hall; the Brandolini buildings are recognized by the red darks all the same, and the seventeenth-century Marian Houses host the exhibition of the Craftsmanship in August.
In Cardeto Park, it conserves 178 tombstones from the 15th to the 19th century facing Jerusalem; the land was granted by the Senate in 1428.

Built between 1885 and 1894 on the hill to the south-east of the basin, on the ruins of the Château du Bramafam, it was the most important fortification of the Cozie Alps; restored since 1995 by the Association for Studies of History and Military Architecture, it houses on more than 4.000 m2 the museum of the Royal Army with reconstructions of environment from 1890 to 1945, uniforms, photographs, diaries and letters. Seasonal opening.
Fermo's living room.
To be combined with San Jacopo to see father and son Pisano a few kilometers.
The ceiling frescoed by Canal.
Prehistoric engravings at high altitude.
A monumental tree above the city.
Giulio Romano and the tomb of Matilde.
Underwater archaeology in front of the coast.
A town buried by Vesuvius.
Collection of Assyrian, Egyptian, Cypriot, Phoenician, Etruscan and Greek-Roman sculptures in the Little Farnesina.
The wooden sculptures of the roof.
The mosaics of the cathedral.

Irpino village dominated by the Marchionale Castle, probably of Lombard origin and rebuilt by the Normans, with next to the Baroque Collegiate of San Marciano; in the municipal palace the Archaeological Museum exhibits the eneolithic finds of the excavations of San Martino district.
damaged by the earthquake, ongoing restoration; Umbriatourism indicates it at the moment not to be visited, information at the Tourist Office Valnerina-Cascia
The Etruscan tombs in the valley.
The heart of the village, between fountain, tower and viewpoint.
A villa of Renaissance delight with frescoed rooms and terrace garden.

The village, documented as early as 797 as "Veterale" is known for its Gothic houses; in the main square the church of San Nicola di Bari with the bell tower of 1754. The patron saint is celebrated on the first Sunday of August and 6 December.
The villa near the Round with a wonderful cycle of frescoes by Giambattista and Giandomenico Tiepolo.
Octagonal Gothic Baptistery started in 1301, covered with white and green marbles, with the source signed by Lanfranco da Como in 1226.
To be checked: tastings in shops
The forced picture on the sea.
History and land art on a hill.
For centuries the seat of the city's government, renewed in neoclassical forms by Giuseppe Piermarini, today the main space of the great exhibitions of the City next to the Duomo.
The headroom.

The village of Barbagia di Belvì is about 700 meters on the slopes of Gennargentu, founded in the fifteenth century, with the ancient area paved in red and black stone: a few kilometers away the copper mine of Funtana Raminosa, today the museum of the Geominerario Park, and the plateau of Corongia with the rocks of Is Breccas on the valley of Flumendosa.

Municipal Museum dedicated to Cardinal Giulio Raimondo Mazzarino, Prime Minister of France, born in Pescina on July 14, 1602 and died in France in 1661: documents on his life, reading room, specialized library on Abruzzo and space for contemporary art exhibitions, in a building of 1971-72. Open Tuesday and Thursday 10.30-19, Saturday and Sunday 10.30-12.

The only remaining part of the Romanesque cathedral, under the presbytery: a 12th-century crypt, rediscovered by chance in 1928, with a cruising vault on sixteen stone columns and medieval and Roman capitals of reuse. It contains frescoes of Byzantine style, three wooden sculptures of the Two-Three Century, Roman epigraphs that evoke a temple of Diana and the funerary stone of Gnesio, priest of the goddess.
In restoration, waiting to reopen; the archive consults by appointment
One day a year private villas open the gates.

Also known as Torre di Michelangelo and indicated by the Municipality as a symbol of Ischia, it rises in front of the Aragonese Castle on a large green lawn, a few meters from the Scogli di Sant'Anna.
It is the symbolic image of the village, unique in its kind.

In Castelmartini, the Garden of Memory, designed by the artist Andrea Dami for the victims of the massacre of the Padule di Fucecchio in August 1944, with the work "Paysage" of 175 plasticized iron signs, one per victim, and "My brother is here" by Simone Fagioli; near the monument "Lo Stupore" by the master Gino Terri, inaugurated by President Ciampi.
The Duomo designed by Ippolito Scalza at the end of the sixteenth century, with three naves, with works by Taddeo di Bartolo, Michelozzo and Andrea della Robbia.
A Ladin mill still running.
Garden with plants typical of the Mediterranean maquis, overlooking the sea, surrounding the City Palace.
One of the most intact medieval fortified complexes in the world.

On the square the Palazzo del Monte di Pietà (XVIII century), the eighteenth-century church of Santa Croce and the monument to the Fallen of Aldo Roncaglia; the 17th-century Clock Tower collapsed in the 2012 earthquake. The parish church of San Felice, fifteenth century with neoclassical façade, preserves a wooden crucifix of the sixteenth century, a terracotta bust of the Christ died of the fifteenth century and a altarpiece of Bernardino Loschi (1500).
Secular chestnuts and menhirs where the stele statues have re-emerged.

In the forge of San Bartolomeo, the center of the Museum of Industry and Work: the hammer put back into operation, a hydraulic wheel and the entire system of exploitation of the energy of the water visible outside, with the plastic of the neighborhood.
The river of Valnerina between rafting and nature.
The clay section of the cyclovia along the bank.
The water sawmill restarted.
Ice waterfalls at the end of the valley, after the museum.
Taste the region in a room.

Gothic-Catalan church of the late fifteenth century with trachyte façade; inside two wooden altars of local woodcarvers, a sixteenth-century statue of the Madonna with Child and silver of the sixteenth century. In mid-November it hosts the feast of the patron.
Visit by reservation, with shifts of about half an hour.

A town of about 27,000 inhabitants on three hills 375 meters, less than 40 km from Bari, known for the Carnival as the oldest in Europe. The old town, a maze of alleys and squares, gathers around Piazza Plebiscito with the Palazzo del Balì and the Seat; in the countryside the Grotta del Trullo, karst cavity with stalactites and stalagmites of alabaster.

It collects traditional work tools, the reconstruction of an ancient kitchen and the façade of a house; among the objects the portal of the parish, lace tombolo and traditional costumes. Open on request.

Municipality of Varesotto developed around the eighteenth-century Villa Molino, now the town hall, on the top of the hill; in the territory the rural village of Caidate and the small church of Sant'Eurosia, both between the Places of the Heart of the FAI.
The ancient springs of the village, including Fonte Maxima, Fonte Filello and Fonte Sabbalone, with a wash basin, tanks and a path that enters the hill.
The legendary walls of the city of Epeo.

Built in 1914 in the form of a Hellenistic temple designed by Luigi Milani, in the pine forest of the Poggetto: furnishings of over 300 Etruscan and Roman tombs of the promontory (end IV - beginning I century BC), with the urn in alabaster of the II century BC that contained the ashes of the Etruscan noblewoman Velia Cerinei.

Masterpiece of the Sicilian Baroque designed by Rosario Gagliardi in 1738 and completed in 1775, on top of a staircase: three-order facade and a neoclassical dome of 43 meters; next to the Duomo Museum with fragments of the church destroyed by the earthquake of 1693.
€5, reduced €2 (18-25 years EU), free under 18
Founded in December 1989 and run at the beginning by the local WWF section, since 1995 it has been entrusted to the Environmental Education Centre.
In the fifteenth century the Aragonese Tower was incorporated into the church for defensive purposes; in the Marian month of May a torchlight runs along the slopes of the San Casto hill.

The cultivation of lemons in Gargnano dates back to the 13th century. Some lemonias are open to the public: La Malora, the oldest one, which today produces liqueurs, gelatins and mustards, the Lemonaia Trevisani and Gandossi.

Digged in the last decades of the nineteenth century and named after a director of the French company of Malfidano, there ran a steam locomotive that brought the mineral to the laverie and the port. Today you will walk on an electric train along the old track and on the return on foot in the pedestrian tunnel of the mules, with dark stretches illuminated by large windows on the sea, up to a viewpoint at about 50 m altitude; guided tours.

The fourteenth-century limestone fountain, symbol of the village and present in the coat of arms, has a circular tub divided by three-pointed arches and a central column with vegetal and human figures and masks with the face of a lion. Next to it, a votive newsstand preserves a fresco of the 15th century Madonna with Child (Madonna dell'Uccellino) with bright colors, then the communal oven where the families cooked bread and another fountain used to water the animals; from the medieval door on the south side of the square you enter the fortified village.
the MiC tab indicates closed every day, check the times (tel. 0421 324440)
Ancient parish church mentioned in a document dated 1141, with a hut facade and a sail bell tower.
The fortress on the hill.

Botanical garden and shelter at 1300 m, built in 1900 in memory of the doctor Pietro Edoardo Rostan; devastated during the war, the shelter was rebuilt since 1966 by the Association Friends of Rostany. From Rue to Sangle and Pragiassaut, you can walk, drive or mountain bike.

Country of the Lombard shore of Lake Maggiore, whose name derives from the Celtic "leze dunum" at the foot of the hill, on a cliff above the lake stands the Hermitage of Santa Caterina del Sasso, while in the village remain the ancient churches of the Saints Primo and Feliciano and Santo Stefano, home of parishes at least from 846.

The small well-preserved old town is located on a hill about 124 meters high, with public buildings and noble villas built from the seventeenth century onwards. On Piazza del Popolo there is the parish church of San Donato Martire, rebuilt after the bombings of the Second World War, with a Latin cross with neo-Romanic façade and rose window, the noble buildings Contini and Mayer and the Fontana delle Cinque Cannelle.
The fortress on the Darsena Vecchia, built on the Mastio di Matilde and on the Quadratura dei Pisani, guarding the Medici port.
Baroque church of the mid-17th century, completely frescoed.
The medieval center between portals and alleys.
Frederick Stibbert's museum house with one of the largest collections of weapons and armor in the world, from samurai to knights.
submerged and not visitable on foot; it is seen with guided tours by boat of the Museo Civico Archeologico della Valtenesi, by reservation
A stop along the Santerno valley.
The church on the valley.
The church with the relics of St. Walfredo, the starting point of the "wrinkles," the maze of alleys of the village.
On the slopes of Vesuvius, with a wide view.
Started around 1470 and consecrated in 1621, it preserves a sixteenth-century altarpiece by the painter Pietro De Marascalchi.
The tour of the walls of the fortified village.
The village is known for the medieval castle of the thirteenth century, with imposing walls and the church of Santa Caterina; the area is known for the State Reserve Mountain of Torricchio.
One ticket to five institutions and the Farnese Theatre.
Impressive fortification on the promontory of Punta Penna, built to defend the city from raids from the sea.

Housed since 1911 in Palazzo Baronale Orsini, with original arrangement of Angelo Pasqui expanded in 1993, it preserves the finds of the Villa of Orazio: Corinthian capitals, marble slabs engraved, a gap with acantum leaves, frogs and crabs, part of a male statue, lead fistulas, lights, coins, ceramics, everyday objects and fragments of frescoes, stuccoes and mosaics.
It is the house of origin of the saint, lived according to the source between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, which every year recalls faithful from all over the world.
Easy and panoramic paths.
Water springs and canoe a stone's throw from the village.
A medieval house-tower inhabited until recent times, open to the public with the furnishings of the family: you can understand how you lived inside a tower.
From the ditch you can see, along the Burano Gorge, the ancient and new path of the Via Flaminia.
18th century frescoes and walk in the green.
The sanctuary of the apparition and its secular tree.
The crypt of the dukes.
Thermal cave with neoclassical plant.

Itinerary that connects Ancona and Osimo passing through Numana, Sirolo, Camerano, Offagna and Castelfidardo; about twenty wineries produce Rosso Conero DOC and Rosso Conero Riserva DOCG from Montepulciano and Sangiovese grapes.

Reserve of 2,049 hectares established in 2000 between Cammarata, San Giovanni Gemini and Santo Stefano Quisquina: includes Monte Cammarata (1.578 m), highest peak of the Sicani Mountains, with Monte Gemini, Pizzo Rondine and Serra della Coin, natural woods of holm oak and roverella and reforestation pine trees.
Walk under the Roman city.
16th century buildings that testify to the past importance of the municipality.
The heart of the historic center on which the districts of Lanciano Vecchia, Civitanova, Sacca and Borgo open.

Nisseno village at 590 meters at the foot of Monte San Paolino, from which you can see 25 villages, the sea of Agrigento, the Madonie and Etna; to visit the Arabic quarter of the Rabato with the houses in plaster, the churches of Sant'Agata, Carmelo and Assunta, the shrine at the top reached by 183 steps and the museum in the former convent of Carmine.
the MiC card reports every day as closed and no time: tel. 0985 72353
End sand for families.
The daily life of those who lived in caves and fields.
Bruschetta with Sabina oil.

Paintings, oil sketches, portraits, studies, cartoons and drawings donated to the Municipality by the neoclassicalist painter Michele De Napoli (1808-1892), author of the design of the triumphal chariot of the Madonna di Sovereto; complete the collection of architectural fragments of the Seven-nineteenth century and a carriage of the late eighteenth century restored.

It takes its name from the ancient diocese of Valva and it was built on the site of the martyrdom of San Pelino, where a early Christian cemetery developed. It combines the Oratory of St. Alexander, rectangular hall with apse which was the transept of a consecrated church in 1092 and remained unfinished, and the basilica completed in 1235, with three naves with raised transept; the central apse is scanned outside by four decorative bands with columns, sculpted slabs and windows.

Buildings of five-sixth-century origin rebuilt after the earthquake of 1783 and enriched by statues of Serresi artists: the parish church of St. Nicholas (of 1600 according to the Municipality), the church of the Rosary (nineteenth century) and the church of Carmine.

On the day of the Ascension the procession crosses the streets decorated with carpets of flowers and leaves, an ancient tradition; in July the Festival of the Chianina Steak and the Festival of wine of the Valley of the Calanchi on the Teverina Wine Road, in autumn the Dinners in the Cellars.
Church already mentioned in 1289, with valuable paintings.

The marina, animated by bars and restaurants, is the heart of the medieval village; there is moored the Siora Veronica, sailboat of 1926 with which you can still sail on Garda. In the squares and in the castle theater folk and cultural events are held in summer.
Church of fourteenth-century origin with three naves, each with its own altar; from the churchyard, on a terrace at the edge of the village, opens the view of the valley and Lake of Idro.
The panoramic view over the village.
The contemporary art of a daughter of Darfo.
The ducal garden beyond the Parma stream, designed in the 18th century in French, with the Doge's Palace, the fish pond and tree-lined avenues.
The College founded by Pope Clement XI at the beginning of the eighteenth century houses the hall of the City Council, offices and the Museum of the Cabinet of Physics.
The landscape of tuff shaped by the erosion on which Civita faces, which has made it its strength.
Neo-Gothic nineteenth century with rosette.

Of the castle, destroyed in the first half of the seventeenth century during the war between Savoy and Spanish for the succession of Monferrato, only the rebuilt tower remains; on the ruins rose the church of St. Peter, demolished in 1770. A plaque recalls the castle and Bianca Lancia di Agliano, mother of Manfredi king of Naples and Sicily cited by Dante in the third song of Purgatory, and a recent painting depicts it on one side. From the top you can see the hills, the roofs of the village and, on clear days, the Alps with the Monviso. For access the page refer to the Municipality (tel. 0141 954023).
The Grandes Jorasses.
Birthplace of the missionary from Limona, founder of the Comboni Missionaries, with materials on his life and his connection with the country.
A century of Italian advertising in lithographed tin.
The treasures of the Flegrei Fields with a view of the Gulf.
A 13th century shrine that preserves the body of the Benedictine nun who died in Cingoli in 1276, with paintings by Pier Simone Fanelli and Antonio da Faenza.
Reservation required by email, maximum 30 visitors per time slot
Six-seventh-century sacred art in the village church.
The living room of the village, starting point of all paths.
Modern art in Turin.
Birdwatching and walks around the lake.
In progress of re-establishment: check the visits on the site of the National Roman Museum

About 22 hectares behind the modern city with the remains of the Etruscan-Campano town, explored only in part; the excavations of the Universities of Salerno and Molise have exposed an entire block of the Roman colony of Picentia, with the decuman and construction phases until late antiquity. It houses an Environmental Education Centre, an outdoor library and urban gardens treated with Legambiente.

Relaxing walk in the woods accompanied by the Rabbies stream, which descends from the Rabbi Valley and flows into the Walnut: from Malé you go up to the locality Brewery, on the road to the Rabbi Valley, and you go back through Pondasio and the Marinelli Fucina.
The peasant life of the Canavese.
The three surroundings and the valley of the Tiber.
Objects and memories of a country of Irpinia.

It is mentioned already in the list of the cathedral of Turin of 1336, it has two Romanesque portals in green stone of Brossasco (the largest on the side), a single nave with bundles of columns similar to those of the parish church of Sampeyre and a bell tower renovated of Gothic structure; on the square a stone cross.

Lake of karst origin in the heart of the Ernici Mountains, born from the progressive closure of two of the three swallows; about 1.7 km long and 700 m wide, is regional natural reserve of 1,824 hectares between Ferentino, Fiuggi, Fumone and Trivigliano. On the banks of herons, smooth and small, wide ducks and flares; towards Fumone there are chestnut woods. You can walk or bike on a cycle track, free and always open access.
Local art and the secrets of the Fanzago clock.

Montiferru country dominated by the basilica of Santa Maria della Neve, the first minor basilica of Sardinia, with the ruins of the castle of Casteddu Ezzu; on the coast the villages of Santa Caterina di Pittinuri, S'Archittu and Torre del Pozzo, the Punic and early Christian city of Cornus and the waterfalls at the sea of Capo Nieddu.
The high town.
Sides in the plane
Stone records.

Behind Dongo is the Albano Valley, already in ancient way towards northern Europe through the Passo di San Jorio (2014 m), towards the Val Mesolcina. It crosses the Via dei Monti Lariani, which runs for 46 km from the Albano Valley to Sorico for the Valle di San Jorio and the Valle del Dosso, touching ancient nuclei once used as alpine pastures.
One of the most beautiful Renaissance facades in Umbria.
Norman architecture survived the earthquake.
It houses a crucifix in cedar wood, Byzantine sculpture of the 13th-14th century.
A pilgrimage to the Holy Land in the Tuscan woods.
The most famous villa in the world.
The 18th-century parish church.

City on the hill Sabulo between the Sibillini and the Adriatic: the Renaissance Piazza del Popolo with the Palazzo dei Priori and the Sala del Mappamondo, the underground Roman cisterns and the Cathedral on the Girfalco, a few kilometers from the beaches.
A noble residence with hanging garden designed by Accornero.
16th century shrine in white stone with octagonal plan, similar in style to the sanctuary of Macereto, at the crossroads for Montecavallo.
Overlooking Piazza Garibaldi, it dates back to the 17th century and is an example of Tuscan baroque; it preserves a stele dedicated to the fallen of the two world wars.

Patronal church on the main square, completed in 1512 according to the regional portal and today in neoclassical forms; it preserves a canvas of Luigi Fontana and the statues of the patron saints of the trades.
Inside the shop of gold and ruby lusters.

Ancient fishing valley in the easternmost part of the lagoon, an area of international value for birdwatching, reachable from Grado by bike: four routes (Five Woods, Visitor Center, Sea, Valley), interactive tour center, bike and binocular rental; the Pagoda and the Sabbia observatory are free access.
A frescoed 15th century and a view over three valleys.

On the noble floor of Palazzo Marcelli, more than 200 vintage and modern phones in chronological order, collected since 1956 worldwide by the collector and restorer Giuseppe Renzini and almost all still functioning. Among the pieces a Meucci receiver dated 1871, experimental wooden and metal devices found in Florence at the end of the nineteenth century and the rare ............

Built around the year 1000 on a more ancient rock fortress and partly dug into the sandstone, it has drawbridge and panoramic tower reached by steep stairs cut into the rock. In 1282, during the Vespers, the French garrison resisted a siege for a year: it is reminiscent of a sixteenth-century inscription on the arch of the entrance hall; inside twelve small circular niches dug into the wall and, in the castle, you can see the weaving of the frazzed.

Building inaugurated in 1871 as a shooting range, today visitor center of the Rio Bianco Nature Area of the Adamello Brenta Nature Park, with an exhibition on the flora of the park; next there is the botanical garden with an illustrative path on the vegetation. Medieval village on the Gulf of Follonica, dominated by the Pisan Fortress: the treasure of Scarlino at the documentation centre Francovich, the museum of the ancient Roman port at the Puntone, the Etruscan tombs of Poggio Tondo and the coves of the Bandite reserve, including Cala Violina.

It was created in 1923-1924, and was the first major public commission of Arturo Martini, who won the City's competition in front of a jury with Leonardo Bistolfi and Eugenio Baroni. It combines a four-figure pyramid in bronze, The War, The Victory, History and The Sacrifice (Pastor Fido), whose casts are in Villa Groppallo.

Private collection of ancient corking machines, dated between 1600 and 1950 (over 200 according to the MiC, almost 300 according to Emilia-Romagna Turismo), with tools and objects related to the bottling of wine.
From the 13th century, it welcomed pilgrims on foot to Loreto or Rome; restored in 1456-57 with the addition of the loggia, it preserves the Romanesque façade and some porticoes.
The baroque palace which houses the museum dedicated to the judges of Arborea.
The central square with the Town Hall with its porch façade, Palazzo Ghilini baroque Prefecture and Province headquarters and the Palazzo delle Poste with the mosaic by Gino Severini (1940-41).
A table of Barnabas from Modena and a Roman mausoleum.
To the right of the entrance of the small cemetery of Poggiana rests prof. First Visentin, commander of the Partisan Brigade Martyrs of Grappa, gold medal in military valor.

Oval relief surrounded by ditches still about five meters deep, the village's "cortina" conquered and sacked in 1309 by Enrico di Prampero di Cuccagna; there is the church of Santo Stefano, whose portal of 1515 has a bas-relief of Giovanni Antonio Pilacorte in the bezel. Several times struck by lightning in the seventeenth century, it was consecrated in 1700 with the new bell tower; a fire in 1971 destroyed the frescoes of the presbytery of Aurelio Mariani.

Venetian hydraulic sawmill built in 1872 by Crisanto Orsingher and active until 1954, with drawer wheel and long vertical blade: it sawed about 3,000 cubic meters a year of timber from the Redòs and Valzanca valleys. Disassembled after the closure, it was rebuilt in the late 1990s by the Paneveggio Park with the whole hydraulic machine. In the summer demonstrations on Sunday 14:30-17.

About 1,700 of the 4,200 hectares of the plateau fall in the territory of Genoni: endemic corks, holm oaks, roverelle, arbutes and myrtle, with paulis, seasonal water mirrors, and over 600 wild horses. The park has about 25 km of marked trails.

The Palazzo dei Priori was built between 1763 and 1770 on the previous medieval palace; the Neoclassical Collegiate preserves a Callido organ of the eighteenth century. The tour is completed by the Torrione, Porta de Moscé and Porta della Sala, the church of Sant'Agostino, now auditorium, and the monument to the fallen made in 1955 by the sculptor Cantalamessa.
A nine-century bridge.
On a rocky promontory at 956 meters above the village, mentioned in documents since 1598; there lived the "Romèt" - a hermit who watched the fires and sounded the alarm bell.

Regional reserve of about 1,200 hectares, Natura 2000 area, with one of the last slices of coastal forest flooded the peninsula: riparian forest, maquis, wetlands and dunes near the sea, over 170 species of birds, otter and nests of sea turtles. The WWF oasis (21 hectares) has a fauna recovery center; guided tours by reservation.
Tower built by the Aragonese between the 15th and 16th centuries for defense and used in the Sabauda era as a prison.
On the central square, until 1860 part of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie: three naves, baroque frescoes and marble altars of Carrara.
Dunes and clear water on the Ionian.
The Post Office and Telegraphs of the twentieth century on the short side of Piazza Saffi, an example of the architecture of the fascist period in the city.
Baroque plasters and carvings with eye on them.
The tower with the Palazzo Pretorio dominates Piazza del Duomo, a symbol of the historic center of the millennia.
A quiet stop between Parma and Reggio.

Borgo dei Castelli Romani overlooking the volcanic lake of Nemi, with the medieval Castle Ruspoli, the viewpoints on the lake and the Sanctuary of the Blessed Crucifix; on the shore stand the Museum of the Roman Navi, built for the ships of Caligola, and the remains of the sanctuary of Diana Nemorense.
At the centre of the large complex founded in 1742 by Saint Alphonsus Maria de' Liguori, with the redemptorist religious house and the basilica dedicated to the saint.
The Amatrician in her country.

Built between 1562 and 1594 by the Counts Fantusio and Antonio di Polcenigo Fanna, who left the castle of Mizza for the plain, takes up the patterns of the castle with corner towers, central tower and rustic around portals and windows. It was the seat of the local jurisdiction until the eighteenth century, plundered by Napoleonic troops in 1797; traces of the facade frescoes remain, while the cycle of Antonio Basoli is lost. Restored after the earthquake of 1976, since 2000 it is the seat of the Municipality and the museum.
On 30 and 31 January, for over a thousand years, banks of handicrafts, music and folklore in the center; in August also the Foire d'été.
It houses a 15th century polyptych by the Master of Staffolo.

Two villages in Chianti: Barberino Val d'Elsa, Bandiera Arancione, and San Donato in Poggio, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, with the Badia a Passignano not far away.
Among the oldest places of worship in the area, with frescoes from the fourteenth century at the entrance.

In the former convent of the Silvestrini next to Saint Lucia, reopened on July 29, 2001 after the restorations followed by the earthquake of 1997, it collects about 300 historical maps, atlases and prints that document the historical, geographical and administrative evolution of the Marches; in the third room there is a faithful reproduction of a globe of Vincenzo Coronelli.

Collegiate of the 13th century enlarged in the 15th century with three naves, with Romanesque bell tower with two-fold windows and frescoes of the Umbrian and Byzantine school, including figures of Jesus, St. Rocco, St. Anthony of Padua, St. Anthony Abbot and St. Lucia. A legend places the Holy Grail in it: the initials of the holy paintings would form the word "Grail."
Visits only by reservation, to groups of five
A pilgrimage sanctuary in the valley of the Err.

The forge of the sixteenth century operated by the water of the Roggia di Breganze through a wheel, still working: the hammer called "head of donkey" is the fulcrum of the ethnographic museum, and the last blacksmith was Angelo Giusto Tamiello. The city guide defines it as one of the best preserved in Europe and a rare example of Vicenza protoindustry of the sixteenth century. Visit by appointment; it is the destination of the Trail of Maglio and the route of the ancient opifici.
The ancient Romanesque cathedral on the hill.

The centre of the flat toast with the Basilica of Santa Maria della Vittoria, whose cult dates back to the return of the Sanvitesi from Lepanto in 1571, and in the countryside two frescoed rock churches: the Crypt of San Biagio, with frescoes dating back to 1196, and the Crypt of San Giovanni along the Royal Canal.
He brought electricity to the Gran San Bernardo valley in 1904; today of the municipality, he conserves documents, objects and machinery recovered in the restoration.

The Naviglio Piccolo, built at the end of the fifteenth century with the contribution of Leonardo da Vinci, was born from Adda and crosses Cernusco from east to west; for centuries it was the main economic road in the area. The lifts, protected by the Naviglio Park, are equipped for about two kilometers with greenery, paths and bike path, part of a municipal network of over 70 km of bikes.

Frazione was born in the sixteenth century when the Jesuit fathers of the novitiate of Palermo, called "Parrini" (Parrini) bought land in the northeast of Partinico building a mill, houses for peasants, watchtowers, warehouses and a chapel dedicated to Maria SS. del Rosario; then passed to the Duke of Aumale, who produced the Moscatello dello Zucco. Today, recovered by private individuals, it is a village of artists with white houses with blue doors, murals, mosaic sculptures and majolica from the atmosphere that recalls Gaudí. The visit takes less than an hour, with parking at the entrance.

The medieval Roman Gate is the only surviving of the five gates (Maggiore, Salera, Segnara, Castello, Valle) that in the fifteenth century gave access to the walled village; the Rodari Museum is located in the historic center, reachable with a small ascent.

The border town of Alto Mantovano, from 1440 to 1797 part of the Republic of Venice that transformed it into a fortress; around Piazza XX Settembre the Venetian Loggia of 1610, the fountain of Hercules and the Gothic cathedral with the works of Romanino, and in Palazzo Monte dei Pegni the Civic Museum Bellini and the Parish Museum Tosio.
Sienese painting in Grosseto.
Natural area behind the bay, inhabited by rare and suggestive birds at sunset.

Medieval fortified village at 725 meters in the Comino Valley, at the foot of Mount Meta on the Lazio side of the National Park of Abruzzo, Lazio and Molise, dominated by a castle of 1054; Orange Flag since 2022, linked to the stay of D.H. Lawrence in 1919.

The medieval village is made of winding alleys with several sacred newsstands; in Via Sant'Antonino there is a small stone house with bifora and Palazzo Cesi dates back to about 1500. From the stairway of Via degli Scacchi, beyond the arch of San Lorenzo, you go up to the Rocca that dominates the village: built by the Crescenzi reusing materials of a Roman temple, passed to the Orsini in 1400 and already in 1500 was abandoned.

Art city on the three hills between the Adriatic and the Gran Sasso, dominion of Acquaviva: the cathedral with the great cycle of frescoes by Andrea de Lithium, the ducal palace and, a few minutes away, the Calanchi reserve.

Museum with sections of paleontology, archaeology and didactics: local fossils, including two sandstone blocks covered with sea urchins from the Duidduru geosite, and Nuragic, Punic and Roman finds of the territory. A model reconstructs the hill of Santu Antine with Punic fortifications, nuraghe, well and church, and a diorama shows the bottom of the well with reproductions of the finds; workshop for schools and families with excavation simulation. Paid admission, total motor accessibility.

Parish of the early sixteenth century, in the present eighteenth-century structure then restored and enriched. In the central aisle two frescoes by the Genoese Gerolamo Graffigna (late nineteenth century) with the Madonna delle Grazie and St. James Major, patron saint of the village; the bell tower was rebuilt after the earthquake of 23 February 1887. Consolidated and restored between 1984 and 1987, with the interior frescoes restored by Giovanni Muratorio.
The cathedral in the historic center, mentioned with San Maurizio for its graceful forms.
Five minutes between Palace and Cathedral.
The sanctuary built by the Dominicans between 1641 and 1660, the destination of pilgrims, with the neo-baroque façade of Lamberto Cusani of 1913.

Opened in 1998, it documents the ancient history of the territory and especially the Neolithic site of Sammardenchia, one of the largest in Europe (about 5500-4700 BC), which has returned tools in flint, stone and ceramics. Educational path with settings, copies of artifacts to touch and experimental archaeology workshops for children; a section is dedicated to the local protohistory and castle of Pozzuolo.
Ancient quarry transformed into a Christian church, with frescoes from the 6th century.

Borgo about 40 minutes walk to Mola, known for the remains of the 10th century abbey of the Basilian monks and a quadrangular tower; near the abbey is cultivated the carrot of Polignano, Slow Food garrison. With clubs and restaurants, it is where you move the nightlife.
Baths and diving on an island with curious history.
The Farnese-Anguillara wedding fresco.

Etruscan necropolis excavated in tuff (IX-III century BC), along the Via Sepolcrale that descends into the valley as Via degli Inferi: mounds and graves like those of the Capanna, the Cornice, the Capitelli, the Greek vases and the Reliefs, with 13 niches in painted stucco.

In the Middle Ages the palace was the castle gate and the tower was the house annexed with the accommodation of the guards; the tower appears in the documents in the middle of the thirteenth century, the brick battlements are after the fourteenth century and the last door is dated 1536 (it remains the Gothic arch with its hinges and the key is preserved). A coat of arms on the tower recalls the domination of Perugia; there is also the clock tower of the brothers Gricci.
A millenarian church of the Lombard period in the district of Piagge, built near the site of an ancient Lombard monastery.
The only work signed by Vitruvio.
To understand the tragedy of the Gleno before or after the ascent to the dam.

It preserves the Latin epigraph of the Table of Trinitapoli, bronzes, avori, remains of ritual sacrifices and finds of underwater archaeology. The Superintendence reports at the park an archaeological museum of the Ipogei with finds of more than 30 years of excavations.
Panoramic trails above the Garda.

Common at the foot of Mount Vettore in the National Park of Monti Sibillini, with capital in Balzo, where in the sixteenth century the inhabitants of the ancient castle of Santa Maria in Gallo moved; among the places to see the church of San Bernardino, Santa Maria in Pantano with the Sibille frescoed by Martino Bonfini and Santa Maria in Lapide with the crypt of the IX century.
The Romanesque crypt with the relics of Saint Amato.

Monregalese Valleys with the stations of Prato Nevoso and Artesina in the Mondolè area: at the bottom of the valley the Caudano Caves, discovered in 1898, and the Water Path, in Miroglio the Museum of the Mountain and its People.
The Apuans around the quarries.

Small excavation with the remains of a patrician residence of the first century A.D. of the Roman Hasta, with the rare mosaic carpet of the triclinium with fishes and ivy branches within white and black frames.

Country of the Volsini Mountains near Lake Bolsena, built on a volcanic cone of tuff above the Etruscan city of Civita: the Civita Museum in the Vignola Palace, the necropolis of Pianezze and Centocamere, the Basilica of Maria Santissima del Suffragio with its museum and the church of San Pietro on top of the village.
It has a wooden choir of the fifteenth century, a painting of the sixteenth century and bell tower and dome covered with green and yellow majolica; in front stands the column of San Biagio.

Piazza that preserves the regular sixteenth-century plant: to the north the parish church of Santi Protasio and Gervasio, on the sides two rows of similar houses with porticos, to the west the space of Villa Schiattarini then Conti-Cottafavi and in front of the church the Town Hall, building of the seventeenth century several times modified.

Born in 1258, renovated in Gothic by the Malatesta family, of which remain the bell tower and the Gothic-Venetian portal in Istria stone and red marble of Verona; transformed into late Baroque in the eighteenth century.
Puccini's family home, with his piano.

According to tradition in 1553 the peasant Leonhard Weißensteiner, who fell into a ravine, saw the Virgin appear and built her a chapel, then enlarged; the original chapel is still inside the Baroque building, with the piety of Our Lady of Sorrows, the high altar covered with gold and silver sheets, the frescoes of Adam Mölk's vault and the lateral altars of Pußjäger. On 24 August 1885 the statue was crowned in the presence of 15,000 faithful and in July 1988 Pope John Paul II went up there; outside the chapel of St. Pellegrino Laziosi and along the side entrances numerous ex-vote. Park along the lake at the end of Sirmione, on the border with Peschiera, overlooking Lake Lugana: centuries-old poplars, a beach and wide panorama. It is the starting point of Sirmione's Literary Route; at the Casa del Pescatore an outdoor exhibition on traditional lake fishing.
The Franciscan monastery became a gallery.

It was 143 metres high, from 1,675 m to 1,532 m high, 60 metres wide at the base; Richard Wagner, Gabriele D'Annunzio, Queen Margherita, De Saussure and Stoppani visited it. The path along the coast was part of the ancient merchant route between Milan and Bern, and on the top stands the hotel Decò of 1923 by Piero Portaluppi. From the 1930s the waters feed the central of Ponte, so the waterfall is in full for short periods only; opening from June to September, with the accessible route         Â A waterfall for all Â .

The Catalan Gothic style arch of the late fifteenth century is reached by a sandstone staircase, next to the smallest Augustinicchiu arch, and leads to a square overlooking the Bay of Taormina; Piazza Pasquale Carullo looks on the Strait of Messina and is a point to observe the meteors of August.

Father's house of Amedeo Pietro Giannini, son of Favale's emigrants who, according to legend, left after the earthquake in San Francisco in 1906 with a safe on a cart and founded the Bank of America and Italy. On two floors it preserves original furnishings of the daily life of the nineteenth century, documents, photographs and panels on its life; you can even walk up a mule track. On the last Sunday of June, the country celebrates the "day of the migrant" with the Ligurian communities in the world. Tel. 0185 975195 (Common).

Ancient parish church of the hamlet of Cantogno, today a sanctuary: it preserves a  "Pietà" , fresco of the second half of the fifteenth century partially recovered. The festival is celebrated on the second Sunday of October.
Medieval town on the three hills, historical UNESCO heritage centre since 1995, with the Campo, the Duomo and the 17 districts of the Palio.

The only remains of the medieval walls, flanked by two massive crenellated towers with circular base; from here the road to Terracina and Naples left.

In the village of the many springs, the monumental nineteenth-century Muta Fountain pours water silently into a large stone pool, while the Fontanella, shaped like a small house with a sloping roof, offers fresh water to drink.

An easy walk from Piazza Don Zunino down via Roma to the chapel of San Martino and to the Maremola stream, with the old mill of the Bringhiera and the remains of the medieval bridge destroyed by the flood of 1933; continues under a canal watering hanging up to Terra Molino, from where you go up to the museum of Bardino Nuovo or continue towards Isallo (Magliolo) and the ruins of an active ironworks from 1730 to 1860, where the mule trackers brought iron ore of Elba.
The medieval canals.

The Nossana, the main tributary of the Serio right, is born from sources that feed an aqueduct of 900-1,500 liters per second, sufficient for 118,000 people in the province of Bergamo, and for centuries moved the sweaters of the village. Along Via Sorgenti remain the traces of a mill mill and the fish hatchery; frequent destination of the schoolchildren, it is combined with the visit to the Maglio Museum.

Founded in the 12th century by Augustinian canons on morainic hills near the resurgences of the Terdomio, in the Middle Ages it was a great agricultural center: from the sixteenth century the cloister became home to peasant families and in the eighteenth century the houses of the wage earners arose, like the Court of the Pigionanti; the community had oven, school, underground glaciers, cheese factory and mill. Today there are few families, with a trattoria and a restaurant; part of the buildings of the XV-XVI century and the cloister are degraded. Free entrance and always open; at the end of January the traditional berry.

Thermal waters on the Tyrrhenian coast.
The parish church of the village, among the stages indicated by the card of the most beautiful villages in Italy.

A mountain swamp for birdwatching.

Ring path that follows an ancient irrigation channel, the Scena Roggia, through chestnut trees and apple orchards above Merano, with a bench overlooking the valley along the path.

Ancient political center, perhaps the seat of the Roman forum, transformed by Cosimo I in the center of the Knights of Santo Stefano: the Palazzo della Caravana of Vasari, seat of the Normal School, the Palazzo dell'Orologio with the Tower of the Muda of Count Ugolino and the church of Santo Stefano.
A Roman mail station.
Dedicated to the patron, martyr in 175, with Romanesque façade and crypt with martyr sarcophagi; the monastery dates back to about 1000.

Built in the XII-XIII century as a round church, it was the chapel of the castle of San Giorgio (Alt-Schenna), of which only the mast remains, today "Uhlentower"; in 1591 a lightning strike destroyed almost half and the central part was reinforced with a pillar. The frescoes of the fourteenth century, well restored, show the martyrdom of St. George, the universal Judgment and the legend of St. Nicholas; there is an altar with Gothic doors with St. George on horseback and a rare seventeenth-century image of St. Kümmernis. Open from the end of March to the beginning of November 11.15-15.30, closed in winter; audio guide available. From Scena about 30 minutes walk or by bus 233 and 234.

Callisto Piazza and Daniele Crespi in the mother church.

The square where the opera house stands, connected to the Duomo from the Gallery, with the monument to Leonardo and his students.

The castle with trapezoidal plan with round towers on the spur above the Taro, then prison, female college and private residence until 1987.
In March the urn for the feast of the blessed opens.

A castle of Ferretti and fifteenth century frescoes.
Open only from June to October (Tuesday-Sunday 9-13 and 16-19), closed from November to May; the source advises you to contact the site before visiting
On the main square, built in 1568 on a medieval church, with Romanesque bell tower with sixteenth century cusp and wooden Baroque furnishings.

Roman rustic villa discovered in 2006, one of the few preserved in the Flegrei Fields: quadrangular plant preceded by a courtyard with porch on pillars, probably of the last years of the II century BC and inhabited until the IV-V century A.D. The press (torcularium) and the wine cell, with a consistent number of coins, indicate a wine production center. Since 2021 it is part of the archaeological Park of the Campi Flegrei; you can visit it on request by writing to pa-fleg.communication@cultura.gov.it.
Spires of sandstone and chestnut trees.
To discover the rural life of Molisana once walking through alleys, stairs and panoramic descents.
Renovated in the sixteenth century in Gothic-Aragonese style on the ruins of a Christian temple of the sixth century, with red porphyry bell tower.
Villages and woods on a walk for everyone.

The eighteenth-century palace of Daniello Bernardi with more than seventy rooms frescoed by Giorgio Anselmi and a view of the Brenta; on the ground floor the Remondini prints, with engravings by Dürer and Mantegna, on the noble floor the ceramics of the city from the sixteenth century.
Walled alleys and sea view from the castle.

Neoclassical church in the center of the village, rebuilt (since 1850 according to the Municipality) on the site of a church of the seventeenth century demolished for breaks: three naves with Latin cross, the colored striped dome and in the central vault a large painting of Neapolitan school of 1775.
Walk on the Roman road.

Overlooking the port, built between the middle and the end of the XII century and dedicated to the patron: the largest Romanesque-Apulian church with domes in axis, with two bell towers, one of which signalled the arrival of the ships. Inside with three naves a Saracen saintly waterworks of the 12th century and a stone high relief of the 13th century under the main altar.

The town of Franciacorta at the foot of Mount Orfano, with a historic heart enclosed in the walls of an ancient Roman fortified castrum in the 12th century; it houses the Museum of Oriental Art with the Japanese collection of the traveller Pompeo Mazzocchi and, in the Park of the Alps, the Montorfano Geological Park.
The ancient cathedral of Baronia, above the frescoed crypt.
An entire nineteenth-century neighborhood that tells the Waldensian community.

Built in 1331 and then modified, it includes the former monastery of the Servants of Mary and houses the civic museum with the finds of Tifernum Mataurense. The church, just before the centre, has manierist interior with Baroque altars and works attributed to Lorenzo Ghiberti, Raffaellino del Colle, Francesco Mancini and the Zuccari brothers, and four ceramic fragments of the Robbiana school next to the eighteenth-century altar.

Example of Venetian Gothic, 66 meters high and visibly pendant.
A walk through newsstands and churches outside the walls.

Borgo della Valle Cervaro-Miscano at 623 meters, home of San Pompilio Maria Pirrotti: to see the Castle Pignatelli with the multimedia museum, the Museum of Montecalvese Religiousness in the birthplace of the saint, the rock village of the Trappeto, the noble palaces of the center and the mud volcanoes of the Bulls of Malvizza.

Palace in the present form of 1883, center of trade of the grains in the Bourbon age; since 1993 the ground floor houses the archaeological museum with the finds of the necropolis of Capo La Torre and Abellinum. The permanent exhibition "La Dogana nella Dogana" is also held, with statues that decorated the façade of the Dogana di Avellino. Open Monday to Friday.
The story of Lake Fucino dried up.

Established in 1981 in the Fortress of Brunella and reopened in 1997: botanical section with Ferrarini herbarium and rare Apuan plants, zoological section with the fauna of Lunigiana and entomological collections, mineralogical section with fragments of a fang of mastodon from Pontremoli, and a roof garden panoramic on Lunigiana, Apennines and Apuans.
