St. Thomas' pulpit.
The Cathedral of the Arborea.

Center of the Iblean plateau near Syracuse, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1693: on the People's Square the Mother Church of St. Bartholomew of 1748 and the MUDAC of contemporary art, in Piazza Umberto I the Ethnographic Museum "Nunzio Bruno" on the Iblean peasant civilization.

Opened by the Municipality in 1994 on the initiative of a group of volunteers, it occupies the second floor and the attic of Palazzo Corielli, next to the homonymous spinning mill active until 1962. Two sections: the seric art, from the breeding of the baco to the trature, and the processing of clay from prehistory to large furnaces, with objects, photos and documents; the didactic model of a furnace of the twentieth century with Hoffmann oven on a continuous fire.
Small medieval church along the path of the ancient Vetus Bell, with a frescoed chapel; a fresco of the fifteenth century probably depicts the village as it was originally.
Caravaggio in Campo Marzio.

Symbol of the city, 46 meters high, built in 1469-1473 and rebuilt in the present form after the fire of 1868, with sundial; it rises on the site of the ancient gate and separates the Old City from the New City, rebuilt more sumptuous after the fires of the mid fifteenth century. Along the main street houses with wrought iron signs painted and gold, shops and hotels; walls remain short stretches.

Small town on the north coast of Ischia, amphitheatre overlooking the sea at the foot of the Epomeum, with the Mushroom of green tuff as a symbol; here stood Pithecusae, the oldest Greek colony of the West, whose finds, including the Nestor Cup, are exposed to Villa Arbusto.
Fiordi, beaches and a country underwater.
Three hundred works donated by the artists.
The city Vercelli.
Italian theater with five orders of stages decorated by seven-pointed stars, by opera, symphonic, dance and prose; in the entrance square a fountain designed by Paolo Portoghesi.
A Norman foundation.

The town of Cilento, where, in the hamlet of Pellare, the Museum Polo "Giuseppe Stifano" gathers in the eighteenth century Palazzo Torrusio the first and most articulated ethnographic museum of the interior Cilento and a water mill of 1747, while on the hill of Civitella, among the chestnut trees, remain the walls of a fortified center of the fourth century BC.

In the former municipal slaughterhouse of Ortazzo, the old district of the boatmen, it collects hundreds of objects, boats and their parts, models, vintage photos and tools donated by boaters who transported goods and people from Vicenza to the lagoon; it tells over seven centuries of inland navigation. Open Saturday and Sunday.

Conca with about ten glacial lakes, once thirteen, including Lake Ramella, Lake Nero and Lake Primo, where you can meet the rare black salamander. Site of regional importance, preserves military testimonies such as the Perrucchetti shelters and, at Lake Ramella, two pieces of cannon of the Second World War; six itineraries range from a walk of about 2 hours to a 6-hour tour.
Rediscovered frescoes and a mocking monk.
Panorama on the plateaus from a fort of the Great War.

Notes already in ancient times: in 1588 the Municipality built the first factories and on July 10, 1857 Vittorio Emanuele II laid the first stone of the present one, designed by Giuseppe Bollati, which at the end of the nineteenth century housed up to 600 people. Sulfurous waters at about 50 °C with algae used in care, thermal pools. At the foot of the Matto mountain at 1,370 meters, open from the end of May to September.

In the nineteenth century Palazzo del Vecchio Tribunale the history of Maremma from prehistory to the Etruscans, to Rome, to the Middle Ages and to the modern age; many finds come from Roselle, including the portrait of Livilla.

According to the Civic Museums in the Palazzo Comunale, it tells the formation of the territory from volcanoes to fossils in five sections (geology, paleontology, anthropology, prehistory, protohistory) with fossils, ceramics and environmental reconstructions.
Villa Santa Chiara houses a nursing home and Villa San Benedetto Menni a nursing home (Lombardy)
Entrance to the free trails; visits by bus for a fee

It is a Romanesque settlement, once in the Duchy of Milan, which became a municipality in the eighteenth century, annexed to Mandello in 1809 and finally united to Abbadia in 1928. It preserves some eighteenth-century buildings and from here starts the path to the Cascata del Cenghen.
The landscape of salt.
The monumental cemetery of about 22 hectares in front of Villa Dante, with an English cemetery and neoclassical, liberty and neo-Gothic architecture.

The historic centre is entirely enclosed by medieval walls that incorporate sections of Etruscan walls of the 6th century BC into large sandstone blocks. From Porta Primo Maggio (Porta San Giacomo) you can reach the "Balcone dell'Umbria" (Balcony of Umbria), a viewpoint over the Umbrian valley.

Built in the 13th century next to the castle, the parish church was sacked by French troops and rebuilt in Baroque forms between 1741 and 1744; the portal depicts the patrons of St. Silvestro and St. Theodora and in the bezel of the small portico there is a fresco of the late fourteenth century with the Madonna and Child and saints. The 65-metre-high stone bell tower was completed in 1764. In front, the small church of Santa Marta with porch, built by the brotherhood of the same name in 1585.
open mon, mer, sat 10-12, Fri 10-18, sat 16.30-18; closed during liturgical celebrations
The lesser known cave.
not available since 2022 for restoration (Visit Lazio)
The fortress of the fourteenth century, now seat of the Municipality, with the contemporary art gallery Arte Viva; the oval walls of the village have two round towers of the fifteenth century.
The gate of the walls desired by Gregory XIII and inaugurated in 1574.
The baroque church with three naves on the terrace of the village.
The Diver's Tomb.

Built around 1336 by Filippo Sangineto, the first Earl of Altomonte, on a Norman church, dedicated in 1342 and passed to the Dominicans in 1443. Latin cross plan with a single nave, facade with rose window and portal of French derivation and massive bell tower; inside the tomb of the Sangineto (about 1360, perhaps of the Master Durazzesco), the monument of an unknown knight of the first half of the fourteenth century, the tomb of Cobella Ruffo and a wooden choir of 37 stables.

Small beach at the south-western end of the island, sheltered by a granite cliff and the promontory of Fort Santa Teresa, with large golden sand, flat rocks that once served as tiles and seabed that descends quickly, loved by divers. Accessible in a wheelchair, with a bar.

Roman funerary mausoleum with circular plan, built along the ancient Appian street in the first imperial age, which preserves remains of the decoration in stucco; not far is the mausoleum called Conocchia. It is entrusted to the Regional Direction National Museums Campania, which organizes extraordinary openings with guided tours, as for European Heritage Days.

Città all'incocco delle valli cuneesi, born around the Benedictine abbey of San Dalmazzo di Pedona, today museum with Romanesque crypt and archaeological area; in the center the sixteenth-century Civic Tower and the Arch of San Rocco, next to the station the Memorial of the Deportation with the MEMO4345 route and, on the hill, the seventeenth-century Sanctuary of Monserrato. At the beginning of December, the Cold Fair is dedicated to snails.
The holy protector of the vineyards.
Built in the late antique age on Velia by Emperor Maxentius, today the site of cultural events.
15th-century ruins of the Basque lords.
The mountain of the botanists overlooking the Garda.

Logudoro-Meilogu country with the late-Gothic parish church of San Giorgio, the sanctuary of San Costantino where since 1923 Ardia has been running on 6 and 7 July, the birthplace of Blessed Edvige Carboni and the Horse Museum in the former Augustinian convent; the territory has about 40 nuragic sites and the Roman bridge of Oinu.
Church linked to the bishops of Spoleto, known for the Romanesque façade with bas-reliefs of medieval stories, scenes of the life of St. Peter and moral allegories.
Walk through the old restored mills.
Excursions a stone's throw from the city.

Begin at the end of the thirteenth century at the behest of Pietro da Morrone, then Pope Celestino V, who is buried there: facade of the first fifteenth century in pink and white marble with three roses and three portals, frescoes of the fifteenth century and the Holy Door open every year for Forgiveness; around the Park of the Sun.

Sunny village along the Way of San Carlo between Orta and Varallo, on the watershed between Valsesia and the valley of Lake Orta; almost destroyed by a fire in 1779, it was rebuilt in Hispano-Moresco style brought by the emigrants who had worked in the Iberian peninsula. To see the Civic Museum Ercole Durio, the parish church of San Gottardo, the oratory of San Rocco and the Falconera ferrata.
The granite staircase and the Apostles of the fifteenth century.
The frescoed ceiling and the theatrical season.

Porticoed streets built mostly between the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, with colored facades, polygonal bovinds (erker), small squares and courtyards; workshops and artisan workshops are located there from the Middle Ages and are still the center of the city's trade.

Opened in 2009 in an eighteenth-century palace belonging to De Scrilli, it was born from about forty years of mons. Vincenzo Catani. On the first floor the section of sacred art with silver, papal medals, liturgical objects, paintings and woods; on the second about 80 Byzantine icons in five rooms; the library has about 4,000 volumes and 53 letters signed (1806-1816) by Francesco Saverio Castiglioni, then Pope Pius VIII.

The valley, which starts from 787 meters, opens towards the side valleys of the Bagni, Porcellizzo and Sasso Bisolo-Preda Rossa, at the foot of Monte Disgrazia (3.678 m), with the Pizzo Badile classic climbing destination; the Sentiero Roma is indicated as one of the most beautiful trekking in the Alps.
The parish church overlooks the large square of the center, built around the ancient castle. It preserves the altarpiece of Titian with the risen Christ that appears to the Mother.

Established in 1989 in Villa De Pisa, built between the twenties and thirties by the Roman Jewish family Bondi, seat of a German command in the Second World War and today in the network of the historic residences of Lazio, in a park of pine, acacia, oak and robinie. It preserves over 2,000 oils, watercolors, drawings, sketches and engravings collected in thirty years by the Association Friends of the Museum of Olevano, witnesses of European artists attracted to Olevano since the nineteenth century; in permanence the Roman Views, twenty engravings of 1810 by Joseph Anton Koch donated by the heirs in 1999, while the works of the twentieth century and contemporary rotate.
On the outskirts in the locality of Bottega, it houses works by artists such as Wildt, Brigoni, Rossi and Ferlenga. Open every day 8-17 in winter, 8-19 in summer.
The path that crosses the Balze del Valdarno, pinnacles and canyons of sand and clay carved by erosion.
The Oristan baroque.
The late-dogotic and Defendant Ferrari at his house.

The Latin Cross Church on the Belvedere at the entrance of the village, elevated to a sanctuary on 31 May 2004; it took its present form with the works of 1623, 1826 and 1908. It houses the table of the Madonna della Milicia of the late fourteenth century, of Giottesca school (restored in 1990), statues and paintings of Bagnasco, the dome frescoed by Totò Bonanno in 1996 with the Pentecost and the bronze portal of Vincenzo Gennaro (2000). On the Belvedere, during the procession of September 8th, the painting stops towards Palermo.
Malfa's mother church.
Cloisters and baroque in the civic heart.

Museum at 2,659 meters, in the refuge Gastaldi, dedicated to the activities of the CAI and the mountaineering between the eight and twentieth century; the refuge is the destination of the most famous excursion that starts from Pian della Mussa.
The island's living room.

Country of the coast of Palermo that for about three hundred years has guarded the Marian cult of the Madonna della Milicia, in the sanctuary on the Belvedere at the entrance of the village; on the hill near the sea remain the Norman ruins of Santa Maria di Campogrosso, the "Churchzza" .

Tonnara of the fifteenth century in Zarbo di Mare, in the Gulf of Firriato, next to the remains of plants for the processing of fish of the fourth century BC; it preserves the "Palazzotto" and tubs in cottopesto. Acquired in 1930 by Plaja and Foderà, it was active until 1969 and is today an example of industrial archaeology in abandonment, along the path to the Zingaro Reserve; in front lies the wreck of the merchant Kent, sunk in 1978.
A coastal tower on the sea.
A stone village of Langa with views from the Apennines to the plain.
Etruscan necropolis, then Carthusian monastery, cemetery since 1801: cloisters, sculptures and monuments of the nineteenth century. Connected to San Luca by a porch.
At the beginning of via Dante, in the area of the Mill, has a front with an enlivened design of pilasters, semi-colons, niches and frames.
the MiC card indicates it is in the refurbishing phase and closed every day
The parishyard houses works of art from the beginning of the sixteenth century to the eighteenth century; the patron saint of San Martino is celebrated in November.
The medieval and modern museum and art gallery of the Metropolitan City dedicated to the painter Corrado Giaquinto, in the palace on the promenade.
Skiing in Sardinia, or walking on the roof of the island.
The work of the sculptor of 1983 offidano Aldo Sergiacomi, a recommended starting point for the visit of the village.

The village preserves the medieval structure adapted to the slope, with loggias, porticoes and the 'vignali', external ladders with covered landing. The fortified part, still known as Castelluccio, stands under the hill with the ruins of the Norman castle, of which the triangular plan remains, defensive towers, a stretch of the Norman tower in the upper outpost and a well preserved cantelmo tower.

The largest hamlet, at 987 meters, among meadows, streams and pine forests, with alpine landscapes and a pond; once had ski facilities. Above the village, the Alpe Corte mountain hut (1410 m), from which the Sentiero delle Orobie starts, the ring at an altitude of about 80 km in stages between the huts (in the area also Branchino and Laghi Gemelli).
The tip of Sicily on the Strait.
A Roman shrine in the hills of Rome.
The Renaissance loggia with two orders of arches, the most characteristic building of the city, overlooking Piazza della Libertà together with the Town Hall with its neoclassical façade.

A cylindrical sandstone tower built between the 12th and 14th centuries, probably part of a larger fortification called "Cittadella" (Cittadella) was perhaps the first cornerstone taken by Frederick III when in 1301 he resumed the feud at Ruggero di Lauria. It is a symbol of Castiglione; next to the church of San Vincenzo Ferreri.

In Palazzo Fantoni-Bononi, restored by the physician and writer Loris Jacopo Bononi: documents the activity of the printer Jacopo da Fivizzano in the years 1471-72, at the beginning of the printing in mobile characters, the invention of the first typewriter by Agostino Fantoni, the Spanish editions of the publisher Emanuele Maucci, with a historical printing rebuilt.
A Franciscan stop on the road to Verna.

The village, about 1000 meters away, is crossed by the Bavorgo, a tributary of Mella; on the central square overlooks the Municipal Palace of the seventeenth century, while the parish church of the Saints Nazario and Celso dates back to the eighteenth century.
In the 11th century castle the human figures carved in sandstone between the 4th and 1st millennium BC, among the most important testimonies of European megalithicism.
Municipality of Varesotto known for the great Archbishop's Seminary of Milan, wanted by Cardinal Schuster and started in 1928, which houses the Museum of Natural History         .

English-style landscaped park designed by Xavier Kurten, spread over 23 hectares with age-old plane trees and a botanical garden, around the castle. Open all year round: in winter 9-16:30, in summer 8-19; you can have a packed lunch, but there are no picnic areas equipped.
At the end of Viale Indipendenza, near Piazza Italia, a panoramic stone terrace overlooking Assisi and its countryside.

San Michele and Sassi Neri, pebble, are partly equipped and partly free and can be reached on foot from the Park of the Republic; Black Stones owes its name to dark sedimentary rocks. Urbani, the largest beach, is reached from Via Bosco. In summer shuttles connect the beaches to the center.
One of the largest cycles of late-Gothic frescoes in the South.
The Circe Mountain boat ride.

Born from an oratory of the early sixteenth century, it was rebuilt in 1628 with three naves with a river stone porch on the Baroque façade; the detached bell tower is of the second half of the nineteenth century. Since 1967 Pietro Annigoni and his students have frescoed the walls with scenes such as the prophets Isaiah and Jeremiah, the Last Supper, the Deposition and the Resurrection, the Four Knights of the Apocalypse, the Resurrection of Lazarus and Pentecost; a side room, called the "Anigonians" is entirely painted by the students. In 1978 the Ministry recognized it as a monumental building of great artistic interest.
for the visit you need to call the Town Hall (0383 551100)

Considered the first Renaissance building of the village, linked to the Galletti family (the house on the Ajalta would have been bought by Neri Galletti in 1397), hosted Duke Alessandro de' Medici, Julius III, Bianca Cappello, Pius VII and the future Leo XIII; since 1891 of the Municipality, today it is the seat of the municipal library. Façade with sandstone window supported by telamoni, vaulted hall, living room with beamed ceiling painted with the coats of arms of the Savinese families and an outdoor theater.
The shrine of the city.
A medieval sanctuary with statues attributed to the Cerano.

Built in 1924-36 on a project by Camillo Galizzi instead of an eighteenth-century parish church, of which the lateral portal dates back to 1752; Fantonian angels at the high altar, the Crucifixion frescoed in the apse by Gian Battista Galizzi (1937) and a table "Byzantine" of the Virgin and Child.

Laghetto 1375 meters at the foot of the Serra di Crispo, called "Giardino degli dei di Signori," surrounded by beech woods and abetinas; near the nearby Iannace Plan (1650 m) some trees exceed 30 meters, and from there the Grande Porta del Pollino is reached in about an hour and a half of walk.
The toll castle.
The Franciscan cloister.

In the watchtower of the castle, it is part of the Ecomuseum of Casentino and collects objects of the life and work of the local population in three sections: work in the woods and fields (grain cycle and tree cutting), pasteurization and transhumance (milk processing, shearing, moving flocks) and domestic processing of wool, from carding to weaving.
The local memory of military internees.
A small garden of trees and legends.
The dish of the city, with its stake.
From the Athena of Fidia to the Civitavecchia of Traiano.
In service for over a hundred years, connects Lower Town and Upper Town in about two minutes.
The square on the lake.

Founded by the International Centre for Research on Aeolian History and Culture (C.I.R.C.E.), it tells the stories of those who emigrated from the Aeolian Islands to the United States, Australia, Argentina and other destinations since the end of the 19th century. Open every day 9-13, on request also at other times.
Museum that exhibits testimonies of rural life, near the parking lot Milicia: the Milicia district is the one where in 1669 the 3,656 refugees of the country destroyed by lava stopped.
A medieval village as it was.
The Resurrection of Fazzini in miniature.

The historic district of Porto Potenza Picena has an eighteenth-century grilled system and narrow and colorful houses, inhabited by the "sciapecotti" fishermen linked to the fishing with the sciabica. In the village remain the fifteenth-century watchtower of Sant'Anna, erected against pirate raids, and the homonymous neo-Gothic church.
Gothic church in Moritzen known for the painted wooden group of Christ's cross bearer with pious women.
A walk between stories and legends.
In the Palazzo del Trono, overlooking Piazza del Popolo, exhibits archaeological finds from Bretty necropolis and underwater finds.

Anthropological demoetanological museum opened in 1994 in the basement of the town house, a former mill built in 1879 by the Trani family. More than a thousand objects in thirteen rooms, from the Frantoio Room with the ancient animal-tracted millstone to the Mestieri Room, the bedroom and the Wheat Processing Room, tell the last two centuries of agriculture and breeding. The MiC card indicates opening on Tuesday-Sunday 10-16, closed on 25 December and 1 January; tel. 0776 546006.
The castle of the counts of Frassinello at the top of the village.
The Santerno Cyclovia (Mordano-Castel del Rio) is closed for flood damage.
Military line built in the 1930s and now converted into a cycle path, which reaches Vicenza.
A monumental tree next to the monastery.
The prehistory of the Maremma.
At the corner of Corso Alfieri and via Roero, the towers of the complex of the ...Tre Re... in the Quarter Tower is the Museum of Mineralogy.

A small town in the countryside of Pavese, where a square-shaped castle, isolated from the fields, has been home to the Oasis of Sant'Alessio since 1973, a park for the breeding and re-introduction of wild species; in the hamlet Vialone the courthouse that gave its name to the rice Vialone.

The work of Istria stone wanted by the Serenissima to defend the coast from the marshes; the Murazzi of Via San Felice were over 5 km long and more than 300 meters wide, built on a territory of palafitte extended to Pellestrina.
By Giovanni Matteo Zucchi, 1790 with hexagonal plan: 17th century paintings, including works by Giovanni Monevi, and organ Collino of 1885.

Borgo della spiaggia piedmontese del Lago Maggiore on a promontory between the Borromeo Gulf and the low lake, a holiday destination from the nineteenth century: historical villas on the lake, the Romanesque Old Church of Santa Maria above the village, the Conelli Park and the Race Society, founded in 1858.

Founded in 1981 and renovated in 2020 in a building from the beginning of the 20th century in the centre, it tells in five rooms the tropical sea of about 240 million years ago (average Triassic): marine reptiles, fish, invertebrates, fossil plants and history of discoveries, started in the mid-nineteenth century by the Museum of Natural History of Milan. The strong piece is the Besanosaurus, ichthyosaur of almost 6 meters with four embryos in the belly; also presented the Saltriosaur, the first great Italian carnivorous dinosaur. Open Tuesday and Saturday 14-17.30, Sunday 10.30-17.30.
Lido on the way to Predore with more than 40,000 m2 of greenery, sports fields and a walkway-solarium on the water; in the village also the Lido Fosio, free area of more than 10,000 m2.
A very rich interior of Apulian baroque signatures.
Characteristic rural architecture, with the fifteenth-century granary of Le Coveyrand used for rye and a building of 1696.
One of the largest medieval squares in Europe, surrounded by buildings of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
The most important church in the village, of the eighteenth century.

Inselberg of gneiss eyedino del Carbonifero, the last strip of the Cozie Alps isolated from alluvial sediments: about 75 hectares, regional natural park since 1980 and 1995 reserve of the Po cuneese Park, the only wooded area within ten kilometers, with over 100 species of birds observed. From the parking lot of Santa Maria, a marked path reaches the top in less than an hour, passing through the "Pera d'la pasa" (Pear of the Pansa) at the top of the public garden overlooking the village, the Tower of Bramafam (a medieval sighting), the remains of the castle of the lords of Piossasco and stretches of the medieval walls.
The highest lake on the island in the Nebrodi woods.

Borgo at the foot of the Pania di Corfino, near the Orecchiella Park, at the intersection of the ancient streets that went up to the pasture of Campaiana, with views from the Apuan Alps to the Apennines; the parish church of San Lorenzo and the Sanctuary of the Madonna del Perpetuo Soccorso, with a sixteenth-century table of the Virgin with the Child.
the MiC card (updated to 2021) reports the closed museum every day: check the opening before the visit

The medieval village of the hinterland is 727 meters above the river Treste, born around the castle built in 1095 by Pandolfo di Sangro; today the Castello Marchesale houses the town hall and, in the tower, the Museum of peasant civilization, while in the village you can visit the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie and the sanctuary of the Madonna del Carmine.
The Cross of Jerusalem.
The imposing building that dominates the village and is the center of the historic center, witness to the ancient history of the village.

The village was born with Bourbon colonization: the first 27 families arrived in 1772 from Torre del Greco, digging the typical cave houses; the church of the Assunta was built from 1772, with the first parish priest in 1781 and the chapel of Santa Filomena added in 1846.
Mosaic of the centuries I-III A.D. with branches of lives coming out from amphorae, between walls in cross-linked work and brick.
In the church of Brusicco Angelo Roncalli received the baptism and the first communion and celebrated his first Mass as a priest; it is part of the common shrine of the country. Open every day 8-18.
The village, perched on a hill at 208 meters in the Pollino Park, preserves the medieval urban layout formed between the XI and XIII century around a Longobard fortress, then become a castle.
A fantastic world that enchants children.
€3 on holidays and pre-festive June-September and every day of August; free under 5 and over 75 years

On the fortress there was a fortification around 1100, linked to the legend of Countess Emma who resisted the siege of Prince Marcualdo and saved himself disguised as a monk; there are traces of Neolithic settlements of the Vase Culture in Bocca Quadrata. The excavations of the late 1970s, promoted by Pro Loco with archaeologists from the universities of Birmingham and Cambridge, have returned weapons, furnishings and perimeter walls and part of the floor of a small church.

Marina and beach of the village, mentioned among the observation points of the volcanic geology of the territory; there are several summer events, including the Festival of the Flegrea Sea and the celebrations of Ferragosto with the fireworks show.
The castle of the "percorso dannunziano" is a castle of the "percorso dannunziano."

In a period building in the historic center, the finds of Nora and the territory: objects of daily use and worship, stele of the Punic tofet (VIII century BC), amphorae and anchors from the backdrops and the golden lamina with gorgoneion, symbol of the museum. Summer 9-20, winter 9-17.30, closed on Mondays; entire 2.50 €, reduced 2 €, guided tour included.
The largest of the three islands of the archipelago in front of Portovenere, on the UNESCO site, with remains of ancient monastic settlements.
The classic beaches around Porto Cervo.
The parish of Badalucco.
A work by Lorenzo di Alessandro outdoors.
The armistice building.

Opened in 1924 in the eighteenth-century villa of Correale, with citrus garden and terrace on the sea: over 10,000 pieces in 24 rooms on three floors, from the Greek, Roman and medieval finds of the peninsula to the Neapolitan and Flemish painting, the Sorrentine tarsia, the landscapes of the School of Posillipo (Pitloo, Gigante), porcelain, watches, shepherds of the nativity scene and fans; the library contains original writings of Torquato Tasso. The garden with the ancient araucaria and the avenue of the plane trees leads to the Belvedere on Vesuvius and Gulf. Amedeo Maiuri called him the most beautiful Museum of Italian province.
Church of the old town on Piazza Marco Berardi, around which there is a neighborhood of houses with external stairs to pergola.

On the second floor of the Palazzo Baronale, it is presented as the first museum in Italy dedicated to depopulation and the abandonment of the inhabited centers, from the Middle Ages to the contemporary age. A room is dedicated to Geridu, a medieval village abandoned and unique in Sardinia excavated in extension, with reconstructions and interactive activities resulting from over twenty years of research; you can also book the guided tour to the site of Geridu. Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday 15:30-20; Wednesday, Friday and Sunday 9-13; Monday closed.

Spilimbergo, one of the most famous cities in Friuli, is famous for its historic centre and for its mosaic tradition linked to the Mosaicist School of Friuli; the monumental heart is formed by the Cathedral of Santa Maria Maggiore, the Castle with the Painted Palace and the towers that close Corso Roma. From here starts the Cyclovia del Tagliamento towards Lignano.

It includes the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie, documented from the fourteenth century, and the sixteenth-century convent of Santa Chiara, enlarged by the wishes of Beatrice Ferrella Orsini up to the Collegiata and transformed in Baroque style by the Orsini. It has baroque façade with porches, painted coffered ceiling and a altarpiece by Giovanni Tommaso Guarini; today it houses the Municipal Library and the Study Center, and the courtyard welcomes events in summer.
The megalithic walls of the Hernics.
Rebuilt in 1862 on the foundations of a building of 1100, it preserves a balcony with the organ and a baptismal font of the fifteenth century.
The fossils of the Panaro, from tapiro to ichthyosaur.
The other district of the Sassi, to the north-west, with palaces and traditional houses built in front of the cavities dug in the tuff.

Tomb of Giganti of the Middle Bronze (XVI-XIV century B.C.), among the best preserved nuragic monuments: basalt blocks in regular rows, exedra of 18 meters with door surmounted by a large architrave, funeral chamber about 10 meters long and niche for the offerings; the name means the house of the ogre. Reused in neo-opunic and Roman age.
Free access during religious services.

The convent was founded by the Augustinians in the middle of the 12th century (1145 or 1147 according to the pages of the tourist consortium), also due to the strategic position of the village on the Adige; today it no longer hosts a religious community. The church of San Michele Arcangelo, with a baroque façade visible from all over the country and from those arriving from Trento, South Tyrol or Val di Non, is rich in paintings and decorations; in the north wing is the Edmund Mach Foundation, an agricultural and environmental research centre.
Church indicated by the Region among the places to see.
The trade of Resian roasts.
The origins of the twelfth century survive only in parts of the stone structure; the rest is the result of a Baroque restoration.

In the seventeenth century convent of the Scolopi, college founded in 1665 and today municipal library: stage costumes, personal objects, photos, posters and about forty recordings of the tenor of Temino Bernardo De Muro (1881-1955), interpreter of Mascagni and Verdi.
About 200 works in filigree ordered by origin: Europe, Asia, Africa and Latin America; the tradition comes from the workshop opened in 1884 by Antonio Olivieri.
The 18th-century cloister of the Town Hall.
Botany and contemporary art a stone's throw from the Victory.

On the highest level of the village, of the 12th century and then renovated, with Romanesque bell tower with bifore, rare in Val Brembana; the restorations have brought to light a cycle of frescoes perhaps even of painters of Averara, the Baschenis. The frame of the altarpiece of 1635 with the Crucifixion bears the coat of arms of the Tasso, with the horn of mail and badger.

The plateau is a natural fortress, covered with oaks, oaks and centuries-old oaks and Mediterranean maquis, suitable for walks, bikes and horse riding; the view ranges from Gennargentu to the hills of Marmilla up to the south-western coast of the island.
The Carmelite monastery of the country.
Water and rock in the heart of the Sibillini.
€11 whole, €9 reduced (with the "Leonardo and Painting" section); cumulative with the whole Christmas house €14, €11 reduced; family €40
Residence of the lords of Challant of the XI-XIII century; not visitable inside.
An open and uncrowded Medici villa.
The two twin squares of the centre, with double loggias, the Palazzo del Podestà and the Cathedral of St. Peter.
Open-air art gallery with more than 100 art walls between murals and sculptures, which make Furore a painted village.
The Madonna found in Cape d'Acqua.
The park on the hill of Posillipo with one of the most spectacular views over the entire gulf, the islands and Nisida.

Square dedicated to Fabrizio De André, surrounded by eighteenth-century buildings and animated by a colorful web designed with Renzo Piano. The Spazio Faber, dedicated to the songwriter, also hosts the Tourist Information Office.
The oldest church in the village, prior to the castle.
The daily life of farmers and fishermen.
To be checked on the official website (secondary sources indicate about €7.50)
In the Palazzo Arnone in Piazza Umberto I, the museum preserves a selection of funeral furnishings of the necropolis, with materials from the 12th to the 6th century BC, and finds of the territory.
The big river and its houses.

Borgo del Parco nazionale dei Monti Sibillini with the Podestà Tower on the Alta square, the fourteenth-century churches of Sant'Agostino and San Francesco with the Anthropogeographic Museum in the cloister, and in the surrounding area the Romanesque abbeys of Santi Ruffino and Vitale and Santi Vincenzo and Anastasio.
Dionysius' defenses on Epipolis.
Gallura cork, from bark to cork.

It tells of the geological origins of the province of Cuneo, the Alps and the Langhe with minerals, fossils of Langhe and Roero, finds of the fossil forest of Fossano and the Rolleri collection of minerals from all over the world; it is dedicated to the geologist of Casca Federico Sacco and occupies the ancient vault of the Cassa di Risparmio. Open on Sunday 15-18 (also on Saturdays from 15 April), free admission.
The hill of the goddess of the harvests.
The underground village that gives the name to the village.
The Annunciation of the Angelic Blessed.
Church of the 16th century about four kilometers from the village, in a natural area with oaks and a nearby spring; a single nave with a Madonna and Child enthroned.

Designed by the Pisans in the 13th century, it is one of the oldest districts: you enter from the port between the trattorias and the arcades of Via Roma to climb towards Castello, crossroads of cultures with a lively atmosphere.
Five centuries of blades in the knife town.
Nature trails in the Muscandia valley, in the woods of Valpinzolo, in the Raseto area and around the Colle Don Bosco, between the vineyards of Freisa and Malvasia.
The shrine in the center of the country, dedicated to the victims.
Busy woods along the stream.
Motor Valley Emilia stop, inside the municipal boundaries.

The first Greek colony of the West, founded in the second half of the 8th century BC by Euboic settlers of Pithekoussai: on the acropolis the temples of Apollo and Jupiter united by the Sacred Way and, at the foot of the hill, the Antro della Sibilla dug into the tuff; in the lower town forum, Capitolium and spa.
the MiC card (updated to December 2020) is closed every day; information to the Municipality, tel. 0775 520213
Birdwatching and sunsets in typical boat.

Large necropolis about 3 km north-east of the village, in use from the Bronze Age to the sixth century BC, with at least 44 graves incinerated; discovered in the early twentieth century, returned in 1902 the Biga from the great princely mound.

Built on the ruins of the church of San Pelino, it has for its bell tower the ancient tower of the medieval castle; restored in baroque style after the earthquake of 1703, the side portal has a carved wooden door.

The most important museum in the region, now in the former municipal slaughterhouse near the Fontana delle 99 Cannelle: the Abruzzo Madonnas painted on a 14th and 15th century table, works by Andrea de Lithium and Giacinto Brandi and portraits of San Bernardino.
The church was built between 1680 and 1722 by the architect Francesco Massari; in the crypt, since 1996, the Museo della Civiltà Contadina ed Artigiana del medio Piceno.

A 250-metre-long railway viaduct, built between 1889 and 1891 on the historical line Gioia del Colle-Rocchetta Sant'Antonio that united Puglia and Basilicata, today no longer crossed by trains: round arches and 19th-century brick pylons between fields and hills. You can reach it from paths and country roads; you can not climb the tracks.
Click a few minutes from the center.
One of the three most famous Marian sanctuaries in Tuscany, with Michelozzo's temple and the Crucifixion of Luca della Robbia; in the loggia the Treasure Museum, by appointment.

Founded in 1982 in the Doge's Palace of the seventeenth century, in the historic centre overlooking the main square: 16 rooms with rural objects from the seventeenth century to the second world war, among peasant tools, carpenters, workshop, blacksmith, blacksmith and cartographer, a kitchen with pots and dishes, an eighteenth-century frame, palment, laundry and private chapel, with different rooms furnished as originally. Outside about 10,000 m2 of green with vegetable garden, biopark, a medieval rock settlement, viewpoint and botanical garden.
Ancient irrigation channels to walk or pedal along.
Two medieval churches merged into one, with a fresco of the fifteenth century.
The palace of the Marquis Colelli where in 1849 lived Anita Garibaldi with her husband.
Baroque jewel of the early eighteenth century, perhaps the smallest theatre in the world.
The only large green sea between Anzio and Neptune.
A Michelangelo project.
The path in the surroundings with the historic Badia and the garden of Scornabecchi, an oasis with medieval springs.
The tallest chapel.
The ancient centers of Castelnuovo Alto and Mondonio, where St. Dominic Savio died, and the old farmsteads of Morialdo, Nevissano and Ranello, guardians of the peasant civilization of Monferrato.
17th century palace, dated 1696, now seat of the Town Hall.
The tower over the village.
Built in the 17th century as a courthouse, the Loggia of Piazza Roma is today a theatre.
The 17th-century park of the Justinians.
A Waldensian temple of the nineteenth century with its wooden gallery.
15th century church in the center of the village, with a statue of the sixteenth century; in mid May the feast of the saint with procession and ardy.
The stone watchman of Ceglie, with a view to the Adriatic.

Excursion of about 4.2 km (1 hour and about 20, 629 m of descent) on path no. 35: from Laion to the Vogelweiderhof, birthplace of the Minnesinger Walther von der Vogelweide, cross Novale and descend to Ponte Gardena with a view of Castel Trostburg. Recommended in autumn, when the farms along the route offer the Törggelen.
The turret door of the medieval walls.

Route through streets, stretches and ancient houses of the historic center, with works that combine objects of rural tradition with contemporary sculptures and paintings. Realized by the Municipality and managed by the Cultural Association Arx Prandi, it was set up in 2004 and enriched in 2010 with the painted Muri and in 2011 with the "Sofitta dei Ricordi" (Ricordi's Attic).
A huge rock portal on the Mison.

Documented since 1040, the present building dates back to the 12th century: an example of Lombard Romanesque with Verona influences, with a polychrome marble facade and a portal carved with plant, animal and mermaid motifs. In the crypt, a sarcophagus guards the remains of Saint Herculaneum; inside a Madonna by Paolo Veneziano.
The view from above on Angera and the lake.
The palace of the accounts, today municipal house and museum.

It tells the craftsmanship of the corn pulp that in the post-war period made Rojale a center of bags and baskets sold in Italy and abroad; after the decline of the early 1950s, the parish priest Don Mario Fabrizio started the relaunch in 1950, with a professional school and in 1964 the Cooperative craft cartocciai Friulani (about one hundred members, closed in 1987). Two rooms: screen, bags, lampshades, footwear and a bed of 1955; then cribs, Easter bells, a Madonna of Lourdes and dolls of crafts. Visits on request (tel. 0432 852222).

It gathers about 500 items, mostly Japanese, brought by Pompeo Mazzocchi (1829-1915), merchant and entrepreneur of Coccaglio who traveled to Europe, Africa and Asia, especially in Japan, on the trail of the silkworm to save the Lombard silk-growing. Weapons, ivory, xilographies, lacquers, jewelry, paintings, ceramics, fabrics, photographs and bronzes are ordered in four rooms: Gelso (Mazzocchi e la bachicoltura), Cherry (history of Japan), Bamboo (daily objects) and Acero (prints ukiyo-e). The Municipality indicates opening on Wednesdays from 15 to 18; guided tours and workshops on request; ticket at variable cost.
Only in the Christmas period

Digged in Roman times, it is the terminal point of an ancient perhaps Etruscan aqueduct and for centuries it was the only public water reserve in the city: on the stones of the pool remain the signs of the jugs; a guardian appointed by the Priors kept its key. The present form is of the early seventeenth century.
The mother church on the square.
A Lombard organ of 1827 in the parish of the village.
Rocks, plants and animals of Sila in one place.

Fortress of Longobard origin (VII century) rebuilt in the fourteenth century, in the highest and oldest point of the village; it was largely destroyed by the Germans in 1944. The round tower, survived the earthquake of 1917, is the symbol of the village and appears in the coat of arms; from the terrace you can see Verna and Monte Fumaiolo, where the Tiber is born.
A late-Gothic church over the country.
Green area with a large goose game and a tree house for word hunting, with accessible and inclusive installations.
The beaches of Coreca and Tonnara and the Scogli di Isca, destination for diving.
One of the oldest universities in the world, where Foscolo and Volta taught; the most beloved place is the Courtyard of the Magnolias.
Remains of an elegant imperial residence on the north-western promontory, with a panoramic ambulacrum overlooking the sea, a loggia and a small late medieval watchtower.
This is the plan that began on May 7, 1565 at the initiative of Francesco Mozzoni and is parish since November 9, 1605; it reached its final appearance only in the middle of the twentieth century.
A cycle of late-Gothic frescoes.
The statue that speaks.
Robbian ceramics signed.

Abbey church rebuilt by Giulio Romano between 1540 and 1545 without demolishing the Romanesque and Gothic structures, incorporating the oratory of Santa Maria dell'XI-XII century. It houses 32 statues of terracotta saints by Antonio Begarelli, the carved wardrobes of the sacristy of Giovanni Maria Piantavigna and the alabaster sarcophagus of Matilde di Canossa on four red marble lions (the remains were brought to St. Peter in Rome in 1633).
The medieval village around the Fortress.
Sulfurean waters known to the Romans.

Born after the apparitions of the Archangel of 490, 492 and 493, it is a continuous pilgrimage destination: from the octagonal tower of 27 meters, 86 steps descend to the bronze gates merged in Constantinople in 1076 and to the cave with the altar and the statue of the saint; in the Lombard crypts the inscriptions of the dukes of Benevento. Longobard tracks have been a UNESCO heritage since 2011.
The village among the fogs of the lake.

Built on the water after the middle of the 14th century by Della Scala di Verona, under Cansignorio and Antonio II, to defend the territory of Verona that the family ruled from 1259 to 1387; then, lost importance in favor of Peschiera, it was storage and barracks, and the restorations since 1919 gave it the current appearance. It is among the best preserved castles of Italy and has its own dock, a rare example of fortification for port use: you can visit the courtyard, walks of the round, dock and panoramic mast; in the internal porch a Roman-Medieval lapidary. Ticket office at the entrance with seasonal opening; it is part of the Musei del Garda circuit with Caves of Catullo and Villa Romana of Desenzano.
Collection of 36 puppets from the Catania school of the late nineteenth century and early twentieth century.
The hamlet of the high Val di Vara, Orange Flag, with the round village of painted porticoed houses, the Castle of the Fieschi and the church of Saints Teresa d'Avila and Filippo Neri.
Fossil, Middle Ages and Frederick II in an eighteenth-century palace.
The pier of the first Italian electric railroad, a few steps from Switzerland.

Established by the Lazio Region in 1989 in Palazzo Gori, it tells on three floors the Sabina civilization: on the ground floor materials of the Middle and Upper Paleolithic, at the first the Bronze and Iron Age with ceramics from the necropolis and a collection of iron weapons, at the second the Hellenistic age, the Romanization and the Middle Ages. Closed on Sundays.

The seventeenth-century palace of the princes of Bisignano, with frescoed rooms attributed to Donato Vitale (1714-1718) and the Sala delle Colonne, donated to the Municipality in the eighties. From 2006 it houses the MACA with 237 works by Silvio Vigliaturo glass master (paintings and sculptures in glass from 1961 to 2004) in 11 halls, exhibitions and workshops, and part of the Museum of Rural Civilization and the Museum of the Risorgimento. Closed on Monday.

The deepest volcanic basin of Lazio, where fishing, sailing and canoeing are practised (the Italian canoeing team is trained there) and which can be turned by mountain bike to the remains of Alba Longa. The emissary, 1,425 m long and according to Tito Livio excavated in 398-397 BC, comes into the locality Le Mole.
Edicola painted by Lorenzo di Alessandro at the end of the 15th century.
The view of Corsica.
The life of the lake fishermen.
The history of the largest popular choir theatre in Italy.

In the convent built by Bartolomeo Colleoni, passed in 1920 by the Dominicans to the Passionists, who in 1984 created the museum dedicated to the culture of sub-Saharan Africa; the proceeds go to their missions in Kenya and Tanzania. You can touch objects, participate in workshops and follow a multimedia guide.

The largest fortified complex in Trentino occupies the entire summit of the hill above the Adige, between Trento and Rovereto: more than a castle is a \"Burg" with streets and squares. It dominates the valley since the 12th century; in 1487 it was at the center of the battle of Calliano against the Venetians, to which are dedicated a section and immersive halls, and in 1796 it resisted Napoleon. You walk the walls, you see the bread ovens, the kitchens and the cellars and you can try helmets and armor; it houses exhibitions and re-enactments. Free with Trentino Guest Card and the first Sunday of the month from October to March; closed from 26 January to 20 March and Monday; final access steep and cobbled, without lifts.
The Medici sanctuary of miracles.
Simple sanctuary about 3 km west of the village, with a fifteenth-century statue of the Madonna enthroned with Child.
Ocher sand and natural pools.
Built to accommodate a Cretan-Byzantine icon considered miraculous.

On the relief of Rocca Angitola remain the ruins of the homonymous Norman city, destroyed by an earthquake and then abandoned; the site is among the cultural heritage of the Kalabria Coast to Coast Way, which rises there and from which you can enjoy a panoramic view of the Serre area.

In the house where Saint Francesca Cabrini lived (1850-1917), born in the neighboring Sant'Angelo Lodigiano and foundress in Codogno of the Missionaries of the Sacred Heart of Jesus: objects, garments and memories of the saint and of the origins of the Institute, with the cells of the sisters visited. In the church of Tabor the relic of the heart of the saint.

The town wine shop is located in Palazzo Locatelli; Cormons is the center of Collio, a land of wines and products such as sweet smoked ham with cherry and laurel wood, radicchio Rosa di Gorizia and gnocchi of plums.
Art and history next to the bridge.
The red sun of Bruno Saetti.
In the printing press founded in 1799 and still active: 19th century press, hand-made writing benches and tools for printing, lithography and calcography.

The residence of the bishops' princes since the 13th century, rebuilt several times and since the end of the 16th century, with a sumptuous courtyard; it houses the Diocesan Museum, one of the most famous in South Tyrol: paintings, sculptures and arts applied from Romanesque to modern times, with crucifixes and Romanesque Madonnas, medieval manuscripts, tables and Gothic sculptures. Next to the Giardino dei Signori with four flowerbeds and Biedermeier bronze fountain. Open every day 10-17.

Centro della Val Fiorentina, mentioned already in 1234 for the church of San Lorenzo, Selva di Cadore houses in the Civic Museum Vittorino Cazzetta the mesolithic burial of the hunter of Mondeval, about 7,500 years ago, and the cast of the boulder of Pelmetto with the dinosaur prints of the upper Triassico.
A tour of churches and the sunset on the Tyrrhenian Sea.

Fortress on the height of the village on three levels plus the 32-metre tower: the square walls date back to 820-850, in 1187 passed to the Canons of the Cathedral of Perugia and in the thirteenth century became fortification of the Perugian territory; damaged in 1479, partly demolished in 1778 and 1816-1817 and hit by the bombings of the Second World War, was reopened in 2008 after the restoration. From the tower you can see the lake and the major islands, Minor and Polvese; open every day except Mondays, 10-13 and 15-19.30.
Small sandy beach and fine gravel, divided by the Dragon, partly free and partly equipped, with clear and calm sea; in the evening the fishermen's boats leave for fishing with lamps at night.

Carpignano is one of the Salento countries with the greatest concentration of megalites: Menhir Grassi remains on the provincial for Melendugno, the fragment of Menhir Staurotomea ("great cross" in griko) on via di Pasulo and Chianca Santo Stefano, a trilite of three plates arranged in door, similar to northern European megalites.

Village clinging to the steep side of Mount San Pancrazio, about 30 km from the sea, with houses that seem to come out of the rock, dominated by the Norman-Svevo castle with four towers; in the village the church of San Pietro (1260) and the abbey of San Pancrazio.
Annunciation stage par excellence.

Ancient parish church on a hill overlooking the village of San Vigilio, along the ancient Valeriana street: a single nave, it preserves traces of the Romanesque structure, was enlarged between the XV and XVI century and dedicated also to San Rocco. It houses two frescoes in the building, a sixteenth-century wooden statue of San Rocco, a wooden crucifix and a seventeenth-century altarpiece; it has been recovered by the parish community and the Alpine Group. It is only reached on foot from via Quarone.
Two seventeenth-century speakers of fraternities.

Founded around the middle of the fourteenth century, it became parish church in 1443 and archipretura in 1737; the present appearance derives from an eighteenth-century restoration. It preserves paintings from the eighteenth century, a Pietà by Giovanni della Robbia and an urn with the relics of Saint Tito.
Remains of a thermal plant built in the late Imperial period, between the II and III century AD; according to the Municipality are freely visitable.
Medieval frescoes in the oldest church in the country.
From the village to the Lao canyon on foot.
Ruins of the fortress of Counts Guidi above the village and its ancient bridges.

Founded in 1996 in the former public weight, it recalls the link of the city with the sea through sails and hemp ropes: history of the Navy, naval activity from Unity to today, marine environment and modeling, with scafandron, periscope and compass.
Renaissance facades in the white alleys.
The reserve established in 1996 with the pine forest of Castelfusano, the coastal dunes of the Gates and the salt pans of Dragona.

The 60-metre bell tower houses the largest and most complex astronomical clock in the world, made by the Ungerer company in Strasbourg and completed in 1933: every day at noon 54 bronze figures animate the history of the city for a quarter of an hour.
The Etruscan Velathri, on top of a hill with a view for almost 40 km, alabaster town with Etruscan, Roman and medieval monuments.
Last municipality before Switzerland, at the foot of the Gran San Bernardo Hill along the Via Francigena, home of the Jambon de Bosses PDO.
The costumes of the mysterious carnival.

A long cycle track that crosses the entire municipal territory along the sea and connects Tortoreto to Alba Adriatica to the north and Giulianova to the south; the first stretch of the Bike to Coast goes from Martinsicuro to Tortoreto.
The devotional climb with a view of the lake.

Four domus de janas excavated in limestone in the eneolithic age, which gave its name to the culture of Filigosa-Abealzu; on the slopes of the hill the Nuraghe Ruju, monotorre of 13 meters of diameter.

In the former church of Santa Croce (1610) the Deposition from the Cross of Luca Signorelli, of 1516, with three tablets of predella on the legend of the True Cross, and the great Madonna and Child in glory between angels and Saints of Pomarancio (1577), coming from the nearby church of San Francesco.
Walking through theater, spa and Flaminia street of a Roman city.

According to the natural lake of Friuli Venezia Giulia, in a glacial basin near the Slovenian border, with the Forte del Lago; in summer you take a bath, in winter ice. A circle of 5.4 km (about 1 hour and 40, difficulty T2) surrounds it between beech and equipped sections, not recommended for families with small children.
Founded in 1932, with about 5 million specimens, next to the Biopark.
Lake of 300 hectares and deep at most five meters, 4 km from the center: rest of the ancient swamps of Valdichiana, is an oasis for birdwatching.
18th century complex, awarded the Holy Door.

About 1.5 km north of the center, on the height of the Civita, the Forum of the Roman city with the remains of a rectangular temple of the Ariane era and of two arches; in the Picena age the place was known for the sanctuary of the goddess Cupra. Visits by reservation (375 739 0077).
The dark rocks that watch over Val Trebbia.
In the old town about a hundred ceramists exhibit and sell table services, vases and hand-decorated items.
The best view of the Forums.
The daily life of a century ago, intact.

Itineraries marked from ancient paths recovered, to be done on foot, by bike or horseback, among vineyards, olive groves and woods, with stops equipped at ancient estates; along the way you will encounter rural testimonies such as the Casino of Moggio, the Torre di Castelluccio and the Mill De Sanctis. The territory produces red, white and rosé wines, in particular from Montepulciano and Trebbiano d'Abruzzo grapes.
Renaissance frescoes and art collections in Masnago Castle.
A walk in the history of the village on the river.

The largest church in the city, dating back to the fourteenth century, rebuilt at the end of the sixteenth century, with an eighteenth-century bell tower; it preserves works by Gagini, family of sculptors and architects.

Started in 1899 and finished five years later on a project by Emilio Stramucci for Queen Margherita, in eclectic style with five cuspidate towers and a staircase in double helicoidal oak; original interiors and rocky garden.
Waterfalls and canyoning in Valnerina.
The lawn of the Great Paradise.
Norman walls and popular devotion.

The present building dates back to the 17th century and replaced a previous church; the Romanesque bell tower, of the 12th century, was one of the defensive towers of the castrum. Inside the 17th century baroque decoration with carved ciborium and canopy altar in polychrome wood, and an organ Serassi of 1764 sculpted and gilded; in front stands the ancient Chapel of the Octagonal Dead.
From the 13th to the 14th century, it conserves a Via Crucis by the sculptor Pericle Fazzini.
The marks of the jugs on the stone.

At the foot of the hill of Sant'Alvara, on the outskirts of the village, tells the history of viticulture in Sardinia from a cultural and ethnographic point of view; the associated regional wine shop offers tasting and sale of wines.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 12 of the 21 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
An ancient bridge and the memory of the Shroud.

Complex of horizontal galleries, including the Lower Grotto and the Upper Grotto, excavated by karst in the Grey Calcars for over 500 meters, once inhabited by the cave bear. Inside concretions and forms of cave life; you can reach it with 200 meters on foot downhill from the road to the districts Tezze and Toldi.
Our Lady in the sandstone of Ascanio da Cortona.

17th century church in the center of the village, on the slopes of the mountain, with two registers façade and portal in stone of Sarnico; the interior with three naves with transept and central dome, restored at the beginning of the twentieth century, preserves the Resurrection of Jerome Romanino, the Martyrdom of Saints Gervasio and Protasio of Callisto Piazza and the fifteenth century wooden statue of the Virgin called "Madonna Vecchia" .
A castle of one hundred rooms with frescoes of Raphael's school.
In the writer's house, with the documentation on the history of Alba and the "Anticamera della morte" by Pinot Gallizio.
The two historic theatres of the city, marked by Terre di Siena among the monuments to see.
The icon from the sea.
Where Spontini was born.
Built between 1226 and 1231 at the behest of Cardinal Ugolino Conti, future Gregory IX: fortified monastic complex in yellowish tufa.
Otters and migratory birds on the Sele.

Medieval village on the highest point of the island, born as a Roman settlement and fortified in the Middle Ages; the watchtowers and a second city walls date back to the era of Saracen raids. It is reached from Marina Corricella with the steep Castle ascent.
The smallest theatre in the world, entered Guinness.
The traces of the castle inside the houses of the village.
One of the most important centers of Nuragic Sardinia.
Sighting deer and chamois effortlessly.

Iblean country between the gorges of the Anapo, one of the two accesses to the rock necropolis of Pantalica, UNESCO World Heritage with Syracuse, with the Civic Museum of the Opera of the Puppets of the Puglisi family and the museum house of traditional beekeeping.
On the trail of the first President of the Republic.

The mountain dominates the village: the ferrata of the Val del Rì can only be walked with appropriate equipment, while the SAT 602B trail is a simple excursion with panoramic points on Mezzolombardo that starts from the cemetery and arrives at the beginning of Fai della Paganella.
A nuragic five-tower complex, one of the almost 50 Nuragic sites in the territory; there was found a bronze ship today exhibited at the National Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.
recorded among the abandoned cultural heritage of the MiC; openings only on the occasion of the FAI days

On the summit of Monte Asprano (669 m), overlooking the Liri Valley, it was built in the 14th century next to the castle of Castrum Coeli and for over five centuries it was a parish town of Palazzolo (the present Castrocielo) and Colle San Magno. It contains 18th century frescoes; restored in 1885. On Easter Monday at dawn there are two processions for the "Kiss of the Madonnas."
Documented as Piazza Grande from 1200 and surrounded by arcades, with the column of the Lion of St Mark of 1519 and the monument to Vittorio Emanuele II of 1881, heart of the city life.
Not far from the village, an area where you can see specimens of suede, especially returned to the Sibillini Park in 2006.
Volcanic nature and the "via dell'ossidiana" of Sardinian prehistory.

Set up in the early 2000s in the former stables on the ground floor of Palazzo Lodron Bertelli, it tells the life of the alpine pasture with original tools collected in the pastures and dairy farms of Rendena and Giudicarie: three rooms on pasture and milking, on milk processing and on the daily life of the malgari. Open from Tuesday to Saturday (in July and August also on Sunday), 9.30-12.30 and 15.30-18.30.
The small staircase called in dialect the ascent of the rats, among the places listed by the municipality.
The caves of water worship.
The library and heirlooms of a professor from the country.
Sienese masterpieces from the thirteenth to the seventeenth century collected by the churches of the Val d'Arbia.
The view over the Tanaro and the Langhe.
The tower of Frederick II.
It was built around 1500 and enlarged since 1743, was destroyed by the earthquake of February 5, 1783 and rebuilt; in 1803 it received the insignia of the chapter of San Giovanni Maggiore of Naples.
The Palazzo Comunale, dating back to the XVI-XVII centuries, houses the Pinacoteca Comunale on the noble floor, in the Sala del Consiglio, in the Sala degli Stemmi and in other rooms.

Small village of the Dauni Mountains, near the border with the Molise, which dominates the valley of the Fortore. The historic centre opens with Porta San Nicolò and Porta Nova and preserves the crenellated tower and the fifteenth-century castle, the church of San Nicola and the municipal palace in the former monastery of Girolamini; in the surroundings woods, paths and Lake Occhito.
Fashion and perfume in Venetian history.

The centre of the lower Valdarno in the leather district, which preserves the castrum plant with two main crossed roads and four doors; to see the Collegiate Church of Saints Peter and Paul, the Bell Tower, the Badia di Santa Maria Maddalena, the archaeological exhibitions of Castelfranco and Orentano and the Natural Reserve of Montefalcone on the Cerbaie.

The eighteenth-century bridge that joins the two banks of the ravine and brought water to the city, symbol of Gravina: from above wide views of the ravine and the archaeological area; it was set of action scenes of No Time to Die (2021).

Inaugurated in 1995, he documents the site from the pre-Roman age to the Middle Ages: at the entrance a funeral lion of the 1st century BC, then ex-vote and miniaturistic offerings of the cults of Angitia and Feronia (IV-III century BC) from the sacred area near Santa Vittoria, reliefs with gladiator games, a room on the amphitheatre with fragments of bronze and marble statues and at the center the monumental epigraph of Traiano, an epigraphic section and late antique and medieval finds.
Summer hike at 2680 meters between coniferous woods, with views over the whole valley of the Gran San Bernardo.
In the Baronale Palace of Tossignano, introduction to geology of plaster.
Megalithic walls in polygonal work.

Museum dedicated to the tradition of oil, in the seventeenth-century Villa Boyl according to Sardinia Tourism and in a mill of the Locci family according to Italia.it: exhibit tools, presses and documents on the cultivation of the olive tree.

Romanesque-style mother church around which the historical centre is gathered, built in Norman-Svevian age between the 12th and 13th centuries.

The municipal territory preserves many rural houses in raw land made with the technique of the  "massone" (straw, water and land); among those touched by the path of the Feast of the Earth 2023 the Superintendence mentions The House of Teresa, the Houses Aceto and the Borgo Malandra Vecchia.

The centre, one of the best preserved in Trentino, owes its prestige to the production of velvet between the end of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries: baroque palaces, courtyards, gardens and paved streets from the medieval path, with 67 fountains that once welcomed travellers. In July, the costume party "Ala Città di Velluto" animates squares, palaces and gardens.

The small chapel on a hill between San Quirico and Pienza, reachable by a white road: it is the most photographed place in the Val d'Orcia.

It was cited in 1339 and in 1357 as Prafafabrorum or Pratum Fabri. It conserves a 16th-17th century plant: narrow houses and three-four-storey square stone houses, large wooden balconies, internal courtyards reached by narrow arches, alleys and arcades; stone houses resisted the earthquake of 1976 without serious damage. From mid-December to mid-January, Poffabro, Nativity scenes among the Nativity scenes, brings a hundred nativity scenes to unusual corners of the village.

Set up in a 1910 mill in the center of the village, it reconstructs the domestic environments and the agricultural and festive life: tools for cheese, oil, bread and wine, care of cattle and weaving, a section on traditional men's and women's clothes for work and celebration and a corner with traditional games; the route ends in the bedrooms. First and second floor with architectural barriers.

Inaugurated in 1935, with the porch façade decorated with the mosaic of the Annunciation and the bell tower of 45 meters; inside the royal chapel donated by Savoia house, originally to Palazzo Margherita in Rome.
The peasant civilization of Monferrato.
Under the Basilica of Saints John and Paul, Roman dwellings with more than four centuries of history and the coexistence between paganism and Christianity.

The parish of Gattorna, named after St. James the Apostle the Major, is the seat of the sanctuary of Our Lady of the Guard, built in 1712 on a hill overlooking the country and always symbol and landmark of the community. Accessible to the disabled, with parking.

Paternal house of Captain Giovanni de Lellis and Camilla de Compellis: Camillo was born there on May 25, 1550 in the barn on the ground floor, partly transformed into a baroque hat born in 1712 and dedicated to the saint in 1897; the environment next to it preserves the original form, as evidence of the poverty of the places. On the first floor, for an external staircase, a room with everyday objects reconstructs the age of the saint. Open every day 7.30-19 (in summer until 19.30), without reservation.

Two-century hospice for pilgrims on Via Aretina, in the hills above Florence.
The rock where Maria Luisa, Duchess of Lucca and Queen of Etruria, dug a pool for her bathrooms, at the beginning of the promenade.

A small town on a promontory in the middle of the Gulf of Sant'Eufemia, linked to the end of Gioacchino Murat, shot in the Aragonese castle in 1815; on the sea the little church of Piedigrotta dug into the tuff, in the square the famous Tartufo di Pizzo ice cream.

One of the oldest mines in Amiata, reachable with a short detour from the mine route that starts from Castell'Azzara: the narrow galleries, where women and children worked in the 19th century, can be visited safely today.

Built in 1576 for the Compagnia dei Disciplinati di San Giuseppe, completed in 1593 and consecrated in 1594; the interior was decorated at the end of the seventeenth century with stuccoes by Giovanni Martello, Bernardino Barca and Domenico Dossa. The great ancona of the Dossa (1697-1699) contains a polychrome wooden statue of St. Joseph of 1630; on the canvas walls of Giovanni Battista Tagliasacchi painted between 1722 and 1727.
Temple of Augustine age, 1st century BC, among the best preserved of Roman sacred architecture: it was church, then prison in 1212, again church in 1456 and since 1539 Santa Maria della Minerva.
Bikes and walks along the river.

Ancient alpine pasture just above Pozza, with the Chapel of the Crucifix the destination of a crossroads and the Festa ta Mont every year; it is known for its traditional mountain huts and is frequented by climbers. At the entrance of the valley the Tower of Pozza, the rest of the defensive system of the Corte Bassa di Fassa, flanked by agricultural buildings of the nineteenth century.
The city walls, with stretches attributed to Leonardo da Vinci, and the Marina Sources on the sea.
An entire Roman city, with its bridge still standing.
The archaeology of Agropoli in the new civic museum.
The history of Mantua in a museum.
The ridge of the Asolani Hills between two fortresses, with a view to the lagoon.
It houses 22 paintings by Carlo Levi, who spent his summers painting in Alassio.
The Romanesque cathedral began in 1122, a stage of medieval pilgrims, with the 71-metre bell tower, the paratic panels and the dome frescoed by Guercino.
The Piedmontese baroque in the heart of the village.
The Blue Flag sea and the sunset from the pier.

The village is surrounded by the Erose walls of the Balze and connected by bridges over the gorges; the fourteenth-century parish church of San Lorenzo, on a natural cliff, preserves the oldest painting of the Madonna del Valdarno Superiore, recently restored in the 13th century. In the area also the fourteenth-century church of San Pietro in Treggiaia.

In the Palazzo dell'Arte designed by Carlo Cocchia and inaugurated in 1947, five centuries of Cremonese violin with the violin "Il Cremonese" by Stradivari of 1715 in the room "Lo casket of treasures"; next, the Auditorium Giovanni Arvedi of 460 seats.
Along the Sile, the most important Italian collection of vintage advertising posters, with works by Dudovich, Cappiello and Mauzan.

Also called Oneglia Cathedral, largely eighteenth-century with Baroque façade completed in the early nineteenth century; the bell tower is the highest in the city and the interior is richly decorated.

Small lake, just under 1,000 meters, born from an ancient landslide, between beech and coniferous woods and connected to the Lagabis pond, with water lilies, reeds and an island of larch, birch and fir trees; it is part of the Biotope Prà dell'Albi-Cei. The tour of the lake, almost all on the floor, lasts about an hour and is also suitable for strollers; from the lake you reach the waterfalls of Strafalt, with caves, mills and the arch of a bridge maybe Roman. Balneation only in permitted areas.
What life was like in the fields.

Church at 2,186 meters on the mountain hut, in the current form of 1899 and probably built by miners, indicated as perhaps the oldest pilgrimage site in South Tyrol; inside a group of the Crucifixion and the saints in memory of the dead. Below, in the basin, Lake Totensee with wooden beds and views of the Dolomites; Vie Crucis from Villanderer Alm and Val Sarentino go up there.

Built in 1634 by the SS Company. Sacramento and seat of the Civic Council until 1819, preserves the Ascise of Saint Augustine in the presence of the SS. Trinity of Pietro Novelli called Monrealese (1640 about), an Adoration of the Magi of the eighteenth century and the Transfiguration on the vault; the bell tower has eighteenth century majolica.
The garden of the monastic complex with medicinal herbs, at the center of the guided path "The herbs and monks" on the way the monks treated the sick.
The Cistercian monastery.

Itinerary that touches Colle Forgiara, with marine fossils and spring blooms of gentian, tulips and peonies, the village of Colle Bertone with fossils of lilies and sea urchins, and Mount La Pelosa, the highest peak in the province of Terni, from which you can see Valnerina, Sibillini, Monti della Laga and Gran Sasso; in the area roe deer, foxes, squirrels and many species of birds.

Dedicated to Jude, sacred representation of Holy Week (about 200 people, 19 scenes of the Passion from the Last Supper to the Crucifixion): rotational stage costumes and photos of the editions from 1912 to today, with paintings and sacred art objects from the eighteenth-nineteenth century and a collection of minerals.
The fifteenth-century parish church of Valsassina.

In the ancient Palazzo Ruffo (1875), acquired and restored by the Municipality: books from the sixteenth century onwards (the complete work of Galluppi, editions of Saint-Non, Barrio and Strabone), manuscripts, parchments, archaeological and numismatic finds and the collection of pipes of the craftsman Rocco De Giglio (1913-2009).
Civic and private collections.
The church next to the ancient hospital of the pilgrims headed to Loreto, where there are overlaid frescoes on the cult of the Virgin.

With a view of Corsica and Capo di Stella, it was the base of the apneist Jacques Mayol and today hosts triathlon competitions; it is suitable for snorkeling and diving and is served by the MareBus.
The bronze sphere created in 1998 by Arnaldo Pomodoro, symbol of the promenade.

Two sections: the Elephant Museum with the skeleton of a female of Mammuthus meridionalis found in 1980 by a fisherman on the gret of the Panaro, in locality Bocchirol, with dioramas on the environment, fossilization and evolution of the trunks; the Museum of Venus with a copy of the statue of about 22 cm carved in soft stone about 25,000 years ago and found in 1925 (the original is at the Pigorini Museum of Rome), compared with the reproductions of the Venus of Lespugue, Willendorf, Chiozza and Marmot. The museum's website indicates opening on Sundays and holidays 14.30-18.30, weekdays by reservation.

A historical and cultural route by the Municipality that from Pian del Gac', a green area with playground, tennis courts and bowls and refreshment point, crosses acacia woods, silvestre pine, chestnut, larch and fir trees and pastures up to the lake of Santa Colomba, next to the traces of the silver mines of Monte Calisio: wells called "cadini" and galleries called "canope" . The extraction had the greatest splendor under the prince bishop Federico Wanga (1207-1218) and almost completely ceased at the end of the sixteenth century; about 80 dead bodies remain open.

The fourteenth century, built on a church of 1130, with large sharp arches on the facade and baroque portals; inside the wooden Crucifix of Giacomo and Giovan Angelo del Maino (1496), the baptismal font in marble of Luni dei Casella (1550), the Bride of the Virgin attributed to Bernardino Luini, a polyptych of 1448 and in sacristy the great polyptych signed by Sebastiano Novelli in 1540.
The most authentic part of the city.

The local cuisine offers the gnocchi di tritello, a peasant dish with tritello and flour, eggs, tomato, garlic, anchovies, parsley, oil and nuts, and the long and thin gnocchi "a co' de soreca" of the Prenestini Mountains, celebrated in mid-June; in the pastures between Cave, Genazzano and Valmontone the Cacio di Genazzano is born, pecorino with raw milk Presidio Slow Food. At the beginning of June the Wineries are held in Varmondò, with food and music, and at the end of June the Snail Festival in the district of San Giovanni.

The Athens of Calabria at the confluence of Crati and Busento: the old town on the Pancrazio hill with the Duomo, the Norman-Svevo Castle, Palazzo Arnone and the Museo dei Brettii, and at the bottom the new city with the Museo al fresco Bilotti along Corso Mazzini and the Calatrava bridge.
The majolica of Montelupo from the Middle Ages to the nineteenth century, found in the "Pozzo dei Lavatoi," with a large Renaissance collection.
The most famous Romanesque cycle in South Tyrol, with the first canederlo of art history.

Masso also known as Masso Falchero, named after the donor, discovered by Marco Cima in 1992 in a mill at the Mills Ninìn, where for centuries it was the basis of a press for nut oil. The three sculpted figures are dated by various scholars at the second Iron Age (III-II century BC) and would represent the Three Mothers of Celtic culture, linked to life, fertility and the cycle of the seasons. Exposed in the market square.
Wiligelmo sculptures up close.
Giuseppe Mengoni's cast iron and glass market opened in 1874: on the ground floor fruits, vegetables, meat, fish and bread; on the first floor shops and kitchens until midnight.

Building inaugurated in 1930 as a memorial of the fallen of the First World War and used as a municipal asylum, then decorated with panels dedicated to the fallen of all wars; since 1968 it is home to the Town Hall.
The arena of ancient Abella.

The eighteenth-century palace has been built since 1748 for the Marquis Pianetti and completed around 1781, with an Italian garden; on the noble floor there is the rococo gallery of stuccoes and paintings, more than 70 metres long. The Pinacoteca has as reference Lorenzo Lotto, with works performed between 1512 and 1535 (Deposition, Annunciation, Madonna delle Rose, Pala di Santa Lucia, Visitation), and over two hundred 18th-century pharmacy vases of the ancient hospital; in the palace also the Archaeological Museum and the contemporary Art Gallery.

Country of the Lower Pavese oriental mentioned already in the tenth century on the itinerary of Sigerico along the Via Francigena, with the ancient monastery of Via Dante (capitals of the eighth century from the royal palace of Corteolona), the peasant Museum of the Lower Pavese and a monumental plane tree.

The museum recovers, preserves and enhances the testimonies of the rural life of Campania, with attention to the Morronese territory, with the aim of an ethnographic museum in part outdoors and for didactic purposes; the research study center and demonstrates with tools of traditional vintage techniques, including food, and promotes the regional craftsmanship of wood, ceramics, iron, goldsmiths, furniture and fabrics.
The Nile Mosaic.
Balcony overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea in front of the Aeolians, in a park of about five hectares around the house of the Repaci family, left by the writer to the city.
