The ancient village of the village Luserna, which can be reached starting from Piazza Partigiani, home of the Town Hall. It gathers the parish church, the Loggia dei Mercanti, the Palazzo dei Conti of Luserna, the Parish House and the Tower of San Francesco.
The church on the fortress of the Colonna.

Alpine centre of the Alta Valtellina at the foot of the Ortles-Cevedale group, skiing and spa destination; the historic centre, flourishing between the 14th and 16th centuries, revolves around the Kuerc and the Torre delle Ore, with frescoed churches, the Civic Museum in Palazzo De Simoni and the Bridge of Combo.
The oldest church in the historic centre of Romano Banco.

Portalbera rises at the confluence of the Versa nel Po, which until about seventy years ago flowed near the village; here there were a ferry and a port from the thirteenth century and a bridge of boats, still present in 1916, then overwhelmed by a flood. Boat excursions of about an hour and a half with Navigare Fiume Po (€15 per person on October 11, 2026, mandatory booking) start from the pier of the village of San Pietro.

Also called Palazzo Castello, it was built in the sixteenth century by the counts Ippoliti in the golden period of their imperial manor, lasted until the Italian countryside of Napoleon in 1796; the rooms of the noble floor preserve stuccoes and floral decorations of the eighteenth century and Liberty decorations of the early twentieth century. The central part was demolished, leaving two separate bodies; today it is the seat of the municipality and in the past it hosted an institute for orphans of the war 1915-1918. On the square in front of the palace stands the monument to the fallen of the Great War, inaugurated by King Vittorio Emanuele III (in 1925 according to the Municipality).
The monumental cycles of Burri.

Pieve del VII secolo nel cuore storico originale di Lu: the first inhabited nucleus was in Mediliano, until in the tenth century the inhabitants moved on a more defensible height, probably for the Saracen incursions.

Closes the village on its rocky spur, overlooking the hill and the sea; from above you can see the district of Vallevò, with low houses overlooking the gardens.
A few kilometers from Bagolino, near the Adamello Park: ski area with five slopes of medium difficulty, the cross-country ring Gaverland 5 km and the snowpark.

Built in 1370 as San Gregorio, decorated with stuccoes in the eighteenth century, with wooden Baroque sculptures and a Pietà attributed to Giulio Sacchi.
Remains of an ancient bridge of the second century BC near the Basilica of San Domenico; Frederick II destroyed him almost entirely in 1229.
The organ of two thousand reeds and the terracotta robbian.
In Piazza Garibaldi the Collegiate Church of 1588 with Our Lady and Child and Saints of Sodom; not far from Santa Croce with the Bride of the Virgin of Luca Signorelli's school.
A stone village climbed on the rock.
Farm life in a 12th century tower.

Fraction about 520 meters, 5 km from the center, referred to as "Holera" in a parchment of 1165; the name comes from the containers in ollar stone. Houses placed around the parish, with arches, gates and lanes; next to San Bartolomeo the church of the Holy Trinity, the oldest, with a golden wooden ancon of the sixteenth century. It is the birthplace of Blessed Thomas of Olera (1563), beatified in 2013.
The walls that enclose the elegant and well-preserved old town.

In the center, Palazzo Calice Screm is a complex with superimposed loggias, considered the prototype of the Carnic house; the eighteenth-century palace Linussio Fabiani was the residence of the family of Jacopo Linussio, founder of one of the major European textile manufactures of the eighteenth century.
The parishes of Saint-Rhémy and Bosses, both frescoed in the nineteenth century by the Stornone brothers of Ivrea.
A marked excursion between Marche and Umbria.

Borgo dell'alta Val d'Agri with a view of the remains of the Sanseverino castle; at the foot of the hill the Archaeological Park of Grumentum, the largest Roman city of Lucania, and the National Archaeological Museum of the Alta Val d'Agri, a stone's throw from Lake Pertusillo.
From the Sibillini to the sea.
An ancient nucleus gathered around his church.
The noble palace of the village.
Italia.it reports the bakery and tarallificio Santoro for taralli and caldatelli and the cheese dairy Gisoldo for cheeses; in April the wild asparagus festival is held.

Also known as Madonna dello Spasimo or "Jerusalem calabrese" (Madonna of Spasimo), about 2 km from the center on a hill: the devoted Domenico Longo started it in 1557 after dreaming of the places of Jerusalem on its soil, went to Palestine and returned with the drawings to reproduce them. It includes sixteen small chapels with scenes of the Holy Land and Passion, so small that one visitor enters it at a time; the stone fountain of the square is of 1890, year of expansion and restoration. On the third Sunday of September, the votive women parade for the feast of Sorrows.

The only Greek-Byzantine church in Abruzzo, dependent on the Eparchy of Lungro in Calabria, conserves 75 icons painted on a table from the 15th to the 19th century: for the Ministry it is the main collection of Byzantine and post-Byzantine icons of Western Europe. Visit on request (tel. 388 1655479).

The Civic Tower was built in 1244 by order of Frederick II through the vicar Ezzelino da Romano and elevated in 1504 for the municipal bell .Martino is a national monument and the clock is loaded by hand. On the square overlook the Castle Cini and the fifteenth-century palace of Monte di Pietà, with the seventeenth-century loggia with Doric columns, now home to the Tourist Office and the Library.
Medieval village of narrow alleys about 1000 meters on the Prenestini Mountains, where in autumn it is remembered the traditional drying of chestnuts with the Festa della Mosciarella.
14th-century gothic and novena cumbessias.

A 17th century shrine built on a rocky spur, incorporating an older temple, reached by a white granite staircase of the quarries of Alzo. In the first chapel on the right there is a fresco of the fifteenth century with the twelve Apostles and Christ in almond, restored by the Superintendence.
The memories of the village.
The castle that dominates the village.
visits only by reservation; the complex hosts weddings and private events

In an elevated position in the center of the village, it probably dates back to the 12th century: in 1252 it passed to the Biandrates, who gave it to Asti, and from 1285 the fief was of the Pelletta; from 1807 the Crova were the only owners until the extinction of the family in 1840. The east and north sides have walls from the 14th to the 15th century with two ogival windows and a padded terracotta frame; renovated in the 18th century, it has an Italian garden in front of the façade and above the entrance the stone coat of arms Pelletta-Asinari. The municipality does not indicate how to visit.
Panorama on the quarries of the Stone of Luserna.

The village grew next to the castle with the survivors of Fiorentino and Dragonara after the destruction of 1255; almost razed to the ground by the earthquake of 1627, it preserves the medieval plant. The itinerary of the Municipality starts from the Ducal Castle and the ancient nucleus of the ...Codacchio , near the Matrice Church of San Nicola.
The ridge to Mount Belvedere.
visits only by reservation, with seasonal timetable (MiC): tel. 0985 9969, Sabap-cal.scalea@cultura.gov.it

In a large tree-lined park, it tells the city from the Bronze Age to the end of the Roman era, starting from the collection of the Bocchi family, which collected more than 6,000 artifacts between the Seven and the nineteenth century. Among the strong pieces the Tomb of the Biga of the III century B.C., with chariot and three horses recovered with its excavation context in 1938, attic ceramics with black and red figures, Etruscan ores, ambre, the milestone of Popilio Lenate on the Via Popillia and the famous showcase of Roman glass, with blown cups in the mould of the Syro-Palestinian glassmaker Ennione (I century A.D.). Closed on Mondays; in the garden an archaeological theme playground.
The land of terracotta: the furnaces are just a stone's throw away.

Otiolithic outings, fragments of oceanic crust brought to the surface by movements that formed the Apennines, trails. The Timpa delle Murge (1441 m), of great scientific interest, has basaltic rocks born from magma of marine seabed, today covered by holly; the Timpa di Pietrasasso (1362 m) is a spur of holiolithic rock more than 50 meters high. On the valley also dominates the large wall of the Timpa Falconara.

The sanctuary stands on the remains of a fourteenth-century chapel dedicated to Saint Margherita: sanctuary from 1511, enlarged in the eighteenth century for pilgrimages, is surrounded by double arched arcades; the frescoes of the dome and the exterior are by Francesco Agnesotti of Sampeyre, late nineteenth century. You can reach it on foot along the ridge east of the village, one of the most orderly of Stroppo, with megalithic portals, covered passages, round columns under the roofs, a sink-oven in the square and a small fresco of Giors Boneto in an alley. In clear weather you can see the whole valley and the plain of Cuneo. Visits: tel. 335 6020527 or 335 6820158.
A small town with church and 18th century palaces.

Built in 1825 by the noble Bonaventura Balsamo as "Teatro del Giglio" in honour of the Bourbons, it was bought by the Municipality in 1874, restored by engineer Oronzo Bernardini and named after Garibaldi in 1879: stages with golden stuccoes and damasks, carvings by Buccarella, Epifani and Nocera and decorations by Melchiorre Zalardi. Visitable with guided tours by reservation.

In the sacristies of the church of Sant'Abbondio tells the Pirus before and after the landslide: a bell melted in 1398, a seat and a pool in ollar stone, a silver head of Galeazzo Maria Sforza, pins, buckles and buttons in copper, swords, rifles and iron lights, and a room with the excavations of 1988 in wood, iron, leather and copper. Open from June to September on Saturday and Sunday 15-17; free admission with the ticket of Palazzo Vertemate Franchi or the Waterfalls.
closed due to the earthquake of 2016 (Let's Marche)
The town that formed the Sardinian painters of the twentieth century.
Listing in extension: the guide covers 1 of the 9 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
The municipality is included in the Oglio Sud River Park, whose marked trails along the Oglio run on foot or by bike; the Park Visitor Centre is inside the Civic Museum.
The lighthouse on the sunny side of the Circeo.
The battle of 1859 told by the memorabilia.

In the Palazzo Ada Caetani, built in 1500 by the De Marchis and passed to the Caetani in 1600, with Salone Nobile wooden ceiling coffered and 17th century frescoes. Since 2004 the museum has exhibited about 300 pieces from prehistory to 1900 and the remains of the Caracupa necropolis; free entry every weekend and every day of August.
The Renaissance sanctuary with Greek cross with the frescoes of Parmigianino in the subway of the presbytery and the tombs of the Farnese and Bourbons.
The Gulf of Naples and the islands at a glance.

Established in 1988 on about 200 hectares in the territory of Campagna, managed by the WWF in agreement with the municipalities of Campagna and Senerchia, with observation points and equipment for picnics and excursions.

San Rocco holds two paintings by Francesco Fracanzano with St. Peter and St. Anthony Abbot; St. Peter's a Holy Family in terracotta of Amalia Dupré and an eighteenth-century wooden statue of the Immaculate of Paolo Di Zinno. Sant'Angelo preserves canvases of the Six and eighteenth centuries and San Nicola a remarkable wooden choir.
Tracks of the Roman countryside in Sabina.
The Bourbon Hunting Reserve.

Reserve of about 3,000 hectares between Vittoria, Comiso and Ragusa, established in 1990 to protect what is considered the last spontaneous settlement of Aleppo pine in Sicily; it includes pine forest, Mediterranean scrub, coastal ponds and the final stretch of the river Ippari, with 32 species of orchids and herons, garzettes and knights of Italy in step.
In the hamlet of Sasso, a Romanesque church built in the 13th century; it contains a painting of Saint Lucia from the 17th century and frescoes from the 15th century.

Castle built on the fortress since the tenth century, destroyed in 1523 by order of Bishop Agostino Grimaldi; today of the municipality, houses the museum of the history of the village, art exhibitions and the Gallery of the Theatre with the scenery of Emanuele Luzzati. From the castle lies the bike of Sergio Bianco.
The Enzenberg collection.
The seventeenth-century district with bridges, alleys, canals, houses and warehouses connected to the port, animated in the evening and summer by Effetto Venezia.

Norman city between Naples and Caserta: the Cathedral of San Paolo started in 1053 with the walk-in and the House of Loreto, the Diocesan Museum, the monastery of San Francesco delle Nunche and a center rich in churches, monasteries and palaces at court, as well as the birthplaces of Cimarosa and Jommelli.
Industrial archaeology of a mining valley.
The Romanesque Abruzzo isolated in the valley.
A stop on Artusi's way to Forlimpopoli.
The view from the cliff overlooking the village.
The high hamlets of the 17th century palaces.
The Roman mosaic of the wolf, known all over the world.
The ancient porticos of the center and the streets of the village, with walks along the wall of the park.

The other villages of Verezzi.
The ideal home of an artist.
The building dates back to perhaps the first half of the sixteenth century.

The lounge of the city is with a neo-Renaissance stone fountain by Rezzato inaugurated in 1924. The market has been held since 1406, when Carlo Malatesta granted it for Thursday; Venice added Tuesday and Saturday. Today it takes place Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday morning between Via Garibaldi, Piazza Zanardelli, Via Villatico and Piazza Martiri della Libertà, and on Friday there is the fish market with local producers.
A place of memory.

The old nucleus preserves the Ruciass House, a rustic 16th century mansion built on a rock above the Stura, and a small castle dated 1591 with frescoes linked to the route of the Shroud from Chambéry to Turin through the valley; in the village also a chapel of the Frescoed Shroud.

One of the most panoramic peaks of the Sarentine Alps: climbing through forest roads, huts and grassy slopes passing through the Totenkirchl and the Totensee; on top the cross and a granite globe mark the geographical centre of South Tyrol, with 360 degrees panorama. Excursion from early summer to autumn.

Didactic path that from the Pradera picnic area on the ancient road of France touches a former cave of Renaissance age gneiss and the Riparo Ruminano, discovered by Rumiano in 1890: shelter of Neolithic shepherds where the excavations have returned sixteen stone instruments, ceramics and animal bones. It then climbs to the Baità, probably home of a prehistoric settlement, crosses chestnut groves and a marshy area and ends at the panoramic promontory of San Pancrazio and the museum.
Austro-Hungarian fortifications of the Tonale system built until 1914, reachable by a medium difficulty walk from the Tonale Pass; guided tours on request organized by the White War Museum.
The Gothic finds of Monte Barro.
The walls of Rhegion.
The medieval canal.
Five hundred corkscrew.
The Madonna born from a tree, according to legend.
A less beaten corner of a village.
An easy walk on the shores of Lake Antola.

Palazzo Spagna has a neoclassical portal of 1807 by Francesco Bitetti di Padula, stone staircase of Padula and chapel of the Addolorata; Palazzo De Benedictis, from the seventeenth century, is placed on a medieval tower and leads to the southern façade the oldest honorary epigraph in the country, dedicated to Marco Tresio Fausto. You can see them from the outside.

It rises on the plateau of Kellerana or Limina, 12 km from Mammola, in the Aspromonte National Park, where it lived with other monks Saint Nicodemus, a Calabrian monk of the tenth century and of Byzantine rite. In 1501, the relics were brought to Mammola, who proclaimed him a patron in 1638; the church, rebuilt between 1960 and 1969 and renovated in 2018, is a diocesan sanctuary since 2002. It is celebrated here on Sundays after 11 May and many pilgrims climb on foot along the ancient path of the Seja, which once joined the Ionian coast to the Tyrrhenian one.
The modest farmhouse where Maria Goretti was born, about 1.5 km from the village, can be visited.
From 1263 the headquarters of the official Sabaudo, then court and prison until 1984, today the Istituto Superiore di Studi Musicali.
A great collection of Sardinian daily life.

Started in the second half of the 13th century and completed two centuries later by eagle workers called by the Countess Jacobella; times redone after the earthquake of 1915. The façade is made of square stone with Gothic rosette and Romanesque portal, in the bezel the Madonna and Child between St. John the Evangelist and Pope Bonifacio IV; doors in elderwood with the Piccolomini and Aragonese coats of arms. Inside the fifteenth-century frescoes of the Sienese school, the Madonna with Child by Andrea De Lithium, the wooden baptismal font of the sixteenth century and the Via Crucis in marble by Novello Finotti (1997-98); the main altar preserves the urns of the Saints Martyrs.

The Merate headquarters of the Astronomical Observatory of Brera (INAF) offers daily visits every first Friday of the month, from 10:30 am to 11:30 am: an astronomical guide accompanies Ruths and Zeiss in the park and in the two domes of the telescopes, telling the story of the observatory, today's research and the technology of the laboratories, with explanations designed also for non-experts. There are also Open Nights with visits to workshops and evening observations of the sky, usually 3-4 times a month with the Moon in the first quarter. Online booking via POEFactory; the path in the park is on gravel paths slightly uphill.
The treasures of Vulci.

In the 19th century tanks with star vaults of the Winery Producers Wines of Manduria: two paths between tools and work of the fields and ancient machinery for vinification, with guided tours, tastings and events.

Fortress on the hill Cidneo built between the fourteenth and sixteenth century, overlooking the city: it houses the first public astronomical observatory of Italy, the railway models, the Museum of Arms "Luigi Marzoli" in the Visconti Mastio and the Museum of the Risorgimento "Leonessa d'Italia" (Leoness of Italy); the park is free, the museums pay.
A magical place with the Dolomites as far as the eye can see.
A building from 2,000 years ago.
Collection of the Fondazione Piccolo Museo San Paolo, a museum recognized by the Calabria Region, in the same building as the Palazzo della Cultura.
A Romanesque country with fifteenth century frescoes.

Fraction on the northern coast of the promontory, about 4 km from Vico: long sandy beaches, pinewood of Aleppo (the Marzini pine forest) alternating with citrus groves and the fourteenth-century Tower of Preposti, once defended and customs; served by the panoramic line of the Gargano Railways.
Climb to the castle in the alleys of the ancient ghetto.
Small sanctuary rebuilt between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries on a promontory overlooking Lake Maggiore, in the Rione Maggiore.
The Renaissance in terracotta.
Contemporary sculpture in the green.

Built at the expense of private citizens, the "Impavidi" (Impavidi), as the Latin motto recalls in the façade dated 1809; damaged in the Second World War and rebuilt, is known for the frescoed ceiling and is the second theater for capacity of the province of Spezia.
The lake that appears and disappears in the rock.

Baths at 1,390 meters fed by the Pèio Sources, known from the seventeenth century: three springs (Ancient Source, New Source and Alpina Source) used for carbohydrate baths, vascular care and mud; the wellness centre has swimming pool, hydromassage, Turkish bath and massages. Open in summer and winter.
The Roman door.
The most beautiful Venetian Gothic.
One of the oldest churches in Abruzzo.

Borgo dell'Alta Irpinia at 863 meters above the valley of Ofanto, home to critic Francesco De Sanctis (1817-1883) from which it took its name in 1934; the castle of the Biondi Morra princes dominates the mother church and houses the archaeological museum Antiquarium.

The first archaeological park in Italy, in the middle of the first Italian UNESCO site (1979): on 30 hectares at the foot of the Pizzo Badile Camuno 140 rocks engraved from the V to the I millennium BC, from the Neolithic to the Iron Age. The Rock No. 1 ha hundreds of figures, n. 70 what the scholars consider the oldest depiction of the Celtic god Cernunnos. Five signposted routes: the shortest takes about an hour, four of them are needed for the complete visit. Closed on Monday; cumulative ticket with MUTRE and Cividate Camuno Museum (7 days) at 12 €.
€13 whole; €9 from 18 to 25 years; free under 18
The sea and the stars.

Ghost village on the northern slopes of the Tolfa Mountains, built by Giovanni da Castro for miners; since 1590 the Farnesian Jesuits settled there and in the mid-nineteenth century the neo-Gothic church of Santa Maria della Farnesiana was built. Today it belongs to a farm but is open to visitors.
A path that from the heights of Luino, passing through Colmegna, reaches Maccagno.

The Roman theatre, brought to light between 1954 and 1960, is part of the museum and still hosts shows; not far away the necropolis of Piazza d'Armi testifies to the aristocracy of the Umbrians of the Iron Age.
The bridge over the river.
A White War outpost returned from the ice.
A karst cave hidden under the village.

Medieval fortress with Arab influences that in the fifteenth century housed the Sicilian Parliament; in the inner courtyard reliefs and arched windows. On the first floor a museum and gallery (the Museum of Arts and Traditions of Taormina), on the ground floor the tourist information office.
Touching the confrontation between Africa and Europe with your hand.

Park born in the late nineties on a project by Raffaello Cattaneo, between Via Piave and the river Cherio, to recover the area and protect the reed: a high part equipped with games, picnics, barbecue and a hexagonal tower for birdwatching, and the reed along the river. On the cycle path of Val Cavallina, it is the last stop before Lake Endine; always open, free access.

Works related to the construction of the ancient Via Flaminia: in Ponte Rio an imposing wall of support of the Adriatic age, in Pieve Fanonica a viaduct of Augustan age, and the remains of bridges on the Topino at Foro, Ponte Centesimo and the Iron Bridge, where the foundations of two pylons of a bridge with multiple arches remain.

Itinerary of about 17 km, of low difficulty, starting from Piazza Garibaldi: follows the main phases of the battle with panels and reconstructions and touches the ustrinae, the pits where the fallen were believed to be burned.

Just outside the center, built towards the end of the sixteenth century to alleviate a serious famine; it has adorned façade, paintings and frescoes and a four-piece brick dome that recalls that of Brunelleschi in Florence.
€12, children 3-14 years €8.50, reduced €9 (price 2025)

On the western shore of the Trebbia, 21 km from Piacenza, in a territory rich in castles: the jewel is the walled village of Rivalta, in the Trebbia Regional Park, with the castle of the Landi and the fifteenth-century church of San Martino; at the entrance of the village the statue of the elephant recalls the battle of 218 BC between Hannibal and the Romans.
One of the valley's destinations, at the foot of Monte Rosa.
The finds of Septempeda.
Go up to the sanctuary on foot through the villages.
Walk at sunset between walls, marina and sea.
The ghost village on the gullies.

Beach resort of Versilia frequented from the beginning of the twentieth century, among others by Gabriele D'Annunzio, Eleonora Duse and Vittorio Emanuele III; the beach has the Blue Flag. The walk to the sea is about 3 km long and the modern pier ends in a roundabout of 700 m2, to be seen at sunset in summer.
Where the prehistoric stone meets the cult of St. Paul and Tarantism.
The three squares of Panicale.

The capital in the Adige valley among the mountains, the city of the Council with the square of the Cathedral frescoed, the Castle of the Buonconsiglio dei principi bishops and the MUSE of Renzo Piano.
To see during the fair.

Village of stone houses at 721 meters, on a terrace on the slopes of Mount Monega in the Upper Arroscia Valley, in the Regional Natural Park of the Ligurian Alps: surrounded by chestnut trees, it houses the museum        . The chestnut and the Bosco Addomesticato , the Baroque parish of San Biagio and, in the surroundings, the alpine pastures of Pian del Latte and Case Fascei.

In the woods, dedicated to the patron saint of Pisoniano: built in the 6th century in the place where Santa Vittoria lived with his sister Anatolia during the persecutions of Decius. On the main altar there is a rare table of Santa Vittoria in Byzantine style, dated to the X-XI century.

We will be under a rocky rock at about 725 meters in the Fosso di Sant'Onofrio, probably linked to the monastery of San Liberatore; church rebuilt in 1948 with the statue of the saint and, behind the altar, the Culla di Sant'Onofrio, bed excavated in the cliff; on the lower floor two rooms turned to barrels. It is reached on foot from Brecciarola district with the path S (the path of the Spirit) and on the evening of June 11 the fire of Sant'Onofrio is lit and the procession is done on the 12th.

Small church built in 1675 by a group of hermits on Mount Casteddu, in a sacred area from prehistory; under the floor were found burials and the altar guards bones of the ancient inhabitants. The feast is held on the first Sunday of May; very close is the tomb of giants of Sajacciu.
The church that collects memories of the destroyed country.
Church of the 11th century in the highest point of the village, built on a previous pagan temple; it is the reference of the historical center.

To the south of the Aragonese Castle, among the Scogli of Sant'Anna and beyond the Tower of Guevara, it has black volcanic rocks shaped by the sea and natural thermal springs that allow hot baths even in winter; rich in posidonia, it is part of the archaeological area and at 5-7 meters deep preserves the remains of a foundry of lead and tin. You can reach it by a trail of about 700 meters from Via Cartaromana or by taxi boat.
The beach favored by the Aga Khan, divided by pink rocks.
The Roman entrance to the city.

Opened in 1996 in the Rocca Farnese, medieval fortress transformed into a palace for Pier Luigi Farnese, with the Courtyard of Love and the well of Antonio da Sangallo the Younger, the octagonal tower over 25 m high and a Santa Scala, replica of that of the Lateran, with sixteenth-century frescoes of the Passion. The prehistoric section exhibits finds from the Upper Lazio, from the Paleolithic site of Settecannelle to the Neolithic village of Poggio Olivaster, to the necropolis of the Bronze Age of Selvicciola and to the palafittic village of Lake Mezzano, with two golden bronze swords; on the second floor ceramics from the upper Middle Ages to the modern age, including Viterbo majolica of the fifteenth century. In the tower the Etruscan collection D'Ascenzi and the enigmatic tablet with the Caldera di Latera.
Rame (2400-1800 B.C.) on the Modolo valley: a straight corridor of about 15 meters covered by eleven plates crosses the tower, over six meters high, with niches, slits and a staircase.

In 1229 Frederick II granted to Recanati the lands between Musone and Potenza, with a port and a castle for the defense of the coast: thus was born the first nucleus of the city. The first building was a square tower on the east side, to which in the fourteenth century a second tower was added to the south-west; the walls keep almost intact the walkway, today not accessible. The courtyard, inhabited by a community linked to the port at least until the sixteenth century, in summer hosts concerts and performances of the Arena Beniamino Gigli.
To discover the sculpture between the eight and twentieth centuries in the country that gave birth to the tradition of the plasterers.
The interiors of a noble Palace in Palermo.
Inaugurated in 1931, it exhibits artifacts from the Paleolithic to today, with rooms dedicated to Monte d'Accoddi and Nuragic civilization.
The most important street in the city, about 3 kilometers long, that climbs from Piazza del Duomo towards Etna among palaces, squares and shops.

On the ground floor of the former school hall of the village, a historic layout of the 1930s, realized for the 250th anniversary, recalls the return of the Valdesi to Piedmont between 1686 and 1690 and the siege of the Balsiglia of May 1690, when about a thousand Waldenses, returned the year before after three years of exile with the "Glorious Repatriation," resisted in this last trench. Audioguide available; management of the Fondazione Centro Culturale Valdese.
The historical village of the Counts of Luserna.

In Arab-Norman style, rebuilt in 1934-35 on a previous cathedral of which it retains the lateral entrance, the choir arch, the altars and the eighteenth-century pulpit; inside four marble altars and a wooden statue of the Maddalena of the school of Bagnasco. From the churchyard you can see the Etna and the Gulf of Naxos.
The finds of the Etruscan city of Spina, Greek and Etruscan port on the delta, in a Renaissance palace called Ludovico il Moro with the garden.
Muggia's sculptor.
Inaugurated in 2025, it exhibits relics of Italian and international champions, including the autographed jersey of the Argentine champion Lionel Messi.
Cazzaregli are a dough of wheat flour and maize usually seasoned with garlic, oil, chilli and tomato; then fried pizzas and focaccia cooked in oil, sweet or salty, and aniseed doughnuts.
the Park indicates opening only by reservation (tel. 0365 745007), the MiC card (221) on Sunday 14.30-17.30
The Sienese musical institution, in the Chigi Saracini Palace, signalled by Terre di Siena among the museums of the city.
Sardinian, Italian and Flemish painting in a country oratory.

Next to the church of San Severo, in the district of Porta Sole, it preserves the only work left in the city of Raffaello: the fresco Trinità and Saints Benedictine and Camaldolese, completed by Perugino.

Ancient bishopric of Cosentino, known worldwide as the home of St. Umile, dedicated to the Franciscan sanctuary with a museum; it is also a land of luthiers, with shops in the alleys of the historic center and a museum dedicated to the De Bonis brothers.
The Middle Ages on the head of the Greek colony.
To be checked on the aquarium site
The Piedmontese baroque of Buniva.

The headquarters of the Superintendence was founded in 1999 in the heart of Bari Vecchia, a reference point for the archaeology of the territory: from here starts the project "Underground Bari" that crosses the archaeological subsoil to the Museum of Santa Scolastica.

Irpino village on the fortress dominated by the castle and its Donjon, above the valley of Ansanto where the sulphurous lake of the Mefite, mentioned by Virgil as \'umbilicus Italiae Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â
A landscape of pinnacles and walls above the Flumendosa.
Calanches and sediments of the Pliocene sea.
One of the smallest historical theatres in Italy still active.
The Roman Venafrum.
A altarpiece by Mattia Preti under a ceiling of 1604.
The cliffs seen from the sea, cave after cave.

The town of Bassa Padovana, where the nineteenth-century Palazzo Valentinelli, a former town hall restored in 2011, houses the Civic Museum of the Villages Scaressi, and the sixteenth-century Palazzo San Bonifacio Ardit, with garden and statues, houses the historical archive of the family.

In the Monte Soratte Nature Reserve, you can reach it on foot from the village and offers a 360 degree view of the Tiber Valley. It is always accessible to the outside; for guided tours we contact the Cultural Association Adventure Soratte.
Built in the 13th century by the Knights of the Order of the Hospital of St. John of Jerusalem.
Public garden decorated with polychrome majolica mosaics on walls, fountains and handrails, compared to Barcelona's Parc Güell.
Waterfalls at Chiappera indicated as the highest in Italy, visible from June to early August; in winter the area around hosts cross-country skiing, snowshoeing and ski touring.
Incunabules and manuscripts of a Abbot's library.
In the bishop's palace next to the cathedral: paintings, silver and wooden sculptures and stone from different eras.
A cast iron church.
