The karst lake where Freud walked.

In the heart of the Venetian Dolomites, between Tofane, Cristallo, Sorapiss and Antelao, Cortina hosted the 1956 Olympics and hosted those of Milan-Cortina 2026; the Natural Park of the Dolomites of Ampezzo, all in the municipality, is part of the UNESCO Dolomites System 5. In the center is the Basilica of Saints Philip and James with the bell tower and the three Museums of the Rules.

The Gutturu Mannu park covers about 35,000 hectares of holm oaks, corks, badgers, agrifoils and Mediterranean maquis suitable for trekking; in the hamlet of Pantaleo, a former mining village, the forest of centuries-old trees houses the Sardinian deer and the deer protected.
The eighteenth century, today's shop, preserves the original furniture.

A small hamlet that was the seat of a Benedictine monastery, included in the Parco Naturale Regionale dell'Antola, known for its views of Mount Antola (1,600 m) and the landscapes of the Apennines and the Ligurian hinterland.
The early Christian intact.
A hermitage dug into the rock.

On the hill of San Bartolo, in the hamlet of Marcellina, about 60 hectares preserve the remains of Laos, achea colony later became autonomous (italia.it date 510 BC): established in 1994 after the Italian-French excavations, it shows the main north-south road originally 12 meters wide, crossed every 96 meters from east-west roads, and large houses around uncovered courtyards, almost all with facilities for rain water. A wooden fence follows the ancient streets; the finds are exposed to the Antiquarium of Scalea.
The heart of the old country and its wooden altar.
Andrea Fantoni's altar.

The Civic Tower, symbol of Stradella, is the only testimony still standing in the ancient fortified city, surrounded in 1300 by Bishop Guido of Langosco by brick walls about a mile long. The square occupies the area of the lower Visconti fortress, demolished to make room for the market of agricultural products, fine wine and textiles; next to the seventeenth-century Palazzo Isimbardi, seat of the town hall, and the 17th-century parish of Saints Nabore and Felice.
Another large dome room of the Baia thermal baths, outside the park, on the promenade.

Municipality of Costa degli Aranci, on the Ionian Catanzare, with hilly historic center and 4 km of white beach in Guardavalle Marina, closed by the Ionian calanchi protected as Site of Community Importance; in the village, the eighteenth-century Palazzo Trua and the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie.
Hidden medieval frescoes.
The building on the castle.
A fourteenth-century reminiscent in a tiny village.

It was built on a 15th-century rural house in the Vimercati area and passed to the Carlotti family in 1601, who completed it in 1632 with a large garden with statues and enlarged it at the beginning of the 18th century; bought by the Municipality in 1937, since 1952 it is municipal seat. On the ground floor the Civic Museum, born from the finds collected by the master Giovanni Solinas and expanded by the researchers led by Mario Marangoni, exhibits archaeological and paleontological finds, objects of the Great War and the late 14th century by the church of the Holy Sepulchre, attributed to the Master of Santa Anastasia; the most suggestive room is the Hall of Dreams, of the early seventeenth century, decorated with grotesques. Closed on Monday.
The University's museum of zoology and mineralogy, with the famous anatomical waxes of the eighteenth century.
The signboards of the smiths of the medieval Ossola.
A stop in the historic center.

Po country sheltered from the bank, already a Venetian port of call on the river: the basilica of San Marco with the dome of 46 meters, the museum-cantiere Po 432 dedicated to navigation, the Casa dei Pontieri and the marina from which depart the motorboats on the great river.
The ancient crafts of the country.
Karst plateau of the Ernici Mountains with a view of the colorful woods.
The burials of the cadet branch of the Gonzaga.
Museum space dedicated to the Etruscans with the findings of the necropolis of San Giustino and the settlement of the Prisons, in the municipal territory.
The sun of the Barberini and the ancient walls.
Busy network of hiking or mountain biking trails, with the park guards' cabins.
A panoramic staircase.
A tour of the churches.

Consecrated on September 25, 1791 on the project of the Chierese Mario Ludovico Quarini, it stands on the site of the thirteenth-century collegiate; neoclassical façade with Corinthian columns and interior decoration largely nineteenth-century, with paintings by the Flemish Claret, wooden choir and major altar with silver busts of doctors of the Church. The bell tower dates back to the work of the late fourteenth century promoted by Blessed Oddino Barotti, with the seventeenth-century octagonal spire of Giovenale Boetto; the late Dogotic reliquary bust of San Giovenale is exhibited on the first Sunday of May.

A 35 m high limestone block to the east of the village, shaped by the atmospheric elements with feline profile; the cave, inhabited in the Neolithic, was transformed by the Longobards into a chapel dedicated to the Archangel Michael. Wide view.

In the square stands the votive column of San Rocco, erected in 1772 in white Lecce stone with the polychrome statue of the saint on top: according to tradition, it was built by a ship captain who escaped a plague that had killed much of the crew. In front of the Church Mother of the Transfiguration, originally dedicated to San Rocco, built in the second eighteenth century, with a sober façade and Baroque interior with stuccoes, furnishings and paintings by Giandomenico Catalano and Oronzo Tiso.
Mountain beaches and water sports in the heart of the Sibillini.
A centuries-old vegetable giant half an hour's walk.
access only with permission of the managing body; groups (max 30) accompanied by staff of the institution (Visit Bergamo)
The treasures of Campovalano.

Less than 2 km from the village, it preserves the medieval urban fabric of ancient Carbonara, destroyed by the earthquake of 1930 and restored in a decade on a project by the architect Donato Tartaglia: Piazza Municipio with the pavement, the churches of San Giovanni and of the Immaculate, town hall, pretura, Monte Frumentario and prisons, remains of palaces and a castle. Nearby there is a baroque fountain-washer of the eighteenth century, unique because it develops on two levels.
The life of the fields in the Marches.
The late 19th century neo-Romanesque.
Among the greatest expressions of the Baroque Palermo, with stuccoes, frescoes and mixed marbles of the major artists of the seventeenth century.

Porta del Parco delle Alpi Apuane, Casola rises on a rocky spur above the Aulella, on the border between Lunigiana and Garfagnana, and was long of the Malaspina di Fosdinovo. The village grew up in the fifteenth century around the castle houses in the old town hall the Museum of the Territory of Alta Valle Aulella; in the territory, the Romanesque parishes of Codiponte and Offiano.
Visits temporarily suspended
damaged by the earthquake 2016, some transennate parts (Turismo Marche)

Ancient oratory, built in part with Roman material of recovery, on a small rise surrounded by a moat; cited in the testament of Speronella of 1192, contains inside two fourteenth-century frescoes with St. Nicholas and St. Christopher.

Begin in 1706 on a back of the historic center, demolishing some houses by resolution of the Neighborhood, and completed in 1760; the expert Antonio Spazzi was probably the designer. A unique nave with episodes of the life of Saint Andrew and Apostles in the veils; a major altar in marble inlaid with mother-of-pearl, statues in stucco by Benjamin Simoni, a altarpiece with the crucifixion of Saint Andrew by Antonio Guadagnini (1883) and four side altars with eighteenth-century altars attributed to Carlo Carloni and Sante Cattaneo.

Borgo on the hills of the Valle del Bradano dominated by the Benedictine Abbey of San Michele Arcangelo, one of the most important monuments of Basilicata, with historical convents, hundreds of wineries dug into the tuff and rock churches in the Murgia.
The taste of the Marmilla in a house at court.

On the right bank of the Po, near the confluence with the Dora Baltea, it preserves the archaeological area of the Roman city of Industria with the sanctuary of Isis and Serapide; on the highest hill the ruins of the medieval towers of the Grep and in the village the Baroque parish of San Giovanni Battista.
Created by the association of the same name in Canezza-Portolo, exhibits tools of the cheese factory of the village, houses and shops. Open on Sunday afternoon; other visits by appointment.
A historic villa in the center, to be seen on the opening days.

Cistercian Abbey probably born from a donation of 1197, with works started by 1208 and interrupted after choir, transept and capitular hall; in the chorus sculptures thirteenth century and frescoes attributed to Antonio da Atri. From the end of the sixteenth century to the eighteenth century the Franciscans stayed there, then passed to the Zambra family until 1968 and then to the diocese. The Superintendence indicates it as an example of the Cistercian Gothic in Italy.
The square with the Baroque obelisk of the Immaculate, the third of the great obelisks of Naples, and the church of the New Jesus.
The life of the fields in 1,300 objects.
The parish church of Fratta Polesine, dating back to the 16th century, next to the beautiful eighteenth-century rectory.
The monumental side of the square.
A seventeenth-century account of the minor friars near the museum Peregrinatio Fidei: the cloister contains frescoes with scenes of hagiographics and the Via Crucis and today hosts cultural events.

Sources probably used already in the Middle Ages, with traces of a spa since the 16th century; in 1856 Dr Johann Scheiber built a sanatorium there, which became the Grand Hotel Wildbad at the beginning of the 20th century, at auction in 1939 and then abandoned for a long time. The chapel of San Salvatore, consecrated in 1594, is only reached on foot in about 45 minutes from the village, starting from the parking lot of the chairlift of the Rocca dei Baranci.
The history of the grotto majolica in a castle.
Inaugurated in 1888, horse-iron hall with four rows of boxes on cast iron columns decorated with golden swans, known for its excellent acoustics.
The ascent by cable car and the city at the foot.
The gates of the fortified village.
The nature of Sardinia in a single museum.
The Modena liberty under the square.

Borgo dominated by the fifteenth-century fortress built by the Anconetans, with the castle that houses the Museum of ancient weapons; in the village the neoclassical architectures of Andrea Vici, the Natural Science Museum Luigi Paolucci and the Liberation Museum of Ancona.

An isolated complex in the Pesaro countryside, dedicated to the Annunciation, consisting of church, sacristy, bell tower and house of the rosit. Of ancient origin, with sixteenth-century architectural elements, the church was rebuilt at the beginning of the seventeenth century, when most of the frescoes were made; it preserves an important collection of ex-votes.

The city on Mount Tauro overlooking the Ionian Sea and Mount Etna: the ancient Theatre, the largest in Sicily after that of Syracuse, Odeon, Naumachia, Corso Umberto with Palazzo Corvaja and the Cathedral of San Nicolò, the gardens of Lady Florence Trevelyan and, below, the islet of Isola Bella.

Cities on the cliff above the gorges of the Black, the ancient Roman Narnia along the Flaminia: the Ponte di Augusto, the Rocca Albornoz, the Underground Narni under San Domenico and Piazza dei Priori.
There is only one part of the complex left: it is seen from outside

The project of the castle is attributed to Manfredi, son of Frederick II; Charles of Anjou completed walls and residence, the Aragonese added circular towers and outer belt, the Spanish viceroys the pentagonal bastion of the Annunziata. Donated to the State in 1968, it has been a museum since 1980: the core are the daunie stems recovered by Silvio Ferri in the 1960s, the most important collection of daunie stems in the world, in a path from prehistory to the archaic age. Closed on Monday.
The viewpoint on the lake just a few steps from the village.
A wet area of 123 hectares with large reeds, where about 175 species of birds have been observed.

On the ground floor of the Town Hall, with a section of peasant civilization (about 300 objects, domestic interiors of the late nineteenth century, costumes, the collar nailed sheepdogs and a wooden spoon of 5.32 m) and a geopaleontological section with casts of fossils of Pietraroja and the diorama of Cyrus, the Scipionyx samniticus.
The noon show.
Sea, nature and monuments in one bay.
The church of the sixteenth century.
The square from which starts the walk in the historic center and the district with elegant buildings of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
Easy paths between conifers of half the world.
The oldest Doric stone temple in Sicily, then early Christian church, mosque, Norman church and barracks under Charles V.
Summer walk to a chapel dedicated to Notre-Dame des Neiges.
Jewel of the late eighteenth century dedicated to the famous Verdi tenor, with an underground harmonic case.
Contemporary installation on the seafront: 46 columns 8 meters high overlooking the Strait.

Parish church of Romanesque origin, mentioned in 1142 and rebuilt in the middle of the seventeenth century; the fifteenth-century bell tower preserves the Romanesque system. It is the main historical monument of the village.
The park above the centre of Villa Fabbricotti and the CARMI museum.

Since 2002 in a municipal building that was sentmental prison in the nineteenth century, it tells the southern part of the ager Campanus and the ancient Atella, a city with a regular urban system still recognizable, grown since the fourth century BC under the influence of Capua and involved in the war between Hannibal and Rome. Among the pieces, an ivory with Dionysus and Ariadne and finds of the necropolis of the fourth century BC of Caivano. Tickets only online or with the app Italian Museums.

Frazione about 6 km from the village and almost 700 meters above sea level, surrounded by woods of holm oaks, corks and secular elm; the village, of medieval origin and from the thirteenth century in possession of the Hospitallers of San Giovanni, gathers around the ancient Romanesque church of San Leonardo. The name comes from the sources (Ad Septem fontes), no longer seven, which feed small ponds with light waters. Since 1906, in the first days of June, it hosts the Regional Horse Fair.
The shrine on the hill, the destination of the pilgrimages of six parishes.

The Franciscan complex wanted in 1279 by Carlo d'Angiò for the friars evicted from the construction site of Maschio Angioino, with the church, the two cloisters and the ARCA museum of contemporary religious art inaugurated in 2006.
The starting point towards San Gimignano.

From the hamlet of Grotta del Cepp, in the Albese Valley, start the paths along the Cosia stream: from Via Gatti you pass through the Rundanina fountain and the Baita degli Alpini, where there was the tank of the Crespi aqueduct, in a wood of beech and chestnut trees with the stations of the Via Crucis marked by colorful tiles. The cave houses a statue of the Madonna of Lourdes; in the area they live roe deer.

In the Palazzo Gabriele Marino, he tells with educational panels and multimedia stations the history of the Cedar of Calabria DOP, the collection, the processing and the ritual use in Judaism; from the museum start an art journey in the historic center and an archaeological towards Laos.

In the former Beltricco barracks, also home to the Institute of Occitan Studies, a multimedia sound museum: places on literary tradition, music, history and material life, folkloric and social valleys of the òc language, consultable in Italian, Occitan, English and French. In summer open Thursday and Friday 10-12 and 15-18 and Saturday 10-12; in winter only by booking for groups over 15 people.
Open only during scheduled temporary exhibitions; information at the Cultural Office 0124 5187616

The mountain is known for the richness of its flora and for the wide views of Garda; around Caprino trails, pastures, districts and nature trails, with the possibility of climbing, paragliding and horseback riding.

A public fountain with six jets in the shape of a loggia, symbol of the city: round and octagonal arches on round columns, twelve hanging arches at the top and stones of different eras, including a Roman marble slab with two dolphins; moved after the bombing of 1943 in Piazza Celestino V.
Hills almost to the sea.
The treasures of the cathedral in the crypt.
Contemporary sculptures of the artist Rabarama along the promenade, between the stretches of Greek walls and the Roman baths.
Diocesan Marian shrine just outside the village, it houses a venerated fresco of the Madonna and Child.

On Piazza Trieste the Collegiate Church of San Lorenzo, rebuilt in 1723 on the ruins of the old parish church, with a single nave with a fresco of the fourteenth-century Virgin, and the nineteenth-century Theatre of the Logge, built from a medieval building. In the village Palazzo Cesarini (former Palazzo dei Priori of the 13th century, of the Marquises Cesarini from 1552) and Palazzo Laureati (1660-1700) with rich brick façade.
Private property, venue of events
Church of Lombardy dating from the 17th to the 18th century, in the area of the ancient lazzaretto.
A sixteenth-century chapel open on three sides.
A unique outdoor pulpit.
The castle at the top of the village.
Three churches from different eras in a few steps.

Frazione at the foot of the hill of San Secondo, attested by the 11th century and cited in 1064 among the lands of the Benedictine abbey of Santa Maria di Pinerolo; it was the most important center of the territory, the capital of the homonymous castle, whose castle, outposted on the Val Chisone, was destroyed at the end of the 16th century. In addition to the neo-Gothic castle, it preserves the parish baroque of Santa Maria, from the mid-eighteenth century, and the villa of the poetess Colombini, today kindergarten.

At the top of Mount Gonare (1,083 m), massif of steep walls and woods destination of excursions, the sanctuary is indicated as the highest church in Sardinia and is shared with Sarule, with which the feasts of March 25, late May and early September alternate; it appears in the novel       .The streets of evil of Grazia Deledda.
The church of the patron on top of the village.
discordant times: MiC card (updated 2020) indicates mon-ven 8-18, My Liguria opening on Sunday; check with the Municipality
Sanctuary of 16th century origin, enlarged over the centuries; the ancient apse preserves an ...Madonna in almond, example of Gothic art.
open about two Saturdays a month from 21, calendar on the website of the Astrofili Messier 42 Group; groups and schools by reservation (Visit Lodi)

Two basins of glacial origin, Lower and Upper, connected by an underground water system, on the border with Slovenia, where the chain of Ponze, Mangart and Masso Pirona are mirrored. Spruce, spruce and beech woods host deer, deer, chamois and migratory birds; a path climbs to the Zacchi Refuge and to Capanna Ponza.
Narrow streets with manor houses and rural houses; the main church is the parish church of Santa Barbara, while the church of San Sebastiano dates back to the 17th century.
Alpine flowers and distant mountains on the Pavese Apennines.
Contemporary art in the walkway of the round.
The coats of arms painted from the judicial past of Villabassa.
From the neoclassical to the Dada, in the castle of the village.
A decorated Roman house.
Ramazzani's paintings and the gallery in the former convent.

It runs along the ridge of the hills from the Rocca di Cornuda to the Rocca di Asolo, in about 5 hours of good walking without any particular difficulty, touching Mount Sùlder, Forcella Mostaccin, the church of San Giorgio, the former quarries of San Vettore and the Fornèt spring. The highest point is Collalto (496 m), behind Villa Barbaro, covered by a larch forest; on clear days the view goes from Grappa to Vette Feltrine, to the Euganean Hills, the lagoon and the sea.

Built around 50 BC on the S'Onnarìu hill, on the northern outskirts of the country, it is indicated as one of only three temples of this type found so far in the Mediterranean. Two inscriptions on the side of an altar, "Dei" and "Iovis" confirm its dedication; the fragments of ceramics indicate a frequentation between II and I century B.C.
Museum presented as unique in the world, dedicated to toy horses and hosted in the former Tornese stables; recommended in particular for children.
The tour of the walls of the village.
The life of the Pinerolean farms.
The center of contemporary art, cinema, theatre and music of the city, in Via Santa Franca.
The old fortified border between Savoy and France.
Large central rose window, two double windows open sky and fourteen pillars of the aisles decorated with votive frescoes.
One of the most scenic squares of the interior Marche.
The sea caves of the Costa Viola.
The spire of Ziracco, symbol of reconstruction after 1976.
The altarpiece of Perugino.

Mulattiera (path CAI 278) from Campertogno (815 m) to Cangello (1.364 m), about 1 hour and 30. It starts from piazza Pier Celestino Gilardi and from the stone bridge doubled in 1606, passes through the hamlet Tetti and the oratory of San Marco and goes back along fifteen chapels with episodes of the life of the Madonna, built and decorated between 1450 and 1939; in Selletto a house with fresco dated 1581. The oratory of the Madonna degli Angeli allo Scarpiolo, with square plan with octagonal dome and lantern, has frescoes by Giacomo Gnifetti (1704) and Lorenzo Avondo (1845-1855). The mule track was extended in 1820 with a legacy of Giuseppe Della Bianca.
Founded at the turn of the year 1000, it houses frescoes from the 11th century, the crypt, the wooden choir and sixteenth-century windows.

Cited from 1276, with an inscription of 1283; in the seventeenth century had the Latin cross plan, in 1822 the medieval apse was demolished and in 1953 covered the façade. Inside, frescoes from the middle of the sixteenth century attributed to Giovanni Maria di ser Giovanni Toulouse and a baptismal font from the sixteenth century.

The village of the upper Maceratese with the Cassero, symbol of the city's coat of arms, and on the hill the castle of Lanciano dei da Varano, then residence of the Bandini, with the museum Maria Sofia Giustiniani Bandini and the park; every year for Corpus Domini the course is covered with carpets of flowers.

Site of industrial archaeology about one kilometer from the village, in the copper mine of Camporciano, active until 1907: in the nineteenth century it was the largest copper mine in Europe, with ten levels and about 35 km of tunnels, and hence took the name of the Montedison. You can visit mining facilities, laverie, offices, part of the 19th century galleries, the Alfredo Well Tower with the original hoist of the elevator, from which the miners descended for more than 300 meters, and the church of Santa Barbara, patron saint of the miners. The descent, a staircase of about 100 meters, leads to the 4th level. Tickets and guided tours can be booked online on the museum website.
The Etruscans of the valley, from Volterra to the sea.

On the central square, with the 18th century Town Hall, the thirteenth-century church dedicated to Saint Francis, who stayed several times in the city and performed an exorcism in 1213: Gothic portal with ancient wooden door and Gothic interior with Umbrian school frescoes.
The palace-fortress at the top of the village.
The finds of the sanctuary of Apollo and Krimisa Brettia.

Norman center overlooking the valley of the Fullone, in the Pollino National Park, which around the year Mille became the seat of Roberto il Guiscardo: it remains the Norman Tower, the Cathedral of St. Nicholas with the crypt and, just outside, the Abbey of Matina.
The small semi-abandoned agglomeration that preserves intact the structures of the village and medieval castle, with the fortress of the Tiberti of the XIII century.
A historic stop on the Via Flaminia.

The village was founded in the thirteenth century by the free Municipality of Gubbio as a defensive point on the road between Umbria and Adriatic. The medieval plant retains two of the four original doors, the Santa Porta with the tower and the thirteenth-century Porta di Macione, and two streets parallel to the sides of the central street. Of the fortress built in 1481 by Federico da Montefeltro on a project by Francesco di Giorgio Martini, then destroyed by order of Duke Guidobaldo, nothing remains.

A large wooden tank of the Bronze Age, found in 2005 during works at the southern edge of Noceto: rectangular structure of about 12 x 7 meters, deep at least 3, in which about 3,500 years ago a terramaric community laid ritual offerings. Among the 15th century B.C. finds five wooden ploughs, large baskets, fictile figurines of animals and dozens of vases; the bathtub is rebuilt in the museum with videos and interactive stations. Open from Thursday to Sunday and holidays.
More than 300 20th century works in a former convent.
Chapel immersed in the green of the Pollino National Park at about 1500 meters above sea level.
An underground river with waterfall inside the mountain.

Station built in the nineteenth century with granite blocks, in the center of the village; the train is indicated as the most evocative way to get to Elini, through limestone reliefs covered with vegetation.
The 17th century cloister just outside the village.
The route in the village touches the ancient fortress, the church and the cloister of San Francesco and the Palazzo Pretorio.

An oil town at the gates of Bari: the Romanesque cathedral with Nicolaus' ambo and excavations under the floor, the National Gallery of Puglia in the Renaissance Palazzo Sylos Calò, the Angevin Tower on Piazza Cavour and the archaeological museum of the De Palo-Ungaro Foundation.
A stone village in altitude.
A collection of fossils and mushrooms are exhibited in the same building as the Museum of Paper.

Borgo dell'alta valle del Volturno, known as the capital of zampogna, one of the few countries in Italy where the instrument is still played and the craftsmen build it with traditional techniques; it is recounted by the International Museum of Zampogna in Palazzo Mancini and the International Festival with market exhibition, while the Museum of the Italian Liberation Corps recalls the battle of Monte Marrone.
The ancient angelic door of the village.
Next to the archaeological museum, it tells the natural history of the plateau and the marsh.
Masterpieces in a former convent.

Parish of the 13th century, transformed into a bastion during the siege of 1557 and rebuilt inside the walls; rebuilt in Baroque forms in 1777, it preserves an eighteenth-century organ and the baroque statue of the patron saint Sant'Ubaldo.
The eighteenth-century sanctuary of the square.

Country of the Parma hills along the Prosciutto Road and the Wines of the Colli di Parma, linked to Salame Felino IGP; above the village the 12th century castle, which in the ancient kitchens and cellars houses the Salame Museum, and in the village the 14th century torrione.

The ghetto established in 1555 by Paul IV and closed in 1870, with the Great Synagogue inaugurated in 1904 which houses the Jewish Museum, and the stumbling blocks for the deportees of 16 October 1943.

The Quartarello is a medieval village clinging to the cliff of the castle, with zigzag alleys, stone stairs and a sixteenth-century house with balcony on anthropomorphic shelves; on Christmas it houses a living nativity scene of about one hundred people. La Magghia has perched houses and the church of San Sebastiano with a painting of the Eternal Father; the Rocca has houses on the rock and the circular square "u tunnu" with panoramic bench.

Around the village there is the Wood of the Empire and other fir woods, a rare species in the Apennines, spruce, beech and oak, with nature trails, cross-country skiing trails, equipped areas, water courses and fountains; a few kilometers away are the springs of the Rio Verde.

Municipality of the Piacenza plain crossed by via Emilia, stretch of the ancient Via Francigena: here stands the Cistercian abbey of Chiaravalle della Colomba, founded by St Bernard in 1135-1136, with one of the best preserved thirteenth-century cloisters and the flowered Corpus Domini; in Castelnuovo Fogliani the residence of the Sforza Fogliani extended on a project by Vanvitelli.
The simple house of a mystical Sardinian of the twentieth century.
Antique market that animates the village every first Sunday of the month.
Cloister and incunabula outside the door.

In addition to Porta Friuli, a tree-lined avenue leads to the hamlet of Barcaroli, a quarantine place for goods and merchants with the remains of the hospital of the 15th century Battuti; the church of San Rocco, invoked against the plague, served residents, travelers and boatmen in quarantine and guards the Madonna della Seggiola.
The city of the dead of the imperial port.
The central park with the artificial lake of the 1942 project, the cherry walk of Raffaele De Vico and the Falls Garden of 1961.
The pontoon marsh and the Cambelotti bronze.

Country of Val d'Agri was born, according to tradition, from the refugees of Grumentum, home of the poet and engineer Leonardo Sinisgalli; it preserves the church and the Franciscan convent of Sant'Antonio, the church of San Domenico and the former Dominican convent today Town Hall.
The tailors' church.
Late Baroque parish church of the eighteenth century on Piazza Roma, with eighteenth-century paintings and an altar adorned with carved angels.
The country of bread under the castle.
The Sella Park.

Centre of the Ecomuseum, in the Pastissu park: eight rooms on the agropastoral culture barbaric, from the shepherds with medallions of "su Giuramentu" used to solve disputes on pastures and livestock, to the products of the wood and to the merchants wandering (torrono, wood, carapigna), from wool to traditional clothes, from the wax workshop to the traditional house, up to the carved cases of Aritzo of the wedding set and to the salt on wood, agriculture, blacksmiths and maniscalci.

According to legend, in the 13th century Pastor Moritz saw three streams flowing from the rock, each with a cross; the small church was built in the 15th century and since then it has been a Marian pilgrimage destination at the foot of the Ortles. From the tour center naturetrafoi or from the parking lot at the Hotel Bella Vista you will arrive on foot in about 40 minutes on a flat path (n. 18), walkable with stroller all year round.

Built at the end of the eighteenth century on a project by Cosimo Morelli of Imola, in neoclassical style then renovated; it preserves eight large paintings between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries, a 16th century Crucifix and an eighteenth-century organ of little less than 500 reeds, inventoried as a cultural heritage of the Marche Region.
The view of the valley.

On the eastern side of the Lanza valley, between Malnate and Solbiate with Cagno, the sandstone called molera stone was extracted, used to make the molera; abandoned the activity, the site has become a natural environment, a natural monument since 2015. A dozen main cavities, deep and with high vertical sandstone walls, open mostly along the Path of Fondovalle, between mixed woods of broadleaf trees; remain short stretches of the ancient consort road in cobbled.
Stone and wood houses around the two squares, including the first wooden inn of 1717.
Of Byzantine origin, with Baroque façade, on Piazza Sant'Eusebio.
The most characteristic building in the city centre.
The park looks like an English garden, cedars of ancient Lebanon, groves and ancient fountains, next to the Palazzo dei Diamanti.
Alleys and views of the lake.

It is located in Palazzo Provenzano, a noble residence of the eighteenth century; it houses among other things a milestone with a Latin inscription of 252 BC and a Roman mosaic of the imperial age (1st century AD).

It rises between 1775 and 1805, the seat of the Town Hall with the Council Hall and the ancient chapel; the museum "Le Stanze e le Cantine del Duca" is also visited in the basement on a suspended walkway.
Where Michelangelo was staying.
Started in the seventeenth century behind the church of Sant'Antonio; the works stopped in 1632 and never resumed.

Medieval village at the foot of Mount Cocuzzo, a few kilometers from Cosenza, called "country of silk": in the river park on the Acheron the ancient Gaudio spinning mill and the Silk Museum, in Piazza del Duomo the church of San Nicola di Bari with the facade in tuff of Mendicino, in the Castello the Clock Tower.
The nuraghi of the Truculu plain.

Hill country on the western side of the Serre, in the high valley of the Messima, perched on a rock spike and for a long time farmhouse of Soriano with the name of ...Soriano Superiore, three churches with works of art, the Museum of peasant civilization and the Valley of the Mills.
The story of the Pontine Reclamation.

Church in Alcantarian style with a single nave with six side chapels, dedicated to the Sacred Heart, to St. Anthony of Padua, to St. John Joseph of the Cross, to St. Pasquale Baylon, to St. Francis of Assisi and to St. Lucia; on the main altar a statue of the Virgin, inside a piped organ, on the portal the heraldic coat of arms. It is connected to a Franciscan monastery, where at the end of 1911 the province of San Giovanni Giuseppe della Croce established its own college.

The village is one of the most beautiful villages in Italy, with the tabies, wooden barns of the Ladin culture used for hay and tools; the church of Santi Fabiano, Sebastiano and Rocco is the only building that survived the fire in 1881.
The city's most imposing church is one of the largest in Umbria; the former convent, with two cloisters, now houses the Archaeological Museum and the State Archives.
Bathroom and boat under the Apuan Islands.

Founded in 2002 and reopened in 2005 in the Art Nouveau Palace Arena, it is dedicated to geology, flora and marine and coastal fauna of the Strait and related traditions: 13 collections from about 150 to 2,000 specimens, including abyssal fish of the Strait, paleontological species studied by Giuseppe Seguenza and a collection of shells; the section Traditions folk tells about the hunting of the swordfish with documents, illustrations of the period and ancient tools. The MiC tab does not report updated times.
An 18th century frescoed chapel.

Born in the nineties from the collection of agricultural tools, pastoral, handicraft and domestic and managed by the Association Sabate: tools for pastoral and viticulture, grape presses, a vintage kitchen with early twentieth century furnishings and documents on fishing in the lake. Multimedia guide Zoomguide in nine languages.

The capital of Sabina, the "Umbilicus Italiae" of Varrone: the Roman city under the streets of Rieti Subterranea, the bridge over Velino, the Cathedral and the Palazzo Papale, the Flavio Vespasian Theatre; around the reserve of the lakes Lungo and Ripasottile, the Terminillo and the Franciscan sanctuaries.
Museum of natural history housed in the Savelli Castle; the Ministry's card indicates it during the redevelopment and closed every day. Contacts: tel. 077463641, c.cultura@virgilio.it.
Marche painting of the Four-Fifteenth century.
The Deposition of Lords.

Complex in marble blocks on a small relief above the valley of the Rio Mannu, built from the 16th-XV century B.C. and expanded in the 14th with a trilobed fortification and a four-tower, then five-tower wall; inhabited until the orientalizing age and re-used in Punic, Roman and Altomedieval era. In the central room, a place of worship from the 14th century BC, was found an altar in sandstone in the shape of nuraghe of the early Iron Age, with a tank for liquids, helmets of swords and a sculpted moon sickle. Excavations started in 1983 by Giovanni Ugas. Opening hours: October-March 8.45-13 and 14.30-17.05, April-September 10.15-13 and 15-19.05; tickets at the museum.
Dimora designed by Rodolfo Vantini for the Tosio spouses, with their art collection and library; seat of the University of Brescia from 1908, to be visited only with guided tour by reservation.
Ancient tomb in the locality Maniano, among the testimonies of the past of the city.

Monastery built overhanging the sea in 1681 by Sister Rosa Pandolfi, inhabited by Dominican cloistered nuns: in her kitchens was born the sfogliatella Santa Rosa. After the death of the last nun, in 1912, it became a hotel; the church guards the head of St. Barnabas, among the most important relics of the province.

At about 610 meters below a large rock roof in the Vallone di Santo Spirito, documented from 1275 and rebuilt by Fr.Pietro da Morrone, inhabited still in 1320: the oratory is almost all carved into the rock, with the Holy Staircase on the terrace, two frescoed squares of the thirteenth century on the façade (Madonna with Child and Christ blessing) and, on the sixteenth century altar, the wooden statue of St. Bartholomew; under a stone flows the water considered miraculous. You can walk from the parking lot of Macchie di Coco with the path

Renaissance church of the historic centre: inside an organ of 1696, wooden altars, the main altar of 1748 and frescoes; on January 17 in the square in front of it a bonfire in honor of the saint is lit.
The volcanic cones of the Colli, to be turned on foot or by bike.
It is the only example of Sicilian baroque architecture in the area.
The covered cloister of the former Augustinian convent, with figurative capitals, now used as a food market; the convent houses the public library.
The life of Brosso's miners-farmers.

Natural oasis with clear springs and lush vegetation crossed by the river Grassano, suitable for picnics, excursions and canoeing, with areas for families, nature trails, canoe rental, play area, bars and restaurants. Open from Tuesday to Sunday from 9:30 am to 11:30 pm (in August also on Monday).
The Biennale house.

The hamlet of magnolies and ligustri with views of the Gulf and the Borromee Islands: on the lakefront the church of San Fabiano of the twelfth century, with the engraving called  "table mill" and the sixteenth-century Santa Lucia.
The castle is privately owned and is not open to visitors

Established in 2015 (regional decree 0213/Pres) and managed by the Municipality, it extends for about 731 hectares along the streams Torre, Malina and Grivò, the river Sjava and the Civivena road, between stable meadows, woods, hedges with rows and a wet area. The itinerary of the park goes from Cerneglons to Ziracco passing through Remanzacco, on roads, bike paths, hoods and paths with wooden bridges, touching rural villages and churches, Villa della Torre Valsassina, Villa Laura and Villa Zoccolari, the mills of the roggia (there is also a "Giro delle acque e dei mulini" (Giro delle acque e dei milli), various farmhouses and the Tonutti Museum; on clear days you can see the Julian Alps and the castles of Partistagno, Cuccagna and Zucco. Access to the houses of Malina (Remanzacco), the Park of Grivons (Ziracco) and the former Public Pesa (Cerneglons); free access in compliance with the regulations.
From the town of pasta to the top of Majella.
Memory of the fallen foreheads of the highlands.

Set up in the old parish house of Ossimo Superiore, it reconstructs the life of the early twentieth century and restores the value of the tools that accompanied the life of mountain people, in relation to the land and the surrounding nature. It is part of the Museum System of Valle Camonica.
The capital-hamlet of the Da Palù.
Ride down the Black to the Marmores.
Tracks of Nicolò dell'Abate in the center.
Built in 1365 by Cardinal Egidio Albornoz and linked with the confiscated property of the Atti family, at the highest point of the city, with a wide view of the surroundings.
Former parish church of the fourteenth century on the Arroscia river, today a museum with local sacred art of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
The shrine on the river.
Only trace of the ancient castle built by Galeazzo Visconti.

White village of the Valle d'Itria founded around an abbey of the Basilian monks in the Middle Ages, with four historic districts around Piazza Vittorio Emanuele, the Norman-Sveva Tower, the Mother Church of St. Nicholas and the viewpoint over the valley; it is considered the capital of the "fornelli" .

The Roman colony, founded in the Republican age and monumentalized by Augustus, was abandoned in late antiquity and for this reason it has been preserved in an exceptional way: a path of about one kilometer on 40 hectares descends from the hill towards the valley between cisterns of the aqueduct, Augustian walls, the theater (the most conspicuous of the Marches and the only in Italy with preserved painted decorations), the niche building, the temple of Salus Augusta with frescoed cryptoportico and the amphitheatre of the first century A.D. wanted by Lucio Flavio Silva. The State Archaeological Museum in the historic centre, founded in 1996, exhibits excavations.
The neo-Gothic mother church of the country.
6 km walk from 750 to 1224 meters up to the Forcetelle refuge; along the way you will find the church of San Silvestro of the 11th century.
The two painted sundials of Piazza Dellepiane.
Arriving in Cornello on foot like merchants.
A walk through medieval houses and churches of five centuries.
A 17th-century octagon born of a peace between two municipalities.
Museum immersive with a working 19th century paper mill; the paper mill of Subiaco was founded in 1587 by Pope Sixtus V.
At the foot of the village, known for its elaborate stuccoes.

Regional reserve established in 1997, 444 hectares between the Via Flaminia and the Tiber, also a site of community interest: the Soratte is an isolated limestone massif of not even 700 meters, crossed by 14 CAI paths including the Path of Hermits (205), Santa Romana and Meri (203), Le Grotte (206) and the Military Road (204). The mountain is home to numerous karst caves, which can be visited only with equipment and expert guides.
The fourteenth-century pulpit and Trivisonno's apse.

14th century church from the inside white with Baroque decorations; behind the altar two coeval frescoes, discovered by chance during the removal of the rubble of the earthquake of 2008. It is part of the path of the Diocesan Museum.
Before you see the birds, you know them.
Birdwatching on Trasimeno reed.
The fortress on the village.
From the 15th century, with a major baroque altar and a cycle of 15th century frescoes among the highest of the painting of the time in the region.
The work of a stone priest, with a view.

Medieval village on the sea among the most beautiful villages in Italy, enriched in the sixteenth century by coral fishing: the Baroque church of the Corallines on the churchyard of the chamber music festival and the castle Clavesana with the ethnographic museum.

Excursion of about 5 km from Brallo (950 m) to Fego (550 m): from Bralello a mule track descends into the Bosco dei Giganti, chestnut grove of centuries-old trees, then to the ruins of the Mill of Cognassi, with a narrow hydraulic wheel about ten meters high; following and gaining several times the Rio Montagnola you reach the Grotta dei Briganti, shelter between granite boulders that was the refuge of bandits, and finally Fego, near the confluence in the stream Staffora. No fires, plant collection and exits from the marked path.

Built in the 18th century on the site of a 13th century chapel, it rises on the slopes of Monte Quarin near the original nucleus of the town, where there was a section of the walls; next to the House of Plevan.
Garden of Mediterranean and tropical plants around Villa Hanbury, on the headland of the Mortola.

In the castle's agricultural courtyard, in a former rural complex renovated with a stable of over 600 square meters, porticos and Italian garden, about 800 objects in three sections (the House, the Crafts, the Earth) tell the peasant life of the Lomellina from the nineteenth century to the sixties: wagons, carriages, threshers, a nineteenth-century typography, a riceria, the wooden sculpture The castle, with square plan with cylindrical towers at the corners and moat transformed into a garden, documented in 1409 and rebuilt by the Sforza at the beginning of the sixteenth century, was transformed into a neo-Gothic residence in 1882 by the architect Vandone for the Vochieri; it is a national monument from the beginning of the twentieth century but is private and not visitable.
The karst landscape of the Bari blades at the entrance of the village.

Among the oldest in the city, born between the Five and the seventeenth century joining more buildings, belonged to Count Rizzardo of Strassoldo, commander of the fortress during the wars of Gradiscan (1615-1617); remained almost intact, has a large courtyard and a monumental rectangular portal on Via Ciotti.
Lakes and rare flora among the rocks of the Musinè.
Country at the entrance of the Champorcher valley, in front of the fort of Bard, to which joins a bridge over the Dora.
Courtyard house with courtyard, hanging garden and staircase in Vesuvius stone.
A gorge just a stone's throw from the center.
The Church of the fishermen of Porto I go.
The most complete story of the tragedy, where it happened.
The real David is bigger than you can imagine.

Romanesque church of the 12th century, perhaps on a high medieval church, on which depended several other churches of the Val di Magra apuana. Latin cross plan with three naves and semicircular apse; of the medieval wall remains the door in the south-eastern corner, the base of the bell tower is of the fourteenth century, the seventeenth-century portal has the architrave with the Bernardine coat of arms and frames with branches and flowers, and in the bezel a marble bas-relief of San Lorenzo placed in the restoration of 1927.
The heart of the 18th century.
The shrine in the woods of the 1656 vow.
The Opera dei Pupi, a UNESCO tradition, in its theatre.
The grand ruins of one of the largest convents in the South.
Market with elegant stalls, every Wednesday from 8 to 14.30 in Piazza Marconi and in summer also on Sundays; on winter weekends antique markets in Piazza Marconi and Vittoria Apuana.
Garnier's walk.
The MiC card (updated 2021) indicates closure in November and December due to lack of staff; in the other months Tuesday-Saturday 10-12.30 plus some afternoons; tel. 0923 909431.

It hosts, with the Archaeology Superintendence of Calabria, materials coming from the temple of Apollo Aleo and materials of the historical phase of the Brettii. At the inauguration of the museum, on April 1, 2015, they returned to Cirò Marina after 91 years head, feet and hand of the Apollo acrolite.
The abbey church.

On the upper floor of Palazzo Beltrami, it preserves relics, documents and works by Giacomo Costantino Beltrami, magistrate and traveler, discoverer of the sources of the Mississippi, including a Sioux medicine drum chosen as a symbol of the Winter Olympics of Calgary in 1988.

Above the Park of Peace, an easy walk on an asphalt road leads to Borgata Forte, where walls and urban layout of the Forte de La Perosa of the 17th century, with a well, a cannonball and the entrance arch. A little further, at the Lighthouse of Freedom dedicated to the fallen of the partisan struggle, the remains of a round tower of the castle of Poggio Oddone, probably before the sixteenth century, were re-emerged in 2002. Here is also the red Big Bench, from which the look dominates the lower Val Chisone and the village.
A medieval Cistercian abbey among the rice fields.
The three doors of the fourteenth century.
Spiral streets and stone overhangs.
A Romanesque abbey on the hill.
14th century church that preserves a canvas of baroque school and works of local stonemasons.

Easy ring of about 14 km between Villafranca, Moretta and Cardè along the two banks of the Po, between poplars and fields, with sculptures along the way, a river ferry in wood rebuilt (according to summer) and the bridge of Cardè of 1914, first concrete bridge on the Po. Realized in 2017 by the Association Friends of the Po; the "Route of the Ali" tells children more than 100 species of birds. About an hour by bike or 3-4 hours on foot; parking and infopoint at the bridge over the Po.
64 meters high, it is one of the symbols of the city; from the terrace the panorama goes from the Sibillini Mountains to the Adriatic Sea.

Founded in 1986 by the State Forestry Corps, it reconstructs the habitats of Majella (beech, rocky walls, mugheta), with sections of geology and fossils, the path "Tana della Lontra" and an archaeological section with finds from the Paleolithic below the Roman age, accessible to blind and visually impaired. Next to it is the fauna area of the Eurasian otter; it is also information center of the Park.
the Municipality presents it as a project in phase of realization and the MiC card indicates closed every day: opening to verify
The most ancient and silent face of the village.
The stars of the university.
The promenade from the mouth of the river Astura to the Rio Martino, with Blue Flag FEE and Green Flag for baby-friendly beaches; the eastern stretch is in the Circeo National Park.
12th century church with 16th century interior; it houses the wooden crucifix used on Good Friday for the rite of the "scavigliazione" .

The most beautiful village in Italy in the upper Cervo Valley, at the meeting between Cervo and Pragnetta, redesigned in the nineteenth century by Senator Federico Rosazza Pistolet with the architect Giuseppe Maffei.
On foot to the sanctuary of San Luca.
The Pisan towers of Casteddu.

The Marmilla village between the Gesturi Giara and the Siddi Giara, Lunamatrona preserves Su Cuaddu de Nixias, indicated as the oldest tomb of Giants of Sardinia, and the Trobas protonuraghe. On the basalt plateau of Sa Corona Arrubia, between Lunamatrona and Collinas, there is the naturalistic museum of the territory "Giovanni Pusceddu."
The castle from which the city was born.

Born from the miracle of Mona Tancia during the plague of 1478, when a grandmother fed her orphan grandson with prayer: the chapel of 1484 became three-nave church in 1523 and the neoclassical façade was built between 1840 and 1856. In the atrium there is the large polychrome terracotta by Giovanni della Robbia (1513), the Assunta that gives the belt to St. Thomas; inside the vaults frescoed at the end of the seventeenth century, the main altar rebuilt after 1596 on a project by Bernardo Buontalenti and the frescoes of the miracle, attributed by Vasari to a pupil of Perugino.
Rectangular church with a single nave and stone façade, accessible from the main street.
The stone bridge.

Castello di origine matildica, poi dei Roberti e dal Quattrocento di un ramo marchanale degli Este: quadrangular plant and an unspoilt corner tower with ghibelline blackbirds and caditoias. Inside the chapel of St. John with a sharp sixth and the noble floor with painted coffered ceilings, frescoes and stuccoes from the fifteenth to the eighteenth centuries; it houses the Pinacoteca Coppelli, the library and the open archive dedicated to Henghel Gualdi. Open Sundays and holidays, 10-12.30 and 15-18.30, with guided tours; closed in August.

Between the localities Lia and Capo d'Armi emerged the remains of a Roman villa, probably of the patrician Publio Valerio who hosted Cicero: excavations near the stream San Vincenzo revealed six environments, three with mosaics. From the territory are also acorns missiles related to the naval war of 42 BC between Octavian and Sixth Pompey, the votive cleft to Demeter found in 1948 (end V-early III century BC) and proto-Christian and Jewish testimonies.
In neo-Gothic Latin cross style.

The city of accordion, with the international museum in the Town Hall and the International Prize of September, and the battle place of 1860 that brought Marche and Umbria to the Kingdom of Sardinia, remembered by the National Monument of the Marches, the Ossario-Sacrario and the Museum of the Risorgimento; around, the Selva, ancient wreck wood.
Frescoes and sundials on the main square.
More than 2 million works and documents from prehistory to today in about 50,000 square meters.
Three thousand years of history of the Orobi in an alpine village dug.

Fortress transformed into a residence by the Sanseverino family, enlarged by Ranuccio II and redesigned between 1697 and 1707 by Ferdinando Galli Bibiena for Francesco Farnese, with facades between four corner towers; since 1749 the Bourbons renovated its interiors with Ennemond Petitot, Boudard and the Rusca stuccoer. On the noble floor the Sala Grande with rococo-neoclassic stuccoes (1755-56) and the new apartment of Don Ferdinando di Borbone, frescoed in 1787-89; after the Unity the furnishings were scattered between Quirinale and museums. Guided tours at 10, 11.30, 15 and 16.30 (Sunday even 17), audio guide Saturday and holidays; closed Mondays not holidays of a few months.

Castle wanted by the bishops of Vercelli and built with pebbles of Sesia: the wounds of the west tower remain, some mullioned windows, parts of the entrance and a wolf tooth frieze on the south tower. In the hamlet also the church of St. Joseph, parish until 1667 with fragments of 16th century frescoes, and the church of the Madonna del Rosario, built in 1628 on the saxo of the Madonna.

Country on the right bank of the Adige, between the slopes of Mount Baldo and the Chiusa dell'Adige, not far from Garda, known for the battle of 14-15 January 1797 won by Napoleon over the Austrians of Alvinczy, which gave the name to the Rue de Rivoli of Paris: the Napoleonic monument on the plain of Canale and the Napoleonic museum, today in transfer; in Incanale the Romanesque church of San Zeno and along the Via Corone the rock engravings.
Skiing and panoramas on the Sibillini just a stone's throw from the village.

Heart of Ariccia, just after the bridge, with fountains bursting; Palazzo Chigi, the Collegiata and the historic Locanda Martorelli overlook it. It was born from the redesign of the city wanted by Pope Alexander VII Chigi between the end of the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, led by Bernini with Carlo Fontana, Mattia de Rossi, Luigi Bernini and Giovan Battista Contini, which also included Porta Romana, Porta Napoletana and the ...Stalloni , the ancient Chigi stables.

Small triangular atoll of about 9,200 sqm a few meters from the western shore of Lake Varese, separated from the mainland by the narrow called "Ticinello." In 1822 it was bought by the Duke Pompeo Litta who called it "Camilla" (Camilla), and since 1865, with the sale of the lake to Andrea Ponti, it took the name of his wife Virginia, and since 1963 it has been of the Municipality of Varese for the legacy of the Marquis Gian Felice Ponti. The excavations started after the discoveries of Abbot Stoppani have revealed inhabited by the Neolithic (4500 BC) at the Bronze Age and at the early Iron Age: it is the oldest pile-dwelling settlement of the alpine arch, UNESCO World Heritage and protected area, with open-air teaching trail, water lilies and many birds. You can only reach it by boat, with transhipment from Biandronno, locality Strencia; on the island a restaurant-bar open all year round.
The house of stone fairies.
The highest peak of the Apennines.
The Lombard church among the olive trees.

The collapse of dolomia boulders detached from the Pelmetto has brought to light a walk of dinosaurs of the upper Triassic, the period in which the first dinosaurs appeared. The cast of the rock with the fingerprints and reconstructions of the animals are exposed to the Museo Vittorino Cazzetta.
In the square, a monument and an epigraph mark the supposed "umbilical" of Italy indicated by Varrone.
Terrace in the center of the village with views of the surrounding villages; near, the oratories of St. John the Baptist and of St. Mary of Graces keep processional chests of the eighteenth century.
An ancient Benedictine abbey with its monumental oak.
A village perched on a volcanic rock.
Painting of the Marche of the fifteenth century in Piazza Alta.
The interior of the tower is open only on special days, events and guided tours organized by the Municipality or by associations; the castle is privately owned

Greek colony founded in 648 B.C. by Greeks of calcidese and Doric origin at the mouth of the Northern Impera, the most western of the north coast of Sicily, destroyed by the Carthaginians in 409 B.C.: remain the high and low city, archaic shrines, the necropolis and the Temple of Victory, erected after the battle of 480 B.C. The Antiquarium of Franco Minissi (opened in 1984) exhibits on four levels the excavations, with the gold foil with Gorgone from the Shrine of Athena and the Golden Phial of Caltavuturo (IV-III century BC); the Museum Pirro Marconi (2016) is dedicated to the Western necropolis and the Temple of Victory.
A hamlet spiraled with pink bricks.

Opened in 1998 in a power plant still in operation, it recalls the Serso plant of 1893, the first three-phase alternating current of the Austro-Hungarian Empire: turbine-alternator group, measuring instruments and documents. Guided tours only by reservation.
Small oratory with two frescoed rounds on the façade: St. Anthony Abbot and St. Louis Gonzaga who received the first communion from St. Charles Borromeo.
For a covered walk in the heart of the village, better on the Sunday of antiques.

Alpine lake at 655 meters with about 10 km of shore, water from green to turquoise that in summer reaches 20-24 °C. Four free beaches: Pieve (pedalò, minigolf, games), Molina-località Besta (beach volleyball, tennis, canoe), Mezzolago (families friendly) and Pur on the south bank ( dog track, wakeboard). A 9-10 km foot and cycle ring follows almost the entire shore (2-3 hours on foot).
The oldest human traces of the Natisone Valleys, by the river.
The Gaeta of the walk and the shops.
The valley inside the park.
The medieval old town, dominated by the castle, collects Palazzo Allegretti on Piazza Vecchia, Palazzo Epifani next to the castle and Palazzo Vitale, known for its rustic appearance.
Ancient fishing village with a narrow marina between colorful houses and a small beach, a traditional destination of the Genoese promenade along the Italian route.
To understand the memory of Bassa Romagna.

The palace wanted by Pandolfo III and built between 1414 and 1421 in late-Gothic style, with portico and double-fores in terracotta, in front of the ancient houses of the Malatesti; after 1463 it was the residence of the Gonfaloniere and the Priors and since 1954 it hosts in summer opera, theatre and concerts.
One of the great Romanesque cycles of Northern Italy.

Tiny chapel with Arab-Norman influences, in the middle of the countryside along the main road that leaves the village, linked to the devotion to St. Vitus: St. Crescent was, according to tradition, the nurse who accompanied the saint.

Built between the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, it has only one nave in five spans, an unusual presbytery open on chapels and a semicircular apse. The patron saints Stefano protomartyre and Saint Isidoro are celebrated on 2-3 August.
The village on the Rio Maggiore.

Two ancient towers built to defend against Saracen incursions, the only survivors of the original five. The ruin of the Rocchetta, among the most famous in Calabria, is located next to the marina of the small fishing village of the Bay of the Rocchetta and is one of the most photographed places on the Costa degli Dei.
The robes of the patron saint.

Città dei Fieschi on the Gulf of Tigullio, at the mouth of Entella, which takes its name from the slate of its quarries: the "caruggio" of Via Roma with medieval porticoes, the basilica of Santo Stefano, the Casa Carbone del FAI, the Tower of the Village and the Blue Flag of Cavi beach.
About 4000 steps excavated in an artificial gallery of almost two kilometers that connects the complex.

Outdoor museum park of about 7 hectares in the valley of the Torbido, created since 1969 by artists Nik Spatari and Hiske Maas in the ancient monastic complex of Santa Barbara and managed by the Foundation Spatari/Maas; it is also workshop where new works are born. Among olive and cypresses monumental sculptures, mosaics and installations; in the church restored the great fresco       Â The dream of Jacob (240 sq m), called the Sistine Chapel Calabria, and in the cloister of the Foresteria a mosaic of 1.400 sq m. According to the official website is open every day from 10 am to 2 pm (last entrance 13), closed December 25, January 1 and Easter; guided tours of about 1 hour by booking for groups.
Rome yesterday in a museum.
The oldest church in the country.

Municipality of the Friulian plain to the east of Udine, crossed by the municipal park of the Tower and Malina, which connects Cerneglons, Remanzacco and Ziracco between streams, stable meadows, mills and villas; in the old workshop Tonutti a museum tells a century of agricultural machines and houses vintage cars and motorcycles.
The small Toledo of the Orobies.
Palladian villa of the first half of the eighteenth century, with four ionic columns facade and pediment with noble coat of arms, in a park of high conifers.
A palace in the historic centre.
The history of the city.

Built between 1454 and 1455 by the Anconetans on the remains of a previous castle, it has quadrangular plan, towers, fifty stations for bombing and the five-storey mast still intact, seat of the Museum of the ancient weapons; along the walls runs the way of patrol with blackbirds tail of swallows. At the top of the mast there is a bell dating back to 1476 and a panorama of the countryside.

In the hamlet of Ciglione, the church of San Bernardo, a Baroque jewel, has the apse frescoed by Pietro Ivaldi called "il Muto" (the Muto), native to nearby Toleto; in the cemetery stands the parish church of San Colombano, of Romanesque origin.
The alpine lakes above the Val Rendena.
The places of childhood that inspired the Gattopard.
The cathedral on the square.

The most imposing complex among the thirty Nuragic sites of the territory: a central tower enclosed by a bastion with four towers, with a sacred source nearby. In the territory also the necropolis at domus de Janas of Sas Fossas and Badde Roma, two dolmens, six menhirs and the tombs of Giants of Istelenneru.
The return of the fishing vessels in the afternoon.
The Sanctuary of San Nicolò Politi.
At the foot of the castle, with remains of the fifth century found in the excavations.

In the 15th-century basement of the Fortress, thousands of objects of work in the fields, domestic life and crafts, collected since the 1970s from a research of the students of the middle school on the work of the grandparents. Open only on the first Sunday of the month, 10-12.30 and 15-18.30.
The fortress marked among the ten things to do in Pistoia.
The 17th century canvas by Vincenzo Manenti.
The church-fortress from which the village was born.
The wooden barns.
Near Piazza Loggia, ancient alleys, churches, historical buildings, taverns and locals; lively in the evening.
The excavations have returned Etruscan materials: the site seems to have been a defensive outpost of Orvieto and a weapons production center, judging by the large amount of iron found.
12th century church with travertine and sandstone façade, with a polyptych attributed to Luca di Tommè where the Madonna holds the castle of Lucignano.
Historical capital of Versilia and marble, called "little Athens" for the artists who live there, including Botero and Mitoraj.

About 10,500 hectares in the Gargano National Park, between Vieste, Vico del Gargano and Monte Sant'Angelo, UNESCO natural heritage since 2017 for beech woods: trails of various difficulties, the Lake of Umbra and 25 picnic areas.
reserve closed since July 2026 after the fall of two trees, pending the investigation of the oldest specimens; the Casino Mollo remains open as a reception point (FAI)
The fortified hamlet enclosed by the walls, with the mast, the castle Scotti and the panoramic walk on the hills.

Marmilla Country divided by the Rio Mannu into two districts united by three bridges: in the parish church of San Michele the retablo dell'Annunziata signed by Lorenzo Cavaro in 1501, in the former Granatic Mountain the multimedia museum Turcus and Morus on the barbaric incursions, in the countryside the church of São Paulo of the disappeared village of Serzela.

The Mother Church of San Nicolò has three portals in local red marble, also used inside; the Annunziata, at the entrance of the village, preserves a fifteenth-century Virgin in Carrara marble with hands and head in plaster, replaced after a Saracen raid, and Byzantine frescoes discovered under the plaster; St. Basil, eighteenth century, keeps remains of a loggia with sharp arches.
Late-medieval frescoes in the village of Bramante.
Paintings of Bolognese school.
Romanesque church about 1.5 km from the centre, with frescoes from the fifteenth century.

Country of the Iblei mountains refounded after the destruction of Gulfi in 1299: palaces of the agricultural nobility along Corso Umberto, the Mother Church, Palazzo Montesano with five museums and the shrines of Gulfi and Graces.

At the base of Capo Carbonara, on the western side, an arc of about one kilometer of white sand and soft between granite cliffs and coves of pebbles, with dunes, pine trees and junipers behind; bottom for tens of meters, suitable for families. Parking, bar, restaurant, rental and diving center; accessible to people with disabilities.
A baroque church of 16th century origin linked to the cloistered monastery of the Redemptorists, brought to the city by Sant'Alfonso Maria de' Liguori in 1766.
The linden avenue and the Venetian façade.
In the hamlet Acquavena houses a statue of the Virgin that legend wants carved in the wood of the tree in which a shepherd saw the image of Our Lady.
Before the movie.

The octagonal square called "Canti" was built in 1807 by the will of Tommaso Gargallo, together with a small church and forty houses, the first nucleus of the village; the small church, named after the Guardian Angel, was elevated to a parish by the bishop of Syracuse in 1814 and the Marquis bought the clock for the bell tower.

Founded in the 11th century and renovated around 1200, it was a stop for the pilgrims of Romea Street, then known as Francigena: it preserves the original apse with stone, terracotta and majolica decorations, capitals with zoomorphic figures of the 11th-XIII century, a baptismal font of the 12th century and a white marble bas-relief with the Baptism of Christ of a 12th-century master champion.

Built in the second half of the sixteenth century on the remains of a Byzantine crypt dedicated to St. John the Baptist, linked to the legend of the apparition of the Virgin to a blind man on July 2, 1568. In the transept 16th century frescoes with the stories of the saints Catherine of Alexandria, Apollonia, Irene, Justina and Orsola; among paintings, Saints Peter and Paul and the Virgin of Purgatory of Ippolito Borghese (1601).
the archaeological area is open from April to October and cannot be visited in case of bad weather
The village is surrounded by terraces rich in trulli and drywalls; in the countryside you will find mirrors, stone towers trunk of cone probably used as sighting posts.

The medieval castle was largely destroyed during the Tuchini revolt (1380-1393), of which two stone doors remain; it was renovated in the first half of the seventeenth century by the Counts Cognengo and expanded at the end of the nineteenth century by Formento with a brick wing and Ghibelline blackbirds. Above the entrance restored frescoes of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries; from the square with terracotta balustrade wide panorama of the Canavese and the valleys Orco and Soana. Walk in 10-15 minutes along the cobbled via Conti di San Martino.
Church of ancient foundation in the medieval heart of the city, among the most important monuments of Asti.
On the slopes of Mount Jupiter, near the village, circular buildings used in the 14th and 19th centuries to preserve the snow in layers covered with leaves and obtain ice for food.

Borgo on the north shore of Trasimeno, the theatre of the battle of 217 BC between Hannibal and Rome: the museum and the historical path of the battle, the columns of serene stone of the Campo del Sole at Punta Navaccia and, ten minutes by boat, the Isola Maggiore with the fishing village and the Museum of Lace.
A fresco in a 14th-century church.
The village rises on top of a hill and preserves the original layout, with the walls still intact, the ancient doors and stone paved roads.

The most important church of the village, outside the historic center: austere exterior with local stone porch and classic portal in white marble, inside with 16th century frescoes, paintings, wooden and marble statues, baptismal font of 1511, golden altar and seventeenth century reliquaries behind doors of golden copper.
The nuraghe-fortress of Orani.

A short ring of 1.38 km (about 30 minutes, 65 m of difference in altitude, rather steep) that starts behind the main church, climbs to the hill of San Pietro, where stands the oldest church of the village with views over the whole valley, and crosses the suspended bridge of 130 meters up to the panoramic tower of the Toresela. From the bridge you can see on one side the colorful roofs of the village and the vineyards of the Piana, on the other the mountain with the mountaineers on the ferrata of Val del Rì. In the summer, the Toresela restaurant opens on Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 6pm, until the last weekend of September.

Fortified settlement built between IV and V century reusing Roman military structures, surrounded by walls with towers; in the Lombard age it was home to a gastaldate. You can see the remains of the Basilica of St. John the Evangelist with cistern and bell tower, the octagonal baptistery with two baptismal sources, the church of St. Paul and a late medieval convent. The excavations, begun in the fifties, are still in progress.
Panorama and fortifications over the Barricades.

Fortress built between the IX and the X century on a Dolomite cliff, originally a castle with three walls and shelter for the inhabitants; in 1527, at the beginning of the Venetian rule, it became the sanctuary of the Madonna della Rocca. Today it houses two overlapping churches, both dedicated to the Annunciation and connected by internal stairs, with seventeenth-century porch, bell tower already sighting, the entrance portal with the guard body and numerous underground passages; at the entrance you arrive with 107 steps. Open from Easter to September on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays 15-18; guided tours all year round by reservation (tel. 339 6856430).

Rebuilt in neoclassical style on the project of the Antonelli, it incorporates parts of the Romanesque cathedral; the central portal is 19 meters high and inside there is the Mystical Bride of Santa Caterina di Gaudenzio Ferrari.
Community life.
The goal of the May procession.

Small church close to the castle of Montone, where the sarcophagus of Bucciarello Jacopo di Bartolomeo was transferred, defined the most beautiful monument of the municipal territory: the nobleman had it carved in stone from 1390 in the chapel of San Jacopo, outside the walls, and carries two coats of arms, his and that attributed to his wife. Sarcophagus and church were restored by the municipality in 1988.
The peasant life of the Marsica object by object.

In the convent of the Friars Minor Conventuals: private chapel with seventeenth-century canvas of the Nativity of Mary, clothes and clothes of the saint, liturgical furnishings, illuminated images on parchment, documents of the sixteenth century and a small royal organ ad ance.

University city at 670 meters on the hill between the valleys of Chienti and Potenza, capital of Varano until 1539: the Doge's Palace with the Botanical Garden, the fort and the convent of Renacavata where the Capuchins were born. The center is still coming out of the 2016 earthquake.
Large three-arched building of the first century A.D. on Via Salaria, largely submerged: the remains emerge in the river next to the modern bridge.
The largest lake in the Marche region.
Minerals, shells and animals from all over the world, now temporarily exhibited in the exhibition space of Palazzo Farnese.

Small natural cave overlooking a lemon terrace, under the Ziro Tower: this is what remains of the Benedictine monastery of Saints Quirico and Julitta, founded in 986 by Archbishop Leo I. The walls preserve Byzantine frescoes of the 12th century with the four Evangelists.
Church with frescoes and Gothic characters, presbytery and bell tower with double windows.

Site of industrial archaeology outdoors, with surface systems abandoned in 1965 that illustrate the first treatments of the pyrite, from the extraction well to the final processing; guided tours also night, workshops, shows and meetings.

Created and edited by Vittorio Scuncio in the castle, it has a section on the Great War (Italian-Austrian front 1915-1918, until the Bulletin of Victory) and one on the Second World War, with relics of Italian, German and allied troops (1943-1945), divided soldiers lodged in the castle, documents on the lines Gustav, Barbara and Winter and oral testimonies of the Pratos. Patronage of the Ministry since 1995.

The village takes its name from the hawks nesting on the top of the Monte del Falcone and stands on a sandstone cliff at about 780 meters; the ancient castle occupies the highest part of the village and from the terrace you can see the Sibillini and the Monti della Laga.
A Romanesque church linked to the figure of Blessed James Papocchi.
From Vesuvius to Matese from the top of the Picentini.
The cathedral at the top of the city.
Ancient Church, one of the few spared from the bombings of the Second World War; it preserves the Madonna of Good Counsel, linked to the wonder of July 10, 1796.
A shrine in the woods, only on foot.
A unique museum in the world, in the heart of the tap district.
Sandy beach and pebbles in front of the main square of the hamlet, which in summer becomes a pedestrian island; the name derives from ... Lagnone , stagnant water, for the ancient marshy mouths.
the MiC card (updated 2020) indicates as the address Via F. P. Michetti and score closed every day; the Superintendence (2023) places the CedTerra at Villa De Lollis

Built in the 13th century by the lords of Marlengo, also known as Lebenberg, on a morainic hill at 505 meters above the village; it was counts Fuchs from 1426 to 1828 and since 1925 it belongs to the family van Rossem, who lives there. You can visit the courtyards, the late-Gothic chapel with frescoes in part fourteenth-century recently rediscovered, the Rococo room of mirrors, the hall of the knights with the large family tree of Fuchs, the armory, the peasant stube with Gothic furniture, the staircase of the coats of arms (from 1216) and the French garden with a mulberry of over 200 years. Open from the end of April to the end of October with visits 10:30-12:30 and 14:00-16:30; Saturday only on request.
The capital of the Ossola, leads to the Sempione: the Renaissance Market Square, the medieval village and the Sacro Monte Calvario UNESCO World Heritage Site.
From Vicenza to Padua by bike.
€3, children 11-15 €1,50, over 60 and groups €2,50

In the former seventeenth-century convent of San Francesco: the Civic Museum has sections of archaeology, ethnography, art and art gallery; the Gipsoteca is dedicated to the Turin sculptor Davide Calandra, with over one hundred works in plaster and terracotta, including the great cast of the frieze for the classroom of Montecitorio. The cradle of Benedictine monasticism in the valley of Aniene: the Sacro Speco dug in the rock of Monte Talio and the monastery of Santa Scolastica, where in 1465 the first printing house of Italy was born. Above the village, the Abbey Rocca; around, the Parco dei Monti Simbruini and Monte Livata.

The museum, inaugurated on 25 April 2004 in the restored administrative shacks, exhibits documents, photographs, letters, personal objects and video testimonies, with a plastic room that reproduces the field in scale and, since 2009, a section on the Shoah.

Set up in six rooms in the basement of a former Augustinian monastery of the eighteenth century, it preserves about 800 nativity scenes from all over the world and about 150 paintings: among others a French copper nativity scene of the nineteenth century, a Palestinian nativity scene in mother of pearl, ebony nativity scenes from Kenya and one engraved on a coral cameo of Torre del Greco. The park museum exhibits the fossils of the site, which affects naturalists from the seventeenth century: fishes (Belonostomus), reptiles (Chometokadmon, Derasmosaurus) and amphibians (Celtedens) of the lagoon about 110 million years ago. It tells the story of Cyrus, a young theropod found in 1980 and recognized in 1993, with some internal organs preserved: his discovery changed the reconstruction of the Italian paleogeography, which was believed to be all submerged in the Mesozoic. The original fossil is kept at the headquarters of the Superintendence in Benevento.

Municipality of Val d'Intelvi formed by the villages of Ponna Superiore, of Mezzo and Inferiore, between pastures and beech woods, with ancient and cobbled streets; home of artists of the Barelli and Tencalla families, preserves the church of Santi Gallo and Desiderio with its eighteenth-century Way of the Cross and the House museum of peasant civilization.

Porto Ceresio is one of the three municipalities (with Besano and Viggiù) of the Italian extension of the UNESCO site of Monte San Giorgio, 240,34 hectares evaluated by IUCN in 2010 for the succession of about 1,000 meters of limestone, dolomies and bituminous schists of the Triassico; on the Italian side, studied since 1863, are known about 35 species of reptiles and almost 100 fish. From the lakefront starts a bike itinerary (about 35 km, 5 hours, 1,100 m of difference in altitude, difficult, recommended e-bike or mountain bike) that goes up to the fossil sites, touches trenches of the Cadorna Line, Sasso Caldo where was found the Besanosaurus, and the fossil museums of Meride (Switzerland) and Besano. The Cadorna Line defended the border during the First World War from a possible Austrian break through neutral Switzerland.

An ancient commercial route that climbed from Bergamo up the Val Brembana towards the Valtellina and the Grisons, making Cornello the most important market in the valley until the construction of the Via Priula at the end of the sixteenth century valley; the mule tracks are still the only access to the village.
