Roman town hall built after the conquest of the 2nd century BC on the town of Ligurian Veleia, 469 meters on a terrace on the valley of Chero, still frequented in the 5th century under the name of Augusta. It was discovered by chance in 1747 with the discovery of the Tabula alimentaria traianea; Duke Philip of Bourbon started its excavations in 1760. You can see the hole paved in sandstone with portico on three sides and the basilica on the fourth, where there were twelve marble statues of the Julian-Claudia family today in Parma, the baths, the residential district and the cistern long believed an amphitheater; the Antiquarium, in the building wanted by Maria Luigia, exhibits pre-Roman finds, the so-called Ligurian Jupiter and the casts of Tabula and Lex rubria. Walk through ancient buildings and mills.

Built in the 12th century, it was the first parish of Montaldeo; it has a unique nave and contains frescoes dating back to the end of the 15th century. Shortly before, for those arriving from Mornese, we meet the chapel of San Gottardo.
Hiking in the highest park in Europe.
The thermal village of the Sienese Valdichiana, where since 2019 the excavations of the Sanctuary have returned dozens of votive statues in Etruscan-Roman bronze.
The paintings and the historical organ of the parish.

Tartaro, 147 km from the Risorgive of Povegliano Veronese to the Adriatic in Porto Levante, is the longest river of Risorgiva of Italy, mentioned by Plinio and Tacito and long border between Venice, Mantova and Ferrara; it crosses the center of the village, where there are two mills and an urban forest of several hectares, partly spontaneous and partly public park.
The Babbaluti crucifix.
Conero's wine in his land.
Medieval village at 594 meters, with stone buildings and sandstone portals, seat of the ancient castle of Uguccione Contrari; the parish church preserves paintings of the seventeenth century.
A Romanesque church overlooking the Gardesana.
To be checked: church; the three museums at extra charge
A movie building on the waterfront.
The theater castle.
The baroque residence of Benedetto Alfieri.
The medieval house.
The relic of the patron.

In the gallery of Gaffione, about 1,244 meters and 4 km from the village, a guided tour of about 3 km in the iron mines closed in 1972: the first 2 km by train, then on foot between rails, wagons and gerle used by the boys; inside there are about 7°C.
Rock and museum on the same visit.
The Gagini marbles in a mountain village.
Licata's most beloved bay.
Verdicchio told and tasted.
The Gothic Cistercian intact.
The ancient history of Villamaina in 933 finds.
The only survivor of the nine mills erected by the Sienese around 1400 in the lagoon, moved by the currents; the Spaniards renovated them adding the sail blades, hence the name.
The fortifications of the abbey of Montecassino on the plain.

Ancient knives and weapons are bought at the Consortium or the dealers known for forging; the tradition comes from the road of the Colvera stream, granted to Nicolò di Maniago in 1453, along which arose the beatings.
In Rovenaud, he recalls Emile Chanoux and Federico Chabod, who were originally from the valley and among the fathers of the regional autonomy of the postwar period.

A noble rural complex that occupies almost the entire west side of the square, with large courtyard, stables and arcades; already shown on the Teresian map of 1725 and reordered in the Baroque age. The palace on the square, with facade to neo-Gothic motifs, was primary school until 1975.
The castle with the art of the twentieth century.
An elymous city suspended on the fortress.

Center on the hill above the mouth of the Trigno, born around the medieval abbey: the Quadrilatero Archaeological Park with Roman mosaic and underground aqueduct, and on the coast the marina with 3 km of Blue Flag beach and a FAI botanical garden.

Built in 1327 on the chapel donated to Saint Francis when he visited the Sacred Speco in 1223: on the high altar the wooden triptych of Antoniazzo Romano (1467) and in a chapel frescoes of the Sodom circle and a Nativity attributed to the Pinturicchio or his school.
The Great Hall is worth a visit.
The Fieschi church.

Around 280 hectares of maquis on the dunes and Mediterranean holm oak in the Statale Reserve of the Roman coast, with deer, hertrics and turtles of Hermann; together with Foce dell'Arrone and the Vasche di Maccarese forms the system of oases managed by the WWF.
In the hamlet of San Martino al Faggio, with the church of San Vincenzo Ferreri, a rare depressed bed-faggeta between the river Rebuscano and sulphurous springs.

Built at the beginning of the XII century in Romanesque-Pisan style on a Lombard building, in local limestone with rosé tones, it is considered the oldest Romanesque architecture of Elba; in 1376 Pope Gregory XI celebrated Mass there. In the sixteenth century it was destroyed by Barbarossa troops except the apse and was then used as a cemetery until Napoleonic laws: today it is partly a ruin, accessible by easy scenic paths.

Karst cavities on the western side of Mount of Helium, about 150 meters above sea level: a large semi-elliptic entrance is divided into corridors, with linear graffiti on the right wall. The excavations of the University of Florence have found silci of the Paleolithic and high-medieval tombs; tradition wants it one of the three places of Garganic worship of the Archangel Michele. You can reach it from the road of the village of Torre Mileto and a short path; for the visit you need lamps.
The Renaissance with a central plan.
Buildings surrounded by walls, once stable of the Challant, now home to the mountain community and library.
From the hot air balloon to the convert plane, just a few steps from Malpensa.
The only Donatello of Umbria.
The eighteenth-century residence of the Carthusians, the cultural heart of the city.

Since 1998 it occupies the north-east tower of the castle and part of the round path; it collects sculptures, paintings and graphic works that the Galliate artist Angelo Bozzola has donated to his community.
A panoramic stop through white roads.

Medieval village on the hills of Trasimeno, closed by fourteenth-century walls with six towers and three gates and designed on three parallel roads: Palazzo Baldeschi with the museum Banca della Memoria del Trasimeno, the Museo Don Aldo Rossi in the church of San Giuseppe and, just outside, the sanctuary of the Madonna della Stella.

Among the best preserved of the Alto Monferrato, it is still inhabited by the Marquis Pinelli Gentile, who received it in 1745 with the marriage between Teresa Gentile and Costantino Pinelli. The square tower, part of the oldest, is from the 10th century and from the top offers a 360-degree view of the hills; the complex brings together towers, houses, a church and a big garden, with frescoed halls, furnishings and arms collections. Wineries have been producing and preserving local wines for 500 years; it is part of the Castelli Aperti circuit (tel. 0143 89195).
The richest museum in the province.
The thermal waters that give the name to the country.
The most famous sea on the Ionian coast of Catanzaro.

Picturesque remains of a castle built around the year 1000, probably on Roman foundations, on the hill above the village that was the ancient Canipa, abandoned in the seventeenth century and invaded by the wood; from the top the view ranges over the village and the vineyards. The first Sunday of July is held the Festa del Castello.
A clearing in the birch with the Monviso in front.
The church at the end of the Grand Canal, where the canal once arrived.
Basilica minor and main church of the city, in lava stone and in Norman-Svevo style; it houses the Salvation of Randazzo, sixteenth-century table that shows the city as it was at the time.
The center of the star.

Città del Mantovano between Po and Oglio, inhabited since the fourth millennium BC and linked to Gonzaga since 1415; in the historical center the Arch of Porta Nuova, the Town Hall of Pietro Antonio Maggi and the parish church of Santa Maria Assunta and San Cristoforo with the polyptych of Bartolomeo Vivarini, and in the cultural hub MuVi the Civic Museum Antonio Parazzi.

Visconti Castle enlarged in 1354 at the behest of Giovanni Visconti, passed with Venice in a feud to Bartolomeo Colleoni, then to the Longhi and from 1539 to Cardinal Gian Gerolamo Albani; in 1842 Wenceslas Albani restored it, created the hanging garden and rebuilt the Ghibelline Merlature, and since 1953 it is part of the municipality. It preserves moat, mastic with secret passages, fifteenth-century staircase, courtyard with Renaissance porticoes, frescoed rooms (Late 16th century grotesques, Four Seasons), room of the Maps and walkway; guided tours by reservation.
Cobbled road with artisan workshops, between the Museo Leone and the Teatro Civico.
A unique neoclassical bell tower-monument.
closed to the public for its position, which can only be visited by qualified researchers; in 2023, the Municipality placed inspections to assess the reopening of the project.
Blue Bay Flag for every taste, from sand to pebbles.
A glacial lake inside a wildlife oasis.
Sacred art in a 17th century church.
The millennial history of the valley in one palace, free of charge.

Ancient Roman route that from the confluence between the Dolo and Dragon climbed to the Passo delle Radici; in the Middle Ages it connected Emilia and Tuscany and was wide enough for the wagons. They are still traversed in the municipalities of Montefiorino and Frassinoro.
The castle overlooking the Volturno valley.
The Museum of Peoples.

Borgo del Roero is the seat of the Ecomuseo delle Rocche, the museum spread over the ridge of the Fortress over 30 km long: on top of the village the castle of Morra Lavriano, the civic tower and the parish church of Sant'Antonio Abate, and on the Valdiana the Sacro Monte dei Piloni, the smallest in Piedmont.
The nature of Sebino in a small museum.
The public garden of the village, with a nineteenth-century circular temple, the "Café House" and next to the statue of Flora.

A fortified area of the Lombard period that preserves the original topography, the eastern and western doors and one of the few churches of the eighth century; there stands the Abbey of St. Nicholas of the thirteenth century, with a altarpiece of Giovan Bernardo Lama and the statue of the saint.
The remains of the Roman city on Via Emilia and the museum in the Palazzo della Cultura.
Impressive three-storey building with roof terrace, in the center of the village.
Church of Gothic plant with a painting cycle of the fifteenth century; it dominates the village from above and is connected to the center of the village by a steep staircase.
The houses purchased by Michelangelo, with two of his youthful reliefs, the Madonna della Scala and the Battle of the Centauri.

The village, documented since 905 and plundered by the Venetians in 1447, preserves in the historic center stretches of walls, palaces and the parish church; the lakefront with pebble beaches and the port of the boats complete the walk. On the evening of January 5, the Vegia Pesa recalls in costume an edict of 1605.
A corner of the sea.

The museum preserves the abbey chair of the 12th century with inlays of Arabic taste, the Madonna of St. William of the late 12th century, a wooden crucifix of the 13th century and oriental icons; next to the permanent exhibition of Neapolitan and world nativity scenes from the 17th to the present day.
Museum of sacred art of the parish, exhibits the sixteenth-century altarpiece of the "Dinner in Emmaus" by Jacopo Bassano and paintings by Andrea da Murano.
A Madonna from Piero's school.
The street dedicated to the poet, flanked by medieval churches and palaces and craft shops of confetti, tradition documented from the fourteenth century.
Walking or cycling: in some stretches you can walk almost on the water that resurfaces after the underground path.
Recipe and buildings on the hill above the Dora.

Established by Napoleon in 1805 as a model estate and hunting reserve, designed by Luigi Canonica: one of the largest enclosed parks in Europe, with Villa Mirabello and Mirabellino, historic farmsteads, dry mills and the Chain Bridge.
The port of Rome imperial.
Nora's gold foil.
The Gothic collegiate of 1436 wanted by Orlando Pallavicino and the Franciscan complex of 1470 with the famous Terracotta Compiantic.

Centre of the Upper Tiber Valley marked by the lordship of the Vitelli: the Pinacoteca with Raffaello and Signorelli, the cylindrical bell tower of the Duomo and the two locations of the Burri Collection.
The patron Saint George.
The old shops.

Borgo on a spur in the National Park of the Apennines Lucano Val d'Agri Lagonegrese, dominated by the feudal castle on the sandstone cliff overlooking the Camastra Valley; it preserves in the Mother Church the body of Blessed Egidio, the frescoed cloister of Santa Maria della Neve and, in the territory, the Abetina Reserve.
The village-castle on the Tiber, among the most beautiful villages in Italy.

Centre of the Bari Murge collected around the square of the Cathedral, one of the four palate basilicas of Puglia, and Palazzo De Mari, ancient fortified residence today seat of the Municipality; outside the center the Cave of Curtomartino opens.
The view of the Maremma.
Museum of contemporary art in the open air spread in the town, with works by Maria Lai, Tellas and Giovanni Campus.
One of the three Romanesque churches of the territory, along the provincial road to Berzano.
The village of the nuragic palace of Santu Antine and the Nuraghi Valley, thirty towers and ten tombs of the Giants in 37 square kilometers.
Mountain life in a family museum.
One of the most beautiful rosettes in the region.
Hills of vineyards, including the Famous grape, and ancient parishes along the Savio.
Picnic in the shade of pine trees.
Built in 1502 by the brothers Buzzatti and today a national monument, it houses a wooden altar and a triptych attributed to Augustine by Lodi.
The bell tower is the symbol of the city.
The country residence of Bishop Bonafede.
An eighteenth-century church on the site of a Gothic church, with a baptismal font of the fifteenth century.
private property, accessible only the ground floor according to the Municipality

Fragments of Roman tombstones already indicate an important building in Roman times; before the Mille, with the Marquises of Romagnano, it became a castle with walls, moats and a tower used as a bell tower. In 1173 Manfredo II of Romagnano obtained the Prevostura of Lombriasco with at least twelve Augustinian monks; assaulted several times in the fourteenth century, in 1382 the fief passed to Antonio Ponte and in the eighteenth century the castle was transformed into a noble palace. Dead without heirs in 1850 the last lord, Nicolao Cesare Ponte, in 1878 bought him the Benedictines of Mondovì and in 1894 Don Rua, the first successor of Don Bosco, established a Salesian community there.
Allifae before and after Rome.
A hill sanctuary with the black Madonna.
The remains of the amphitheatre of the Roman city, strategic along the Cassia street and known for its ceramics; the Archaeological Museum is built above its structures.
Medieval ruins and a tiny Romanesque church in a granite landscape.
€3 guided tour, €2 reduced
Fossil and geology, good with the boys.
The plateau of the Ernici Mountains.

It rises on the site of the Latin village "Castrum Sancti Salvatoris," abandoned after the earthquake of 1465 and repopulated by refugees from southern Albania, who renamed it Civita. An itinerary touches the fifty of historical comignoli (probably built between the end of the seventeenth and early twentieth centuries, each designed by the foreman and considered capable of keeping away evil spirits) and the  "speaking houses" of Kodra, with facades reminiscent of a human face, dedicated to the Albanian painter Ibrahim Kodra. The district of Sant'Antonio, the oldest, of medieval origin, has hanging ovens, loggias and the chapel of Sant'Antonio; in the Gjitonia, squares where the alleys cross, the inhabitants are found.

Ancient house in the historic center on three floors, restored preserving table floors and ceilings of beams and reeds, with internal courtyard, porch and oven for bread: kitchen with fireplace, rooms with wrought iron beds, cellar with the corner of the bakery and pantry, peasant tools, costumes and embroidery of the local tradition. Guided tours by appointment with the City's cultural office; admission fee; on the day of the visit you can attend the preparation of the culurgiones and taste them.

Romanesque-Norman, consecrated in 1045 and again in 1222, partly built on the rock, with a Greek crypt perhaps of the eighth century and the chapel of Our Lady of Itria, obtained in 1261 from a rock church.
City park mentioned among the gardens that characterize Udine.

Built in 1809 on the Tschalawai promontory by the captain of the genius Friedrich Hensel, who died defending him from the French in May 1809; modernized in 1884 for 18 cannons, he was reactivated in the Great War and reduced in rubble by about 4,500 shots of the Italian artillery. There are ruins between the vegetation, a tunnel with slits, the monument of the Lion of Hensel and the view of the Val Canale.
The clay landscape on which the village stands, perched on a ridge.
The streets of the painter Valorsa.

The oldest castle in Naples after Castel dell'Ovo, of Norman origin, at the entrance of Via dei Tribunali; for over five hundred years the seat of the Court, which can be visited on organized occasions.
Church of 1449 in Poggio Baldino with convent of Friars Minor: icons attributed to Sano di Pietro, the Annunciation of Welcome by John (1470) and works by Guidoccio Cozzarelli.

Spa resort at the foot of the Euganean Hills, known in Europe for its mud therapy and frequented already in Roman times, as shown by the excavations of the Augustan thermal complex; in the city the International Museum of Art Glass, the Duomo on the Montagnone Hill, the Oratory of the Madonna and Villa Draghi with its park of 30 hectares.
The frescoes of the fifteenth century.
Monte Tinisa, 2120 metres, is the highest peak in the municipality; from Passo Pura you reach the dense high altitude Forest of Ampezzo, crossed by hiking trails.

The Lido is the long strip of beaches and coves that connects the port to Ischia Ponte, starting from the beach of San Pietro, where the boats used to dry up; the Beach of the Fishermen, of fine sand, arrives a few hundred meters from the jetty of the Castle, with facilities and recreational activities.
Built in the 13th century, probably on a pre-existing building, it is considered the oldest cult building in the village; the façade follows the canons of the Lombard Gothic.

Opened in 1997 in the former 14th-century convent of San Francesco outside the walls, on three floors: archaeological finds from the Bronze Age to the 6th century AD, the tower of the Bebe and the war of Chioggia, a medieval cistern; a room dedicated to Cristoforo Sabbadino and to the brothers Aldo and Dino Ballarin of the Great Turin; on the top floor shipbuilding and local marine with models of the bragozzo, the civic pictorial collection and the marinery of the high sea.

Two basins for about 2,200 hectares, one of the largest in Europe and Ramsar site with the nearby wetlands: nidify flamingos and real germans, fish the moss from which the bottarga is born, the Cabras gold, with the traditional junk boats "is fassonis"; birdwatching and fishing at the fish pond of Mar'e Pontis.

Protected natural area of more than 1,600 hectares, already a wood reserve, open all year round, with about 50 km of hiking trails, horse and mountain bike among hardwood woods, pine trees and Mediterranean maquis; wild boars, roe deer, deer, mouflons, horseback riding and badgers live there, and migratory birds such as beak and buzzard.

The city between the two seas, in a panoramic position on a buttress of the Sila Piccola from which you can see Tirreno and Ionio, has origins between the end of the IV and the beginning of the III century BC; the Museum Polo Tiriolo Antica brings together archaeological museum and section of the costume, while in the historical center survives the craftsmanship of the vancali, the shawls of the "Pacchiana" .
Baroque-style shrine built near a spring whose waters, according to legend, heal skin diseases.
A shovel of Gherardo delle Notti.

A town built on the remains of the ancient Oplontis, suburb of Pompeii buried by the eruption of 79 A.D. and part of the UNESCO site with the Villa of Poppea; born around the chapel of the Annunziata of the fourteenth century, it was famous for the Real Fabbrica d'Armi borbonica, the port and the pasta factories, and today offers a seafront overlooking Vesuvius and the thermal baths.
Stairways and slopes along the route

Mesozoic limestone massif, 1,315 metres high, on whose cliffs you can see the royal eagle and the griffon; large areas with little trees, pastures and walls that attract climbers and hikers, with paths between Alcara li Fusi, Longi and San Marco d'Alunzio. The Rocche guard the hermitage of San Nicolò Politi and are crossed by the path dedicated to him, in the Nebrodi Regional Park.

Set up in the eighteenth century former church of San Biagio, already shrine of the fallen of all wars, exhibits weapons, uniforms and relics from the seventeenth century and from the Risorgimento to the Second World War.

Protected area since 1996 that includes Costacciaro, Scheggia, Fossato di Vico and Sigillo, with gorges, valleys and pure waters; the Cave of Monte Cucco is among the largest in Italy and the massif offers excursions for everyone, even simple for children, as well as abbeys and Romanesque and Gothic hermitages.
The protected area of the Apuan chain, about 60 km long between Versilia, Lunigiana and Garfagnana, where the village of Colonnata is located.
Small village at the foot of a picturesque waterfall, destination for families.
City hall, insides with guide on occasions like Open Villas in Brianza (booking on villeaperte.info)
The history of the village, from Roman statues to ceramics and Vespa.

Small oratory on the shore of the Lemene near the Molini, linked to the devotion of fishermen from the first half of the seventeenth century; plundered in 1917 and restored in 1920 by Giuseppe Bittolo Bon. Every August 15, after Mass, the evening arrives the procession of boats from Caorle and Concordia.
The elliptical plant.
Walk through the palaces of the village of De Capua.
The villa that gave its name to the locality Guitar.
The sea of Versilia, accessible to all.
The cloisters of the complex of Santa Corona, which in summer host the "Cinema under the stars" and installations in the garden.
The colorful fishermen's houses.
Castle of the fifteenth century.

Arbëreshë village of Alto Belice, founded by Albanians who arrived in Sicily in the 15th century, with the Mother Church of the Greek-Byzantine Rite; in the territory the Rocca d'Entella, an ancient town with the cave in the casts protected as a reserve, the Antiquarium of its finds and the abbey of Santa Maria del Bosco.
Romanesque and frescoes next to the Neolithic park.

Itinerary No. 13 of 4 km, about 3 hours and 800 m of difference in altitude, classified difficult: starts from Pozzolo, historical hamlet of Gavirate, with an ancient wash-house, rises between woods and rural houses towards Cà dei Monti, crosses the Nature Reserve of the Campo dei Fiori and the "Road Red" and ends at the Fort of Orino, garrison of the Cadorna Line, with 360 degrees view over Prealpi, the Piedmont Alps, plain and lakes. We recommend the GPS.
Summer and winter mountain near Lake Iseo, on the streets of the Pirate.
The history of Bolzano in 200 works.

15th century national monument, built under Sixtus IV as a former vote against the plague, with five fornics narthex. To the altars a votive picture for the plague of 1657, a fresco in memory of the battle of Lepanto (1592), a sixteenth-century Crucifix and a marble group of thirteen figures of Saints Rocco and Sebastiano (16th century).
The ancient church around which the village grew.
Aragonese-style castle remained unfinished after the killing of Count Giancarlo Tramontano; it hosts cultural and musical events.

The main house is probably sixteenth-century of the Horses, bought in 1680 by the Marquises Giulio and Bonaventura Carlotti and transformed between 1670 and 1711; the loggia has date 1704 and the octagonal chapel of San Biagio, of 1695, has an altarpiece of 1731. The original frescoes are no longer there and the rustic court is still in agricultural use.
Parks Lazio indicates opening all year 9-12 and 15-17 with free entrance (tel. 0774 899084), but MiC card (December 2020) gives closed every day

Fortress built between the end of the XII and the beginning of the XIII century on the top of Mount Rich, 310 meters, as military garrison of the city; you reach from Porta Colmarion with 276 steps and from the stands the look goes from the Dolomites to the Venetian plain. It often hosts cultural events and costume reenactments.
The civic square of the Roman Pompeii.
Equipped beach with views of the Spanish fort.

At the entrance of the village, church completed in 1602 in late Baroque style, a single nave with relief ceiling, large wooden altar, friezes and stucco; reopened to worship in December 2000 after a long restoration. Next to the fifteenth century fountain, with the arched niche surmounted by the coat of arms of the Di Sangro.
1.5 km from the village, with frescoes from the sixteenth century.
One of the top of Lombard art between Gothic and Renaissance.

A coastal town at the gates of Ancona, with a long sandy beach and four castles: Falconara Alta, seat of the town hall with views from the Apennines to the Adriatic, the Rocca Priora, Castelferretti and Barcaglione; in the monastery of Sant'Antonio the contemporary Franciscan art gallery "In the name of Francesco" .
The university collection of plaster casts of ancient sculptures.
The walk where the lake becomes river.

Church with neo-Gothic portico and baroque crowning, decorated inside with frescoes by Filippo Bellini and several paintings by Ercole Ramazzani; a cloister connects it to the Palazzo dei Conventuali, a former 18th century Franciscan monastery that houses the Pinacoteca comunale (Museo civico), the Library and the Historical Archives.
In the center of the village, built in 1792 on the chapel of the old hospital.
The cycle of Jacopo Siculo.

Pinacoteca from the fourteenth to the twentieth century and exhibitions in the Loggetta Lombardesca, the 16th century cloister of Santa Maria in Porto, with a section dedicated to contemporary mosaic.

Visitor centre of the Park on the first floor of the cloister of San Francesco, rebuilt in the early seventeenth century with frescoed lunettes in 1635: presents the Sibillini Mountains with paths for images and texts on environments, flora, fauna, legends, art, history and popular culture, with attention to how man shaped the landscape. Reduced €3 for children 7-16 years and groups, free of charge up to 6 years.
The history of the country between documents, devotion and trunks of migrants.
It collects prehistoric finds and collections of ancient coins.
The life of the High Irpinia peasanta, craft by trade.
View of the Valtournenche with the Grandes Murailles and the Matterhorn and the central valley.
The Bardi's palace with its historical organ.

Small mountain village in the Matese Regional Park, with a historic centre of alleys and stairs, the church of San Giovanni Battista with the Santa Spina and, about 5 km, the Forre di Lavello dug by the Titerno.
A work by Aldo Rossi that reinterprets the Venetian villa.

In the premises of the former cemetery church of Santa Caterina, dating back to the 16th century: tools of fields, vineyards, stables and cellars from the second half of the 19th century to the 1960s, household objects (lights, skis and snowshoes made by hand, Gerle), ancient books of the Confraternita di Santa Caterina, lanterns and processional clothes, stones and gravestones from the excavations of the destroyed castle. Visit by reservation at the municipal offices.

Small Romanesque building with a rectangular plan along the ascent to the castle, almost hidden by two tall pine trees; for some scholars it dates back to the 10th century and is already mentioned at the end of the 13th century in the Liber Notitiae Sanctorum Mediolani di Goffredo da Bussero. The dedication to St. James Major suggests a pilgrimage to Santiago. The restorations of the fifties and sixties of the twentieth century brought to light frescoes from different eras: in the apse paintings byzantine with apostles, a fragment of the martyrdom of St. James, a St. John the Baptist and a Madonna with Child who blesses a devotee, probably a Visconti, of 15th century painters.
Free
It keeps a wooden statue of the Virgin covered with jewels donated as a former vote, carried in procession on the launch on 24 August.

Naturalistic oasis a few kilometers from the village, reachable also on foot from the center, with large beech trees, oaks, oaks, maples, hornbeams and Neapolitan alders; it is crossed by the river Peschiera, habitat of the otter. It has parking, fountain and the Adventure Park of Pollino, inclusive and suitable for all ages.
Uncontaminated beach near the port, with formations of white rock called  "timpe" along the sand.

Renaissance church built in the sixteenth century in honour of Our Lady of the Rosary, at the foot of the ravine among the traditional houses, with the churchyard overlooking the ravine. Entirely in local tuff, it has two entrances (the main one with five steps flanked by columns with capitals with angel heads), bell tower with pyramid cusp and lantern, interior with three naves with barrel vault in the central and a fresco of San Martino di Saverio Ierace. Tel. 334 3050780.
Already in the 12th century, it houses the marble statues of the Madonna del Soccorso and Santa Caterina d'Alessandria, of the school of Gagini, of the 18th century.
Baroque plasters and silver reliquary.

Founded in 1872 at the will of the widow in the neoclassical palace that tenor Rubini (1794-1854), the first Elvino of Bellini's Sonnambula, had built, with six ionic columns, frescoes, stuccos and Venetian mosaic floors. In the five rooms on the ground floor the billiard room with private memories and the Pirate room with the memories of the career; among the works the Last Supper by Giovan Battista Moroni, works of the Caniana and Trento Longaretti. Open on Sunday 10-12.
Defined by italia.it an open air museum. Open Monday to Saturday 8-18, Sunday and holidays 7-13.
An entire medieval village suspended over time.
Small church at over 1,800 meters above sea level, signposted for religious architecture.
The ancient popular district along Via Cavour and Via dei Serpenti, a short walk from the Colosseum.
Mountain elm of about 600 years, described as the oldest in Italy, with next to the trunk a Marian chapel and near a spring.
private tower, guided tours only on scheduled dates (September 2026)
One of the largest squares in Italy, with the Romanesque abbey of San Mercuriale and its bell tower over 70 meters high.

On the plateau of Monte Lauro (986 m) the lava stone, cave, dome or square snowshoe remains, where from the seventeenth century to the end of the Second World War it collected and conserved snow, used first in medicine and then for sorbets. Rural routes with views of Mount Etna and the Calabrian coast.
the MiC card (updated to June 2020) indicates "closed" every day but describes seasonal summer openings; times and prices to be reviewed
Typical small village theatre, of the kind spread in the area a century ago; Italia.it defines it as a rarity to protect and enhance.
At the Gate of the Valley a stretch of 'cyclopic walls of the VII-VI century B.C., the ancient entrance to the pre-Roman acropolis.
Underground galleries that follow an aquifer: the collected water is decanted, purified and conveyed into an eighteenth-century fountain to thirteen mouths.
Stone carved between East and West.

In the hamlet of Vendrogno, in Val Muggiasca, the church of Sant'Antonio Abate was built in 1362 and contains frescoes from the sixteenth century; that of San Lorenzo has a Baroque façade and Romanesque bell tower.
Notary town hall.
temporarily closed for inventory and restoration of the collections according to Touring; guided tours and workshops for schools and groups by reservation
In Palazzo Cappellani, exhibits artifacts from Akrai, Kasmene and Leontinoi.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 5 of the 10 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.

Valico at 986 meters above Rango, a large valley of lawn surrounded by woods overlooking the Carè Alto and Cima Sèra; picnic area and starting point for excursions. Along the old road from the Val Marcia to the pass are the "filagne" , walls of vertical slabs of granite.

Borgo della Valle Bormida refounded in 1253 as a villa fortified by the bishop of Acqui Enrico Del Carretto and home of the sculptor Giulio Monteverde and the statesman Giuseppe Saracco: to see the Gipsoteca Monteverde, the Sanctuary of the Pieve, the parish church of San Giovanni Battista with the medieval tower and the red Big Bench of Roncogennaro.
Bombs, weapons and a view from the mastium.

Isolated among the olive trees outside the center, with the Santa Croce mountain behind: facade and apses are built with square blocks of the nearby Roman theatre; inside frescoes and marbles. The current aspect is due to the restorations of the 1960s, which eliminated the baroque parts.
Borgo on the eastern slopes of Etna, founded at the beginning of the 18th century as Porta in the territory of Acireale, where volcanic herb liqueurs are distilled.

The Augustinian complex of the Oltrarno with the basilica designed by Brunelleschi and begun in 1444, loved by Leonardo and Michelangelo and defined by Bernini the most beautiful church in the world; in the sacristy the young Crucifix of Michelangelo.

Started in 1589 by the prior Constantine Massino around the Marian sanctuary, at 455 meters: 23 chapels and 5 romans dedicated to the mysteries of the life of Mary, in two phases (Five-Sixth and Nineteenth century), with polychrome terracotta statues, in a forest of oaks and ashes. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Palladio's last work, commissioned in 1580 by the Olympic Academy and completed after his death: the oldest theater covered in masonry in the world, inspired by the Roman theatres of Vitruvio, with the fixed scene of Scamozzi and 95 statues; hosts the Cycle of Classic Shows.

The symbol of the city: Palladio redesigned the Gothic Palazzo della Ragione enveloping it in the marble lodges that for over four centuries watch over Piazza dei Signori; venue of exhibitions, with panoramic terrace.
The Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, between Gothic, Baroque and Neo-Gothic, with the Museum of the Treasury of San Gennaro; three times a year there is the rite of the renown.
Built in 1218-1219 for the courts: the 82 for 27 meters salon with ship hull cover, fifteenth-century frescoes, the stone of the Vituprio and the large wooden horse.

The largest medieval castle of Naples, of the thirteenth century, on the Vomero, with the Museum of the twentieth century in Naples (over 170 works) and the view on the sea, Vesuvius, islands and Campi Flegrei.
On the tip of the promontory, in Gothic Genoese style; it is among the churches mentioned in the UNESCO site description.

Fortress, palace remained unfinished on the project of Juvarra, barracks and then museum: since 1984 the first museum of contemporary art of Italy with masterpieces of the Poor Art, the Long Channel and since 2019 the Cerruti Collection (Picasso, De Chirico, Kandinsky, Bacon). From the panoramic sport the view of Turin. UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Capitanio Palace in front of the Basilica in Piazza dei Signori, stop around the historic centre of Palladio and scenery of shows.

UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997: nuraghe and village inhabited by the ancient Bronze Age to the end of the Iron; the 12-metre-diameter mast on three floors with terrace, a four-tower bastion and a well of over 20 meters in the courtyard.
Residenza Sabauda on the hill, stage of the panoramic route from Monte dei Cappuccini towards Superga.
One of the stages of the Arab-Norman itinerary of Palermo.

Royal residence born in 1141 and rebuilt several times, today with about 300 furnished rooms, including the large ballroom with stuccoes and frescoes of the  "Fasti di re Arduino" by Giovanni Paolo Recchi. UNESCO World Heritage Site.
